Phrolova: Among thousands of paths, surely one will lead me back to them.
Phrolova: And even if I'm wrong... I fear not starting over. I've done it time and time again.
Rover: What meaning is there in chasing something that's neither realistic nor attainable?
Phrolova: I know they're there.
[Dialogue Option]  I saw them in the Beyond.
Rover: Those fading Reverberations did not, and cannot, return to life. No matter how long you hold onto their frequencies, the result will be the same.
Rover: The villagers are dead. What you've created are Tacet Discords. If you continue turning the entire town into that... you're not creating a paradise. You're creating a hell.
Phrolova: "The villagers are dead..."
Phrolova: So, you saw them in their human form.
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Phrolova: Then how can you claim my goal is unattainable?!
[Dialogue Option]  Your goal is the one the Fractsidus gave you.
Rover: It's what they forced on you. And the Triss you saw? Fleeting, unstable, an illusion. And yet, you still believe everything they say can become real?
Phrolova: The Fractsidus showed me a way forward.
Phrolova: Even if they have their own motives, even if we're only using each other... I care not.
Phrolova: If they can help me take this step, then another step may follow. And another. No matter how steep the price, I'll pay it, step by step, until I reach the end I seek.
Phrolova: Love? Sincerity? Compassion? Trust?
Phrolova: What you and your cronies hold dear is but a jest to the Fractsidus. No bond lasts forever. Without true loyalties, there can be no betrayal, no deceit.
Phrolova: I no longer buy into such illusions.
Phrolova: After all, even if you believe with all your heart, even if you wait patiently at a crossroads...
Phrolova: The one you're waiting for may have long since forgotten you. Forgotten the promise they swore to keep.
Phrolova: I waited. For a long time.
Phrolova: I won't wait anymore.
Phrolova: What was once an unforgettable encounter between us can now be the thread that weaves a paradise for "them."
Rover: You've gone too far.
Phrolova: Heh, you're one to talk. How amusing.
Phrolova: You, with your long life and its endless possibilities, still choosing to start over, even at the cost of all your memories?
Phrolova: The irreplaceable bonds, the emotions that make us human, are the brightest lights and most precious treasures in our fragile existence.
Phrolova: What madness, what cruelty, what impossible goal could drive you to cast them all aside?
Phrolova: You've gone further than I ever could.
Phrolova: Perhaps you believe more than I do that only in endless time can true, eternal perfection arise.That only then will a brave new world arrive.
Phrolova: We walk different paths, yet in the end, we are both driven by the same madness. Why argue over who's fallen further?
Phrolova: The only difference is that... you've forgotten it all.
Rover: You never understood the true value of human life.
Phrolova: Nor have you stepped beyond the bondary that death has placed upon the human soul.
[Dialogue Option]  Our cooperation ends here.
Phrolova: Hehe...
Phrolova: ...
Phrolova: So, this is our finale.

content:
Abby: Oh... Alright. Are we heading back now?
[Dialogue Option]  We still have to tie up loose ends here.



"Once I dreamt that we were dear to each other."
"I woke to find that we were strangers."

content:
[Objective: (Optional - Approach the entrance to the Lost Beyond)]
Abby: Achoo! Hmm... The smell here is kinda weird...
[Dialogue Option]  This must be the entrance to the Lost Beyond.
Abby: Wait, it feels alive.
[Dialogue Option]  Alive?
Abby: I know that sounds odd... but I mean, whatever's on the other side is pulsing along to the beats of someone's life!
Abby: It's kinda faint, btu it's definitely part of a person's frequency!
[Dialogue Option]  Phrolova...
Abby: Hey, what was that thing you were holding? It smelled exactly the same as this place.
Rover: You mean her baton?
Rover: It seems like the Beyond has now completely merged with her.
Rover: If you can feel the pulse of life in the Beyond, it means she's still alive...
Abby: Okay, I just gave the place a good sniffin'! Only some leftover energy. Nothing smells wrong.
[Dialogue Option]  If we go in there, will she know?
Abby: Hmm... maybe? It's kinda like we're walking right into someone's thoughts!
[Dialogue Option]  Since it's harmless, we'll leave it be for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Let's go in and take a look.

title: Dreamcatchers in the Secret Gardens
subsection: (Inside the Shards of the Beyond, find and talk to Phrolova)
content:
[Objective: (Inside the Shards of the Beyond, find and talk to Phrolova)]
Phrolova: You... How did you get in...
Phrolova: Entering another's realm without permission like this... Did you forget your manners along with your memories?
[Dialogue Option]  The energy portal outside wasn't your invitation?
Phrolova: Obviously not.
Phrolova: You will gain nothing in this bygone realm. Must you cast your gaze here?
[Dialogue Option]  Bygone, but cozy.
Phrolova: Anyone who comes here should experience a simple sense of joy... It seems we share similar feelings about this place.
Phrolova: Is that why you've returned? How unexpected.
[Dialogue Option]  (I'd like to immerse myself in melodies of the past)
Rover: I'd also like to know whether listening to past melodies allows me to hear realms that I once went through.
Phrolova: You wish to listen to past stories? Ah... It seems I have an audience for the songs I've collected throughout history.
Phrolova: Go ahead. Every song kept in this room is at your disposal. There's a seat by the window.
[Dialogue Option]  How much of what you said is true?
Phrolova: The people here are of no use to you. Don't try anything. I will protect this place.
[Dialogue Option]  To the end? With your life?
Phrolova: Heh, an empty and graceless threat. After all, you are not one to harm commoners.
[Dialogue Option]  They're not commoners.
Phrolova: I alone am enough to bear all your hostility. Stay away from this sacred land. Whatever you do, I will accompany you to the end.
[Dialogue Option]  A foe's weakness is worth preserving.
Phrolova: What exactly are you here for?
[Dialogue Option]  (To watch what my foe is doing)
Rover: I will return here often to watch them and you. Even if you're not personally here, that should be sufficient.
Phrolova: Holding us under your vigilant eyes... Looks like I'll never be able to fully rest here. How cruel.
;(Obtain the Trophy, Between Here and Beyond)
[Dialogue Option]  You're right. I'll leave.
Phrolova: ......
Phrolova: See yourself out.

title: Dreamcatchers in the Secret Gardens
content:
Dark Tide - A Waveworn Phenomenon unique to Rinascita, the Dark Tide is a manifestation of the Threnodian Leviathan's power of Unity. Dark clouds amass overhead and crash down like a waterfall, surging in all directions. Wherever the Dark Tide spreads, it spawns Tacet Discords and scars the land with Tidal Blight. At its epicenter, a new Tacet Field forms.
Echo Brooder - A device for incubating Common Echoes. Twisted, shattered Echo frequencies are reconstructed into new Common Echoes within its chamber.
Fabricatorium of the Deep - A secluded underwater experiment facility built by the Fractsidus and the Order, where they both pursue hidden ambitions under the guide of Common Echo reprocessing and production.
Harbinger - Humans selected by the Threnodian Leviathan to spread its doctrine, and sow sorrow and despair among the masses. Influence appears to be a key factor in their selection. Marked by the Dark Tide's corruption, they wield fragments of Leviathan's power, such as summont Its creations.
Retroact Rain - High-density Remnant Energy from the Etheric Sea that projects past events with uncanny fidelity. The Retroact Rain unfolds in three distinct phases: natural descent, near-ground suspension, and reverse flow.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content: Rust, Sword and the Sun is a Segue in Chapter II of the Main Quest.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content:
You and Abby arrive at Solis Tavern. While waiting for contact from the Ephor's Palace, you run into a blind wandering bard, Nestor. He shares with you Augusta's stories before she rose to power.

A girl whose homeland was devastated by the Dark Tide, Augusta, follows Septimont's Gladiators to the city. Her heart yearns to find the power to protect her home, and the crowd's buzz of the Great Agon catches her attention. The girl thinks this path may help her find the strength she is seeking, so she is determined to participate in the Agon. According to the rules, she needs a mentor. With no identity or status, she faces repeated setbacks until she finally finds Cato as her "lifeline." The girl continues to hone her skills, passing the entry trials Cato set for her, and finally makes her first step into the Agon.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content: The Great Agon draws close as time passes. Besides a mentor, Augusta also needs a sponsor to participate in the Gladiatorial events. Sponsors are mostly nobles and merchants, and for someone with no identity or status, the only place to approach them is the underground arena, where nameless Gladiators are sold like commodities. Realizing she's become the bottom pick, Augusta takes the initiative by offering herself to the nobles and merchants in the audience, only to be met with waves of mockery. An old-school nobleman studies Augusta and offers her a deal: if Augusta manages to pass the three trials he sets, he will become her sponsor.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content: It is the day of the final trial, and the stands are filled with spectators. Everyone is eager to witness how a human will rival the strength of Arsinosa. Augusta looks up as Arsinosa appears. Facing the massive guardian of Septimont, she is unsure when the battle will begin. The moment Arsinosa opens her eyes, she immediately charges towards Augusta, who barely manages to deflect the attack even with her trained reflexes. After several exchanges, Augusta seizes an opportunity to land a strike on Arsinosa, but she is almost at her limit. To Augusta's surprise, Arsinosa halts its attack and bows. The audience erupts with thunderous applause, and the girl is raised to the high platform amidst the cheers. Only then does she realize that after gaining Arsinosa's approval, the people of Septimont will make a special exception for her. Augusta will bypass the Great Agon and be crowned "Champion."

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content:
Nestor has told you everything he knows, yet his stories barely scratch the surface of Augusta's life. In the end, Nestor poses his questions: What is it that has lifted Augusta to the seat of power? What is it that makes a ruler? He expects no quick answers, but hopes you will meet Augusta with these questions in mind and seek the answers yourself.

The Ephor's Palace rings with the Senators' criticisms toward Priestess Iuno as usual. After addressing their complaints, Augusta meets with the center of the grievances herself on the Palace roof. Iuno has some reservations about the upcoming hunting operation and their plans due to the prophecy she saw, but Augusta assures her firmly that she will fight to the very end.

content: Quest Objective: While waiting for contact from the Ephor's Palace, you and Abby arrive at Solis Tavern, where you run into a blind wandering bard—Nestor. Having learned of the Ephor's invitation to the hunt, Nestor shares with you Augusta's stories before she rose to power.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content:
[Objective: (Head to the designated location)]
Abby: Ugh, muggy day... Sky's gloomy, air's all wet...
Abby: Oh, man! At least let me finish my sentence!
Abby: Brrr... cold, cold, cold...
[Dialogue Option]  A hot meal should warm you right up.
Abby: Oh right, I'm famished! We barely had a bite sprinting all the way here from Ragunna...
Abby: Woah, pinch me! This is a feat and a half!
Abby: Hey, Rover... so, uh... we did bring enough money, right? I mean, we kinda rushed out without grabbing anything...
Rover: Oh, that... don't worry, money's not an issue.
Rover: Augusta made sure we're covered. All our food and lodging here in Septimont is billed straight to the Ephor's Palace.
Rover: But...
Rover: I think the owner might've overdone it a little...
Abby: Hah, better get used to it. You're the champ of the Great Agon!
Abby: And you know me. If food's on offer, I'll be a scoffer. No leftovers, guaranteed!
Abby: Mmmf, yum yum...
Abby: Free stay, free meal... This Ephor really knows how to treat guests. Maybe we should, you know, hang around a bit longer.
Abby: (Sniffs) This smells amazing!
Rover: Abby, what do you think Imperator wants me to find? If Cartethyia's right, the last clues should be somewhere on the Sanguis Plateaus.
Rover: We're so close to the finish line, just one step away. But our pace has slowed...
Abby: (Hiccups) Relax! We're already back in Septimont, what's the rush?
Abby: I remember Lupa said there's this weird Blightcloud hanging over the Sanguis Plateaus.
Abby: And when the "High Tide" or whatever rolls around, all the Gladiators go there to hunt Tacet Discords.
Abby: Wait, is the High Tide coming up soon? The Ephor's invite did say something about a big hunt.
Abby: Huh... that reminds me, aren't we supposed to meet her today?!
Rover: A messenger came this morning. Augusta is dealing with an emergency, so our meeting's postponed... looks like it'll be a while.
Rover: An unexpected change. It's throwing everything off course... I don't like the feel of it.
Rover: And why me for this hunt? If it's about the Great Agon... the messenger said none of the other Gladiators were invited.
Abby: Who knows? Maybe she just wants to test her strength against you. Typical Septimontian, right?
Rover: You think so?
Rover: I've only met her a few times, but I doubt she acts on such simple impulses.
Rover: And as the Ephor, can she really thoughtlessly do whatever she wants?
???: Guest from afar, you possess eyes as clear as crystal.
???: But... what troubles you so, that eyes once bright as the highland sky now darken with rolling clouds.
???: ...A warrior who walks the blade's edge does not falter over trifles.*
???: The clouds, if I may guess, are cast from the throne...
???: At the peak of Capitoline Hill, beneath the pale walls of the Ephor's Palace... secrets lie buried. And the most intricate among them are those born from the pursuit of power.
???: Even one as honorable as the Ephor must learn when to be ruthless.
???: In Septimont, a city forged in iron and blood, anyone who seeks the throne without knowing the cost is no better than a lamb marching to the butcher's knife.
[Dialogue Option]  And you are?
Nestor: I am Nestor, a traveling poet.
Nestor: The rains in Septimont never seem eager to leave this season. So then...
Nestor: If you are curious about the Ephor... then allow me to say that nothing would honor me more than to offer even a modest service to the Champion of the Great Agon.
Abby: Wait, how do you know Rover is the Champion? And all that stuff about the Ephor, too...
Abby: ...Your eyes... hmm... Were we talking too loud?
Nestor: To see and to hear are but two of the many ways to perceive. Trusting the senses is a habit, a natural expedience, but not the only option.
Nestor: Truth be told, I've been gathering inspiration for my next epic, and its protagonist is none other than Augusta, the Ephor of Septimont.
Nestor: That's why I speak of her with some familiarity.
Nestor: I have a feeling your tale with her will soon be written. And knowing more about those who walk alongside you is rarely without its benefits.
[Dialogue Option]  Then tell me about Augusta.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Then tell me about Augusta.



Nestor: Augusta—
Nestor: A girl of humble birth, a Resonator of modest talent, a commoner without noble patronage. And yet from the den of wolves that is Septimont City, she rose, and eventually claimed her place.
Nestor: Just like the burning sun was once a cloud of dust.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
subsection: (Quest continues to New Arrival in The Big City)
content:
Nestor: Fail enough times, and you might eventually succeed. Should we call it resilience, or mere stubbornness?
Nestor: Or perhaps, for a girl who has lost everything, there was never a second option. She had no one to trust but herself, and naught but a blade to hold.
Nestor: And yet...
Nestor: As the first stanza of an epic, this is nothing extraordinary.
Nestor: Since the Lament, across the scorched lands of Solaris, I've heard this story repeat itself again and again.
Nestor: Greatness, yes, our era has certainly seen it. But true greatness is never found on the first page of a story.
Nestor: Courage, glory, and honor... such immortal virtus have been etched in tablet and stone. They are never forged overnight.
Nestor: Light as a thread, elusive as the wind, they weave themselves into every twist of fate, tangling with every "insignificant" choice we make.
Abby: Hmm...
[Dialogue Option]  What's wrong, Abby?
Abby: I don't know, it's just unbelievable. The Augusta he's talking about and the Ephor we saw in the arena... No way they're the same person.
Nestor: Heh, a girl far from home, arriving in the city upon Capitoline Hill in pursuit of strength. No title, no status, no wealth...
Nestor: I doubt anyone at the time could've imagined her rising to where she is now.
[Dialogue Option]  No, there might be one.
Nestor: Do you mean... Cato?
Nestor: Do you believe Cato handed her that final victory on purpose, and that his scathing words were a test of her resolve?
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe he had long grown tired of that corrupt system.
Nestor: Then Cato must've been an idealist, to place his faith in a girl with nothing to her name.
Nestor: Now, why don't we keep this question in mind and see where the story leads us.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
subsection: (Quest continues to At the Summit of Septimont)
content:
Nestor: Merely the rough shape of a short epic. This is all I can offer about the Ephor.
Nestor: Now, as a listener, what do you make of my narration?
[Dialogue Option]  I enjoyed it.
Nestor: I appreciate your kind words, my generous listener.
Nestor: I am only a humble wordsmith spinning verses and rhymes. The essence of poetry is granted by those who dare defy their fate.
Nestor: But there is one thing I must confess.
Nestor: Through my words, your knowledge of the Ephor is... partial, at best.
[Dialogue Option]  Nothing special.
Nestor: Unembellished opinion. I appreciate your honesty.
Nestor: If the tale is bland... then perhaps my heart hasn't yet aligned with her noble soul.
Nestor: ...May the ever-burning sun cast away my doubts, and wake my dusty mind from its slumber.
Nestor: But putting uninspired rhetoric aside, I still have one thing to confess.
Nestor: That is, through my words, your knowledge of the Ephor remains, at best, incomplete.
[Dialogue Option]  I still don't know the Ephor enough.
Nestor: In this, you are right.
Nestor: Poetry can only offer a glimpse of the true story. The reality of people, events, and things slips beyond the grasp of words.
Nestor: I do not belong in the pages of the epic, so I remain confined to the observer's gaze. I can imagine events and emotions unfold, but I cannot truly recreate them.
Nestor: Here's some advice for you, though I hesitate to call it such...
Nestor: If you want the truth of a story, step into it. Become part of it. The opportunity stands before you now.
Nestor: As I've said, the tale between you and Augusta, the hero of Septimont, is only now turning its next page.
[Dialogue Option]  You seem to know exactly what I'm about to do.
Nestor: It's not difficult to see. Fate flows like the stars tracing their course. Your destination is written in the steps you take.
Nestor: The rain is passing... I hear it ceasing its symphony upon the earth. It is time for farewells.
Nestor: Before I leave, may I ask you one last question? What is it that has lifted Augusta to the seat of power? What is it that makes a ruler?
Abby: Well... I'd say strength.
Abby: Let's be real. There's no way Augusta could've passed those trials without strength.
Abby: Rover, what do you think?
[Dialogue Option]  It was strength and conquest.
[Dialogue Option]  It was her unyielding resolve.
[Dialogue Option]  It was born from the hardship of the past.
[Dialogue Option]  I don't know.
Nestor: Hehe, you needn't rush to answer now. Keep it in mind as you continue your journey.
Nestor: When the final chapter is written, the answer will reveal itself.
Nestor: Farewell, my friend. Our paths crossed by fate and by chance.
Nestor: Soon after this brief encounter, everything about me will be gone with the wind. But you... your epic continues.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
subsection: (Quest continues to At the Summit of Septimont)
content:
Nestor: Soon after this brief encounter, everything about me will be gone with the wind. But you... your epic continues.



The previous day...
Astute Elder: Your Excellency, you have indulged her too much.
Astute Elder: As the Priestess, Iuno is far too unruly in both action and word. It's a disgrace to her title.
Stuffy Elder: Indeed. She entered the Palace unannounced, uninvited, and with no decorum.
Stuffy Elder: A blatant affront to the authority of the Palace.
Augusta: Heh... same as always.
Augusta: Senators, all she crossed was a doorway. One too insignificant to carry the weight of our authority, or defend anyone's fragile pride.
Augusta: Let us not forget, it is not the walls of Capitoline Hill that command fear.
Augusta: It is my will, my sword, and our relentless conquest.
Augusta: I know your fear. You fear a Priestess's voice drowning yours, and a rebel challenging the Senate's rules.
Augusta: But listen well, power does not bow to sycophants cowering behind their traditions.
Augusta: If you seek power, then step from the shadows. Face me and prove yourself worthy.

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
subsection: (Quest continues to At the Summit of Septimont)
content:
Augusta: If you seek power, then step from the shadows. Face me and prove yourself worthy.



Iuno: Took you long enough, Augusta.
Augusta: Handling the senators takes time. You know that.
Augusta: Well, to keep our esteemed Priestess from waiting, maybe next time I'll just leave them to their own devices.
Augusta: I'll make sure they record every detail of your "feat" and relay it word-for-word to Grandmother .
Augusta: "Priestess Iuno: Unruly behavior, left Tetragon Temple without permission and trespassed into the Ephor's Palace."
Augusta: ...I wonder, who will lose it first, Lillibet or you?
Iuno: Let those old foxes report me all they want.
Iuno: If they step into the Tetragon left foot first, I'll shoot the left. Right foot first? I'll shoot the right.
Augusta: Heh, I'm with you on that one.
Augusta: The Senate should be reminded now and then that the Tetragon's kindness is not a reason to take Priestess Iuno lightly.
Augusta: Why didn't you wait there? I had everything handled. We depart for the hunting ground tonight.
Augusta: If anything changed, you could've reached me by my Terminal. You didn't need to come all the way here... I want you free of duty until that day arrives.
Iuno: You're overthinking it, Augusta. I'm here to see that person.
Iuno: Grandmother Lillibet said his fate is one of "unknowable void." Sounds intriguing enough to make time for.
Augusta: So that's it. Too bad. The ship from Ragunna won't dock until tomorrow morning, and we'll be gone by then.
Iuno: Ugh, what a hassle.
Augusta: Patience, Iuno. Rover has accepted the invitation, so you'll have plenty of time to meet during the hunt.
Augusta: Is there something else you want to say?
Iuno: ...
Iuno: I read Grandma Lillibet's . The hunt and our plan... neither end well.
Iuno: Are you sure... we should go through with this?
Augusta: Risk does not trouble me. Peril simply requires greater strength. But really, when did you start caring about the Temple's traditions?
Iuno: ...
Iuno: "O ye faithless of Septimont, the Divinity is enraged. Should your ruler defy Their will again, doom shall be your fate."
Iuno: Lately I've been hearing murmurs from the nobles again, about the ancient prophecy from Ragunna...
Augusta: I will admit, those words once carried weight.
Augusta: But when our ancestors crossed the waters and climbed these hills, Ragunna's "Divinity" didn't get a seat on the ship.
Augusta: And the Priestesses all said the prophecy was incomplete.
Augusta: "Only the  wielding extraordinary power, risen from the dark tides, shall bring eternity to Septimont. Then shall the waters quiet, the tempest still, and glory return with the blood of the old king."
Augusta: Do not forget, this is the other half of the prophecy.
Augusta: Fabius, Atilius, Valeria... One after another, these heroes have saved Septimont from the brink of ruin.
Augusta: As long as a hero stands, no disaster can break this eternal city.
Iuno: What if… this time is different? What if ruin is our fate?
Augusta: ...
Augusta: Then I will sever that fate with my blade.
Augusta: Haha...
Iuno: What's so amusing?
Augusta: o the fearless Priestess Iuno can be frightened after all...
Augusta: But it's fine. If you're afraid, don't push yourself. I can handle this alone.
Augusta: Most Revered Priestess, wait for me in the Temple. I shall return victorious.
Iuno: Frightened? Me? If anything, it's you, trying to shut me out and face it alone.
Iuno: Fine. Go ahead. You'll come back to me sooner or later.
Augusta: That, I can't deny.
Iuno: Ha! I knew it. So you do need me for this hunt.
Augusta: Thank you, Iuno.
Iuno: ...Why are you saying this?
Augusta: The storm is coming...
Augusta: Come, Iuno, my friend. The best way to greet a storm... is to walk straight into it.
(Obtain Trophy: Blood and Sun)

title: Rust, Sword and the Sun
content:
Sanguis Plateaus - The Sanguis Plateaus were once the Septimont frontline against the Dark Tide. Due to the region's unique landscape, Remnant energy gathers here in unusual density, along with a Blightcloud perpetually looming overhead, formed since the first Dark Tide. During High Tide seasons, Gladiators from across Septimont arrive here to hunt Dark Tide creations in the name of glory.

Lillibet - The current Head Priestess of Septimont.

Book of Prophecies - A scroll Lillibet carries, recording visions glimpsed in the flame light. Both this book and the murals within Tetragon Temple are media through which the Priestesses of Septimont convey prophecies to the people.

Hero of Heroes - The legendary ruler of Septimont. The legend traces its roots to an ancient prophecy that only the one who becomes the Hero of Heroes can save Septimont from falling into ruin.

title: New Arrival in The Big City
content:
New Arrival in The Big City is a Gameplay subpart in Rust, Sword and the Sun, in Chapter II of the Main Quest.
During this quest, you must manage 4 Attributes (Health, Martialism, Willpower and Reputation). If any of those attributes reach 0, a Game Over happens.

metadata.page_title: New Arrival in The Big City

title: New Arrival in The Big City
content:
Nestor: Dear guest from afar, do follow me into the near-forgotten stories of Augusta. But simply telling it might be a bit dull.
[Dialogue Option]  What are you trying to do?
[Dialogue Option]  What methods do you have in mind?
Nestor: Perhaps, having the listener become the protagonist of such stories might be a good option. This should add a more "immersive" touch to the sounds and images you've yet to hear and see.
Nestor: At this moment, you are Augusta. You shall relive her past. Face the same choices she once made. Thus... please forget your name for now.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm ready.
[Dialogue Option]  Are we role playing?
Nestor: Of course, Augusta's story is already written. No matter what choices you'd make, they will not alter our reality.
Nestor: Yet, be wary. Fate is fickle, and a misstep can lead to a swift end. Weigh your choices carefully.
[Dialogue Option]  Her past decisions may not have always been the best.
[Dialogue Option]  I understand.
Nestor: Well, then. Let the story begin. Set aside the complex thoughts, and let me sing the epic of a young girl—Augusta.
[Dialogue Option]  I am Augusta. I am Augusta.
[Dialogue Option]  Take a deep breath.
A gentle, warm light begins to blur your vision, and you slowly close your eyes... When it clears, a small, frightened girl clutching a sword stands amidst the ruins. A group of solemn Septimontian Gladiators stands guard around her.
Gladiator: Hey, kid, are you alone? Don't be afraid. We know what the Dark Tide did to your home, and we're here to help.
[Dialogue Option]  Timidly observe the man in front of you. (+ Health)
[Dialogue Option]  Boldly observe the man in front of you. (+ Health)
Gladiator: You must be hungry. Here, this should be enough to keep you from starving for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Refuse the food offered by the Gladiator. (- Health)
[Dialogue Option]  Take the food offered by the Gladiator. (+ Health)
Gladiator: We can take you to Septimont City. It's not safe here. We don't know when the next disaster will strike. Staring at these ruins won't change anything.
Gladiator: Even if you rebuild these walls a thousand times, they'll never hold against the Dark Tide. You don't have the strength to stop it. Bring your sword and come with us...
[Dialogue Option]  Let go of your sword. (- Martialism)
[Dialogue Option]  Grip your sword with determination. (+ Martialism)
The Gladiators shake their heads and pat your shoulder.
[Dialogue Option]  Look back at the ruined village. (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Follow them. (+ Willpower)
In the end, you chose to leave the village. The Gladiators' words revealed a bitter truth: you lacked the strength to protect the home you are leaving behind. In your travels, you...
[Dialogue Option]  Stay quiet. (- Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Engage with the Gladiators. (+ Reputation)
Following the Gladiators, you arrive in the City of Septimont by ship. You wave them goodbye after arriving at the central square. Meanwhile, you notice the square is crowded with citizens.
[Dialogue Option]  Remain quiet and anxious. (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Show your awe of the city. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
A poster for the Gladiator's Agon is pinned to a wooden board. The air is filled with heated chatter about the upcoming match.
[Dialogue Option]  The gathering people push you towards the crowd. (- Health)
[Dialogue Option]  Draw closer to the crowd. (+ Willpower)
Septimontian Onlookers: You must know, Septimont reveres strength. Here, only the victor reigns. That is a law older than the city itself.
[Dialogue Option]  You notice the disdain in the eyes of this Septimontian. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  You notice the passion-filled eyes of this Septimontian. (+ Reputation)
Septimontian Onlookers: Eat or be eaten, such is the way of this city. To survive, you'll have to find your bite and seize the crown with your own teeth.
You can't stop thinking about their conversation. You realize that Gladiators are the very symbol of strength in Septimont. If there's a way to dominate the arena, maybe you'll find the strength you're looking for...
[Dialogue Option]  Tear down the poster and walk away from the crowd. (- Health, + Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Quietly leave the crowd. (+ Willpower)
As you leave, you notice that three words stand out in the incessant chatter: identity, status, and talent. They seem to be an essential part of gladiating.
Arrogant Septimontian: There are always those commoners who view the Agon as mere boring displays of butchery. But we're hardly entertained by the sight of rats shrieking in the dirt. What we crave is true magnificence, a warrior who can make roses bloom from blood.
Cold Septimontian: Wanna have a little bet on how many mangy rats are gonna try for the Agon this year? Them and their stench be stinking up the place.
[Dialogue Option]  You're slightly concerned about your status and talents. (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Ignore their words. (+ Willpower)
Nestor: You are determined to step onto the arena. The rules demand a mentor at your back. Someone to keep death from claiming you on the first day, and perhaps even teach you to see the fight through to the end.
Nestor: After hitting several dead ends, you eventually come across Cato. Cato is a retired Gladiator star but takes on few proteges.
Cato: So you want to join the Agon, you say? Why don't you start by telling me a little about yourself?
You recall the discussions about Gladiators—identity, status, and talents. People in the city of Septimont seem to value these more than anything. You choose to...
[Dialogue Option]  Lie about your past. (DEAD END)
Cato: Done with your little tale? You can't even bring yourself to say who you really are. What good is strength and power to you?
Cato: Adorning yourself like this... Hah, you're just wearing a fake crown to cover your cowerdice. What else wouldn't you abandon if you can toss away your home and your name! Please, leave, now!
[Dialogue Option]  Speak honestly about your past. (+ Reputation)
Cato: The Dark Tide took your home, and you came to Septimont seeking strength. Is that so? You've got some mettle, but that's not gonna cut it here.
Cato: Go home. People like you always show up with nothing but fancy dreams, only to see them crushed and trampled. I've seen enough of idiots like you.
[Dialogue Option]  Stay silent. (- Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Try to argue. (+ Willpower, - Reputation)
Cato: What now? Still here, are you? You think your stubbornness will change my mind? Pathetic.
[Dialogue Option]  Tighten your grip on the sword. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Look Cato straight in the eye. (+ Reputation)
Cato: Alright then, let's have a duel. Land one strike and you win. If you manage that, I'll teach you how to be a true Gladiator. This duel here is your entrance trial.
[Dialogue Option]  Accept the duel without hesitation. (+ Martialism, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Accept the duel after great deliberation. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
Blades meet in a sharp clash. Cato moves with practiced ease. You are quickly defeated.
Cato: Strengthless. Do you realize how weak you are?
[Dialogue Option]  Which is why I want to become a Gladiator. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Which is why I am seeking power. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
Cato: Heh, do you really know who you're fighting against? Can you really best me? You can't. Now, how do you plan to end this?
[Dialogue Option]  Challenge him again the next day. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Give up. (DEAD END)
Your will crumbles. There you stand, gazing up at that towering peak men call "Strength," frozen at the hill's very foot. Perhaps a simple life is your best choice.
Cato: Back for Round two, are we? Country rats like you sure are as pestering as the city folks say you are, huh?
[Dialogue Option]  Defend. (+ Health, - Martialism)
[Dialogue Option]  Attack. (- Health, + Martialism)
Just like last time, you aren't much of a challenge to Cato. You are swiftly beaten once again.
Cato: Go back. This is not your path...
[Dialogue Option]  Continue the challenge on the third day. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Give up. (DEAD END)
Your will crumbles. There you stand, gazing up at that towering peak men call "Strength," frozen at the hill's very foot. Perhaps a simple life is your best choice.
Cato: Too slow, too weak... Your foolish swings only bring smiles to your enemies.
[Dialogue Option]  Then I'll be stronger. (+ Martialism, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Then I'll be faster. (+ Martialism, + Reputation)
Cato: Is that your best? How naive. Well, I guess a rat that lives in the dark is never meant for the sun. Checkmate. You've lost.
[Dialogue Option]  Challenge him again on the fourth day. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Give up. (DEAD END)
Your will crumbles. There you stand, gazing up at that towering peak men call "Strength," frozen at the hill's very foot. Perhaps a simple life is your best choice.
Cato: Still not ready to give up? Why don't you sell your sword? It'll get you some food at least.
[Dialogue Option]  Continue the challenge on the fifth day. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Give up. (DEAD END)
Your will crumbles. There you stand, gazing up at that towering peak men call "Strength," frozen at the hill's very foot. Perhaps a simple life is your best choice.
You stand before Cato again. Dragging your exhausted body, nearly at your limit.
[Dialogue Option]  I can still fight... (- Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I'm about to collapse... (- Willpower, + Reputation)
The wind swept up by the blade whispers past, and you're suddenly home. Soft sunlight cascades on the great oak's leaves, and you hear your friends' laughter, your parents' gentle calls.
But in the very next breath, a bone-deep chill engulfs you. That touch, you know it all too well. Thoughts race across your mind, and your hand instinctively gripped the sword hilt.
[Dialogue Option]  I won't surrender... (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I can't stop here... (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
You seize the opening and land a hit on Cato.
Cato hands you his sword and turns to leave...
[Dialogue Option]  Call out to Cato. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Catch Cato's sword. It's rather heavy. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Cato: In Septimont's arena, the victor claims the weapon of the defeated, a symbol of conquest. This sword is yours now...
[Dialogue Option]  Conquest... (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Victor... (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Cato: If you are determined to bite off that crown, do not fall before you get there. Augusta, that's your name, isn't it?
[Dialogue Option]  Yes. I am Augusta. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Nod. (+ Reputation)
Cato: The moment you step into the arena, you will lose this name. The spectators may brand you with a number, a symbol, or even the name of some wild beast.
[Dialogue Option]  I have no other choice. (- Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I am prepared. (+ Reputation)
Cato: And only the last one standing has the right to reclaim their true name.
Cato: By then, all will be chanting your name—Augusta. You'll have to conquer their hearts and win their applause even without identity, status, and talents. Tell me, will I see that day?
[Dialogue Option]  I will make them know my true name. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I will make the crowd cheer. (+ Reputation)
Cato: Training starts tomorrow. Six sharp. Right here.

metadata.page_title: New Arrival in The Big City

title: Gladiator Training
content:
Gladiator Training is a Gameplay subpart in Rust, Sword and the Sun, in Chapter II of the Main Quest.
During this quest, you must manage 4 Attributes (Health, Martialism, Willpower and Reputation). If any of those attributes reach 0, a Game Over happens.

title: Gladiator Training
content:
Nestor: Dawn breaks with a pale glow. A month has already passed under Cato's training. And today, the grind continues.
[Dialogue Option]  A little rest won't hurt. I'll go later. (+ Health, - Martialism, - Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Stick to the training schedule. (- Health, + Martialism, + Willpower)
You arrive at the training site. Repeating the same moves over and over again has begun to wear on your patience. You notice some Gladiators training in moves you've never seen before. You decide to...
[Dialogue Option]  Peek into their training. (+ Martialism, - Willpower, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Stay focused and keep to your own training. (+ Martialism, + Willpower, + Reputation)
You reflect on your training. It was always you alone, facing the wooden post, patching yourself up, over and over.
[Dialogue Option]  Give in to sadness. (+ Health, - Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Endure and push through. (- Health, + Willpower)
Days slip by, and the Gladiator's Agon draws near. Today, Cato will give you one final lesson...
Cato: I've done all I can to prepare you. Now, you're on your own.
[Dialogue Option]  Is this the graduation ceremony?
[Dialogue Option]  The training ends today?
Cato: Here's my final task for you: tell me, why do you want to become a Gladiator? What pulls you through all this training?
[Dialogue Option]  You are unsure of what to say. (DEAD END)
As the memories of your homeland begin to fade, you start questioning why you put yourself through this hellish training.
You stand frozen in doubt, and then fear. Without waiting any longer, Cato shakes his head and walks away.
[Dialogue Option]  You already know the answer. (+ Willpower)
Nestor: Your ideal has never faltered since you left home: to be strong enough to protect others. You meet Cato's gaze, and he reads the answer in your eyes.
[Dialogue Option]  Offer Cato your thanks. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I remember my true ambition. (+ Willpower)
In the meantime, a flicker of desire crosses your eyes. You recall Cato's words from when this all started—
Cato: By then, all will be chanting your name—Augusta. You'll have to conquer their hearts and win their applause even without identity, status, and talents. Tell me, will I see that day?
[Dialogue Option]  I very much look forward to it. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  I will make it happen. (+ Willpower)
You're aware that sponsors for the Gladiator's Agon are mostly nobles and wealthy merchants, figures beyond your reach, except, perhaps, in the underground arena...
Underground Merchant: Hehe. These are all top-of-the-line "merchandise" I got here. Care to have a look?
Like products on display, you and a few other Gladiators stand in the middle of the underground arena, scrutinized by nobles and wealthy merchants in the stands. One by one, those beside you are chosen and escorted away.
[Dialogue Option]  Volunteer yourself. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Take a step forward. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
The audience cast their eyes in your direction. However, all you receive is constant laughter in return.
[Dialogue Option]  Glimpses of the nobles' lavish lifestyle flicker through. (- Health, - Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Visions of your home's ruin flash within your mind. (- Health, - Willpower)
Augusta: These laughs... So they really did have a hand in that disaster...
[Dialogue Option]  The rot in high places also played a part in your home's ruin. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  The Dark Tide alone did not destroy your home. (+ Willpower)
When the Dark Tide struck, those with power and wealth continued their life of indulgence and luxury. The might of the Gladiators existed only to serve their desires.
[Dialogue Option]  Silently, you swear to shatter these rules. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  A fire of anger ignites in your chest. (- Health, + Willpower)
Arrogant Noble: Well, well, a village girl with such unremarkable Forte dreaming of power and strength. I can't remember the last time Septimont had a joke this amusing.
[Dialogue Option]  Show them your sword. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Try, and you'll see. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Arrogant Noble: What can you offer? Prancing around like a circus clown and scrambling for your life so we can all have a good laugh? Or do you think playing innocent will win you favor?
[Dialogue Option]  Don't underestimate me. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  I never disappoint. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Arrogant Noble: Anyone interested in this one? After all, watching the weak struggle is always a fine source of entertainment.
[Dialogue Option]  You bear a small anticipation that someone will pick you. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  You give the nobles a chilling stare as they talk in whispers. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Old-school Noble: Entertainment, you say... Heh, in Septimont, strength defines worth. We shouldn't be so quick to judge a Gladiator who offers herself.
You turn your view towards the voice. With heavy steps, a well-dressed old-school noble walks down from the stands towards you.
He smells of rotten stench. It's unlike the smell of rats as the Septimontians had put it, but a foul odor of power and wealth.
[Dialogue Option]  Silently clench your fist.
[Dialogue Option]  You frown at the old-school noble.
Old-school Noble: I engage only in profitable ventures. To stand in the arena, you must prove your worth. I have three trials for you. Survive them, and we may speak further, brave young lady.

title: The Impossible Trial
content:
Gladiator Training is a Gameplay subpart in Rust, Sword and the Sun, in Chapter II of the Main Quest.
During this quest, you must manage 4 Attributes (Health, Martialism, Willpower and Reputation). If any of those attributes reach 0, a Game Over happens.

title: The Impossible Trial
content:
Nestor: You accept the noble's trials. Though "trials" is too fine a word for something intended only to break you.
[Dialogue Option]  Head to the trial grounds.
[Dialogue Option]  Head to the trial grounds.
Outside the walls of Septimont City lies a wasteland plagued by the Dark Tide, your homeland.
[Dialogue Option]  Returning home, you can't help but feel sentimental. (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  It's now different from the home you remember. (+ Reputation)
They say a ferocious Lion Beast corrupted by the Dark Tide prowls deep within a cave. No common blade can cut through its skin.
Your first trial is to slay that beast. The noble, however, decides to strip you of all equipment but a dull sword.
[Dialogue Option]  A dull sword is more than enough. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  I have no choice but to accept. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
The mountain trail winds like a serpent. Among the charred tree stumps, dozens of bleached skeletons lie scattered. You suspect you're getting close as you continue forward against the unpleasant smell.
When the first rays of sunlight split the clouds, the cave reveals itself, breathing death. Before you get a clear picture of the cave, a crushing force presses down upon you.
[Dialogue Option]  Try to break free. (+ Martialism, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Who are you? (- Health)
???: Shhh, get down! You trying to get yourself killed? Hold your breath or you'll alert it!
[Dialogue Option]  Struggle. (+ Martialism, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Do as he says. (- Health, + Reputation)
You turn around and see a hunter. Just then, a massive beast roars and walks past where you are hiding.
[Dialogue Option]  Secretly stare at it. (+ Health, + Martialism)
[Dialogue Option]  Keep your head down. (- Health, - Willpower)
After the Lion Beast has left, you apologize to the hunter. It was thanks to him the beast did not notice you.
Hunter: Going by those clothes, you're a Septimont Gladiator, eh? Heh, I used to be just like you. Lost a big match, got tossed out by the nobles, and ended up like this. We're nothing but their playthings.
The skills honed for battle are now merely tools for survival. Septimont has abandoned the strength it desperately needs. You pity such reality.
[Dialogue Option]  Ask the hunter what you should do. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Ask the hunter about the Lion Beast. (+ Martialism, + Reputation)
Hunter: Only a madman would go after that lion.
[Dialogue Option]  I know what I'm doing. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  I have my reasons. (+ Willpower)
His words are rough, but he eventually tells you everything he knows.
You bid the hunter farewell and make preparations for the hunt. To gain more knowledge of your "prey," you choose to silently observe the Lion Beast in the following days.
After a few days, you've managed to grasp an overall behavior pattern of the Lion Beast. Thus, you march towards the deep cave.
[Dialogue Option]  Enter the cave.
[Dialogue Option]  Enter the cave.
Deep within the cave's dark embrace, you tread softly. Then, a sudden dread freezes your steps. Between the flickering torch flames, a monstrous shape appears: the Lion Beast. Fire from the nether dances amid its golden mane, while claws like scythes tear wounds in the earth.
[Dialogue Option]  Maintain distance and swing your sword. (+ Health, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Draw your sword and strike the Lion Beast. (- Health, + Martialism)
As you expected, your sword fails you. It's ineffective against the lion. Before you can take a breath, the lion's thunderous roar storms you again. You decide to...
[Dialogue Option]  Quickly analyze the cave's environment. (+ Health, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Dodge its attack and search for a weak point. (+ Health, + Martialism)
Augusta: No good, can't find an opening... It's moving faster and reaching further. Can't keep this up.
Augusta: If strength alone isn't enough... Perhaps... I can borrow some help...
Just before the Lion Beast pounces at you, you slash with all your strength at the stalactite above. It crashes down into the lion's gaping jaws.
[Dialogue Option]  It still has the fight.
[Dialogue Option]  It's not over yet.
You land on its neck. It lunges to seize you, but your swift dodges force its claws into a deadly knot around its throat. Seeing your chance, you give a final pull, and the beast strangles itself in a frantic struggle.
[Dialogue Option]  Finally... (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Guess using the environment is one way to do it. (+ Martialism)
The trial has ended, and you drag your exhausted body towards the stream. Clear water cascades down into the mountain valley, and the dense forest slumbers quietly in nature's cradle.
You rinse your blood-stained hands in the water. The clear stream slowly turns red. The birds scatter and the fish vanish. You sense the forest's unease at your presence.
[Dialogue Option]  Are they afraid of my power?
[Dialogue Option]  Are they afraid of me?
The critters' panic plunges you into reflection. For the first time, you realize that power can instill fear.
[Dialogue Option]  You are still somewhat shaken. (- Health, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  You desire more power. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
With no time to rest, you approach the nobleman again. He imposes the second trial upon you.
[Dialogue Option]  I know full well the next one won't be easy. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  What is it this time? (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Old-school Noble: Killing a mad beast is hardly an achievement. I'm sure you're aware, girl, that all the warriors of Septimont have "two lives."
[Dialogue Option]  Cato seemed to mention this before.
[Dialogue Option]  "Two lives"?
Old-school Noble: One by their parents, and the other by their sword. You may consider the sword in a Gladiator's hand as their "life" in the arena.
Old-school Noble: For your second trial... Bring me one hundred "lives." Yes, prove to me you are worthy of standing in the arena.
[Dialogue Option]  Turn with disgust as you wave to accept. (+ Willpower, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Calmly accept. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
To get the "admission pass" for the Agon, you start the second trial. Day after day, you fight Gladiators of Septimont. As your reputation grows, so do the spectators. They don't care who you are, but only want to see when you will fall.
Septimontian Onlookers: Look, it's that girl again. Didn't think she would get as many wins as she did. Just look at the size of her. How will she even carry those swords?
[Dialogue Option]  Focus on the opponent before you. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Ignore their comments. (+ Willpower, - Reputation)
You have grown used to this kind of noise. The deafening cheers numb your fatigue. Your sword now rests against your opponent's throat.
[Dialogue Option]  Spare the opponent and wait for the next challenger. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Suppress your desire to kill. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
One by one, the Gladiators you've challenged grow in numbers. Those you've defeated kneel before you, offering their swords symbolizing their honor with both hands.
[Dialogue Option]  Steadily plant the opponent's sword into the ground. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Raise the opponent's sword. (+ Reputation)
Even in Septimont, there's a limit to opponents that prove a challenge to you. Eventually, you will need to seek out tougher challengers. You have targeted Viktor, a frequent champion of the Agon from one of the noble houses.
Noble's Servant: Do you have any idea who Viktor's father is? His lordship is the largest sponsor of the Agon.
Noble's Servant: Power, wealth, those aren't things brute strength can rival. Viktor has the best mentor, the finest weapon...
[Dialogue Option]  Oh? So what?
[Dialogue Option]  Indeed.
The house behind Viktor comes to you with an offer. A perfect job and a substantial fortune, if you walk away from the duel.
[Dialogue Option]  Take the offer. (DEAD END)
Noble's Servant: A wise choice. Rest assured, beauty, I'll put in a good word for you with my master...
Tempted by the offer, you sign the contract, only to find it's all a lie. No job, no money, nothing. You recall the noble's mockery... In their eyes, you are but a circus clown.
[Dialogue Option]  Rip the contract. (+ Willpower)
You reject the bribe without a second thought. Humiliated, the noble's servant spits curses in your face.
[Dialogue Option]  Say nothing. Avoid any altercations. (+ Willpower, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Respond calmly. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Noble's Servant: You ignorant country peasant. Do you know what it means to refuse a noble? Hmph, then you shall suffer for your arrogance. When the time comes, don't expect any pity as you won't be getting any.
[Dialogue Option]  Eye the scion beside the servant. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Ignore the servant. (+ Willpower, - Reputation)
The scion silences the rambling servant and tears up the contract.
Viktor: Let's go. There is no point in talking sense into an ignorant fool. Then again, I'd appreciate it if you don't waste too much of my time in the arena.
They throw a bag of Credits as a way to humiliate you, following it up with sarcasm and mocking gestures. They attempt to overwhelm you with their pride.
[Dialogue Option]  Retaliate with the same insults. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  You feel nothing. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
The day arrives. Viktor accepts your challenge with his honor of nobility as the stake. You remember well the haughty look he wore but a few days prior.
But the nobles wield only words, not swords. Viktor knows nothing about swordsmanship. You easily defeat the weak, incompetent scion, and casually lift his pretty helmet with the tip of your sword.
[Dialogue Option]  Stare at the watching nobles with contempt. (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Approach the nobles' seats. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
Augusta: I have won. And I achieved it without wasting your time. Do you see? Your gilded lies shatter before real strength!
[Dialogue Option]  Toss the helmet back to Viktor. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Step on  helmet. (+ Willpower)
The crowd erupts in cheers and applause. The nobles, unable to deny your triumph, lower their heads.
You return to your lodging to count your trophies: ninety-nine swords, ninety-nine opponents defeated. Now, only one "life" is left to claim... Most Gladiators have long feared your reputation and dare not challenge you, except one...
Aridel, the rising star of the underground arena. Unlike you, he was born with powerful Forte. He is undoubtedly the "king" of the arena.
[Dialogue Option]  A sword tempered by countless battles is no less sharp. (+ Martialism, + Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Talents no longer matter to me. (+ Willpower)
Amidst the endless chanting of the name "Aridel," you arrive as promised.
[Dialogue Option]  Even the old-school noble is present this time.
[Dialogue Option]  As always, spectators crowd the arena.
Your opponent's towering physique dwarfs yours, and his crushing presence brings to mind the fearsome Lion Beast.
After several exchanges, you notice something unusual. The floor is too slippery to gain a foothold, and Aridel's armor is unusually heavy... You are all too familiar with the nobles' despicable tricks.
[Dialogue Option]  Anger brews within you. (- Health, + Willpower, - Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Keep calm. (+ Health, + Willpower, + Reputation)
You then shift your pace, luring Aridel into the very trap meant for you. After a few more rounds, his steps grow loose, his reactions sluggish.
[Dialogue Option]  Now's the chance! (+ Martialism)
[Dialogue Option]  Seize the opportunity! (+ Martialism)
Your sword stops just before the neck of Septimont's strongest Gladiator. The entire arena falls silent, and almost immediately, the crowd erupts into applause.
Spectators: Stab! Stab! Stab...
[Dialogue Option]  Is that so... (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  What? (- Willpower)
Spectators: Kill! Kill! Kill...
[Dialogue Option]  Right here? (- Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  Now? (- Willpower)
(Aridel closes his eyes and accepts his fate)
[Dialogue Option]  Victory is already mine. (+ Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Let's leave it there... (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
In front of everyone's watchful eye, you only take Aridel's sword. You then bow towards the audience before turning to leave.
[Dialogue Option]  You feel a sense of relief. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  You feel the people's gaze. (+ Reputation)
Spectators: ...
Spectators: Live! Live! Live!
[Dialogue Option]  Leave the cheers behind you. (+ Willpower, + Reputation)
[Dialogue Option]  Look back at the crowd and wave. (+ Reputation)
The next day, you arrive before the old-school nobles with one hundred "lives."
Old-school Noble: Hmph, Aridel is merely made of Septimontian flesh. Above him stands a far greater force.
[Dialogue Option]  Power beyond any Septimontian... (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  I'm ready for the third trial. (+ Willpower)
Old-school Noble: Your third trial is to earn the blessing of Arsinosa (Lioness of Glory).
[Dialogue Option]  He never planned to let me pass the trial... (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  This is an impossible feat... (+ Willpower)
Augusta: I know Arsinosa. It has never tasted defeat. People say it's a peak no humans can ever reach. The last wall of Septimont. But...
[Dialogue Option]  I have no reason to yield! (+ Willpower)
[Dialogue Option]  I accept. (+ Willpower)
It is this insurmountable challenge that stirs the thirst for victory in your blood. You accept the third trial: to confront the guardian of Septimont, Arsinosa.

title: At the Summit of Septimont
content:
' is a Gameplay subpart in .
During this quest, you must manage 4 Attributes (Health, Martialism, Willpower and Reputation). If any of those attributes reach 0, a Game Over happens.

title: At the Summit of Septimont
content: It is the day of the final trial, and the stands are filled with spectators. Everyone is eager to witness how a human will rival the strength of Arsinosa. Augusta looks up as Arsinosa appears. Facing the massive guardian of Septimont, she is unsure when the battle will begin. The moment Arsinosa opens her eyes, she immediately charges towards Augusta, who barely manages to deflect the attack even with her trained reflexes. After several exchanges, Augusta seizes an opportunity to land a strike on Arsinosa, but she is almost at her limit. To Augusta's surprise, Arsinosa halts its attack and bows. The audience erupts with thunderous applause, and the girl is raised to the high platform amidst the cheers. Only then does she realize that after gaining Arsinosa's approval, the people of Septimont will make a special exception for her. Augusta will bypass the Great Agon and be crowned "Champion."

title: At the Summit of Septimont
content:
Nestor: On the eve of the trial, you return to the training grounds once again. While you wait for Cato, you find yourself standing before the familiar wooden post. It has been your most enduring companion in your pursuit of true strength.
[Dialogue Option]  Hug it gently.
[Dialogue Option]  Cut it down, and leave the past behind.
Cato: "Well? Not particularly an easy path, is it? Tell me, what did you learn from this path?"
[Dialogue Option]  Strength can instill fear.
[Dialogue Option]  Strength can be destructive.
Cato: "Strength brings conquest. Such is humanity's oldest rule. Augusta, I'll be there for your last trial, and I will call your name for all to hear."
[Dialogue Option]  I will not stop here.
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you.
Back in your room, you stare blankly at your stacked collection of swords. These trophies symbolize strength and conquest, but how will you show them to the world?
[Dialogue Option]  (Continue)
You once heard the tale of a legendary Gladiator. A warrior who would always fuse their opponent's swords with their own after victory. Now, you decide to tread the same path and stand before the smithy.
[Dialogue Option]  Stop outside the blacksmith's forge.
[Dialogue Option]  Gaze at the flying sparks from the blacksmith's forge.
You wish to demonstrate your strength, yet now you still seek to do this with power not of your own... Watching the blacksmith's hammer rise and fall, an seemingly impractical idea emerges.
[Dialogue Option]  (Continue)
—In the end, you use your Forte to fuse all the swords into one.
(Proof of Honor - Forging a great sword)
[Dialogue Option]  Grip the heavy sword in your hand.
[Dialogue Option]  Feel the power.
Your Forte never stood out among Resonators. But its seemingly insignificant power is enough to be stronger than the forge fire and hammer swings.
[Dialogue Option]  (Continue)
The day of the final trial has finally arrived. You walk to the arena's center with your "newly forged" sword. The bronze horns blare from atop the twelve stone pillars. All eyes are on you. Everyone is eager to witness how a human will rival the strength of Arsinosa.
[Dialogue Option]  Survey your surroundings.
[Dialogue Option]  Take a deep breath
Suddenly, a rumbling roar cut through the noise of the crowd. The nobles' banners flutter and fall. A colossal shadow swallows the sunlight around you Arsinosa appears.
[Dialogue Option]  Arsinosa's mountainous size catches your eye.
[Dialogue Option]  There's a slight ringing in your ears.
"It's awake!" A noble shrieked. Arsinosa stands silently opposite you. Slowly, its eyes open, coldly watching you.
[Dialogue Option]  Focus and stay alert.
[Dialogue Option]  Rest your hand on the hilt.
With a sudden sweep of her tail, the Lioness shatters the stone pillar. You roll aside, barely dodging the flying debris. A chill seeps through the tear in the cloth of your left shoulder.
[Dialogue Option]  Take the initiative.
[Dialogue Option]  Take up a defensive stance.
The screams from the stands are soon drowned by the Lioness's roar. A wave of sound and dust rips past your ears. You can taste blood on your lips and tongue.
[Dialogue Option]  Quickly patch yourself up.
[Dialogue Option]  Ignore the pain and tend to the wound later.
Her second attack comes without warning. You barely have time to react before your sword rises to meet her descending paws.
[Dialogue Option]  Recall your encounters from previous battles.
[Dialogue Option]  This strike shall be my all.
You manage to withstand Arsinosa's fierce attack, and at the moment it withdraws, seize the opportunity to thrust your blade into the ancient crack in its right foreleg. Golden blood spills the arena.
[Dialogue Option]  Steady your breath.
[Dialogue Option]  Look up at Arsinosa.
Arsinosa ceases her attack, her mane brushing against your bloodstained face before she lowers her head. The arena shakes with applause. You hear the crowd chant your name in honor.
(Summit of Septimont - Gained Arsinosa's acceptance)
[Dialogue Option]  I have passed the final trial.
[Dialogue Option]  I have gained the Lioness's blessing.
Augusta: "The voices... They are..."
[Dialogue Option]  Listen to the waves of cheers.
[Dialogue Option]  Listen to the waves of cheers.
Septimontian Citizen: "O wise and noble Arsinosa, the mighty guardian of Septimont! Bestow upon her the crown of courage and strength!"
[Dialogue Option]  Walk up the steps after Arsinosa.
[Dialogue Option]  Walk up the steps after Arsinosa.
Septimontian Citizen: "When the cries of triumph resonate with the earth, we see the fire of humanity blaze across Septimont."
[Dialogue Option]  Wave after wave of applause. The Septimontians salute me as I advance.
[Dialogue Option]  Wave after wave of applause. The Septimontians salute me as I advance.
Septimontian Citizen: "O sun and moon, witness this extraordinary feat! Witness her epic dedication to Septimont."
[Dialogue Option]  Take another step forward.
[Dialogue Option]  Take another step forward.
As the platform rises, you realize that by earning Arsinosa's blessing, you have been granted a privilege.
[Dialogue Option]  They are all bowing to me.
[Dialogue Option]  They are all bowing to me.
You are crowned the Champion without the Great Agon. Nevertheless, you have already conquered countless Gladiators with your strength. Under everyone's gaze, glory now bows at your feet.
[Dialogue Option]  Silence the crowd.
Raise your sword.

title: At the Summit of Septimont
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Silence the crowd.
Raise your sword.



Nestor: At last, you stand atop the summit, the "Champion." Only now, with battle-fire cooled in your veins, do your wounds raise their voices in protest.
Nestor: You have shattered the decaying order with strength. And through strength, you shall reshape new rules.
Nestor: You shall wield Gladiators' valor on the righteous path. You shall allow no more fragile lives to tremble before death. You shall ensure that your homeland's tragedy will forever be undone...
Nestor: Yet... should these new rules, forged by might, lose their foundation, will they not fall? A cold whisper of unease coils in your chest...
Nestor: Well then, no time for pointless pondering now.
Nestor: From this day forward, your sword, your honor, your two lives, shall serve Septimont!

title: At the Summit of Septimont
content:
[Objective: (Fail)]
Exhaustion takes over. You have given everything, but still cannot defeat Arsinosa. She doesn't spare you another look before turning away. You fall at the center of the arena alone.
Unable to bear the bone-shattering pain, you fight and stagger, until, at last, you fall on your knees before Arsinosa.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content: Quest Objective: As the High Tide draws near, a lurking calamity stirs, with its gaze fixed upon the borders of Septimont. Ephor Augusta invites you to the Sanguis Plateaus for a fateful hunt, the one that may decide the realm's survival...

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Return to the Leonidas Hotel]
Abby: Woo-wee. Sure is a beautiful day.
Abby: So any news from the Ephor, Rover? Or are we still chillin' like we've been for the past few days?
Ephor's Palace Attendant: Good day, Sir Rover.
Ephor's Palace Attendant: I am Damian, an attendant in service to the Ephor's Palace. By direct command, I have come to deliver you Her Excellency's personal letter.
Ephor's Palace Attendant: It concerns a matter of utmost importance.
[Dialogue Option]  (Take the letter.)
Abby: Me and my big mouth...
Abby: Hey, what does it say? Scooch up a bit.
Rover: It says Augusta has taken care of everything on her end. She's ready to meet us at the Ephor's Palace as agreed.
Rover: It's most likely something to do with the .
Rover: We shouldn't keep the Ephor waiting... Time to go, Abby.
Abby: Aww. You mean now?
Abby: Well, I think I'll sit this one out and leave all the heavy stuff to you guys. Hehe.
Abby: Chat for as long as you like. Just gimme me a holler if you need me.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Head to the Ephor's Palace]
Rover: The Ephor's Palace is just ahead.
Rover: Looks like Augusta's already taken care of everything... Let's do this.

Ephor's Palace An ancient marvel built by master artisans, the Ephor's Palace stands solemnly as a silent witness to the shifts of Septimont through the ages. As the administrative center of Septimont, it upholds the city's order and cohesion. Here, Septimont's leaders convene daily with the Ephor to chart the course of the land's future.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: (cutscene end)]
Augusta: Impressive!
Augusta: I expected a challenge, but your performance far exceeds what I had imagined.
Augusta: Just as I thought, watching from the Colosseum's balcony is no way to understand a warrior's true spirit.
Augusta: Only by crossing blades can I feel the will to fight pulsing through your veins.
Augusta: Come. Step closer.
Augusta: Laureate of Ragunna. Champion of Septimont. Favored Gladiator of Arsinosa (Lioness of Glory)—by the honor of these titles, it is only right you stand by my side.
Augusta: I, Augusta, Ephor of Septimont, offer you my highest esteem.
[Dialogue Option]  You've got a unique way of greeting guests.
Augusta: Hehe. Simple and efficient, no need for pleasantries. Here, we let our blades do the talking. The Septimont way.
Augusta: I have no doubt that you and I will have plenty of opportunities to get acquainted. But that's not why I called you here today...
Augusta: On my behalf, and that of the Ephor's Palace, I extend my deepest apologies for failing to keep our appointment.
Augusta: I hope this delay hasn't dampened your enthusiasm for the hunt.
[Dialogue Option]  It was urgent. No need to apologize.
[Dialogue Option]  Your hospitality very much made up for it.
Augusta: Haha. Tolerant and strong. Just as I've heard. Virtues of a true hero.
Augusta: Well, then. Seeing that your interest still holds. Shall we discuss it?
[Dialogue Option]  Please.
Augusta: The hunt—in Septimont's long fight for survival, it holds profound significance...
Augusta: It is both honor and duty. For a hundred years, countless Gladiators have taken up the hunt and met their end in glory.
Augusta: It's no exaggeration to say that the blood of Gladiators still burns in every inch of the crimson Sanguis Plateaus.
Augusta: Our ancestors built the defenses that line those grounds. To this day, they stand as the frontline of Septimont's resistance against the Dark Tide.
Augusta: You've surely noticed the lingering Blightcloud that hovers over the Sanguis Plateaus. Since the first Dark Tide outbreak in Rinascita, that place has become a breeding ground for its .
Augusta: As you've no doubt realized, our prey are Tacet Discords born from the Dark Tide. Only those who desecrate Septimont fall beneath the Gladiators' blades.
Augusta: The High Tide is upon us... and it will be a storm like no other.
Augusta: My hunting party requires unstoppable warriors. Sacrifices are inevitable, but I believe you will be a banner that stands unbroken, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  There are plenty of great Gladiators in Septimont...
[Dialogue Option]  What made you want to invite me on this hunt?
Augusta: I share your sentiment. Septimont takes pride in its many remarkable Gladiators. But you, you are exceptional.
Augusta: A grand hunt awaits us, and my warriors and I long to do battle alongside a fighter such as yourself.
Augusta: Of course, the will of the extraordinary deserves to be heard.
Augusta: I'd like to know your thoughts on the matter, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  I agree to join your hunt, but I have my own goal to accomplish.
Augusta: A straightforward answer. I like it.
Augusta: As for this "goal" of yours...
[Dialogue Option]  (Share what you've learned about the Sentinel's Relic and the Journeying Paradise.)
Augusta: Ah, yes, the Journeying Paradise. I've heard that laughable name before. A pity the hunt was made to shatter that little fantasy.
Augusta: As for the Sentinel's Relic...
Augusta: Go to the . It's where the Sentinel Imperator first descended upon the Sanguis Plateaus and is the "epicenter" of every hunt to this day.
Augusta: However, due to its significance, not even Septimont's highest officials are permitted near it.
Augusta: But if that is what you wish... say no more. I will make it happen.
[Dialogue Option]  You have great trust in me.
Augusta: The trust I place in you stems from your recognition of my character. I admire your honesty, and I will honor it to the fullest.
Augusta: Only those bound by trust can go the distance together.
Augusta: I look forward to the hunt ahead. It honors me to journey by your side.
[Dialogue Option]  When do we leave?
Augusta: Patience, my friend, is the first step to becoming a hunter.
Augusta: When the storm rages in the skies southeast of Septimont, I will await you at .

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Augusta]
Augusta: No need to worry. The Ephor's Palace will still cover your expenses in Septimont.
Augusta: Enjoy the peace while it lasts.
Augusta: The storm is coming... and our wait will not be long.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Goffredo]
Goffredo My little boy will be joining the hunt this time. One of the youngest gladiators in the ranks!
Goffredo Haha, I remember Avidius started just as young!
Goffredo They all say Avidius is the next Hero of Heroes. That's only because no one's seen my boy Fredrico fight!
Goffredo Hey, I know you... aren't you the Champion of the Great Agon. Will you be in the hunt?
[Dialogue Option]  I will.
Goffredo This hunt is really shaping up to be a big one! All the better. Fredrico needs a chance like this to prove himself.
[Dialogue Option]  Haven't decided yet.
Goffredo Really? Well, even if he goes up against the Champion, I believe Fredrico will still leave his mark.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Nerio]
Nerio Hunting and gladiating share the same root. But over time, they've grown into different paths.
Nerio Tell me, Champion, which do you prefer: hunting or gladiating?
[Dialogue Option]  Hunting.
Nerio I see. A hunt on the Plateaus tests not just strength, but courage and calrity of mind.
[Dialogue Option]  Gladiating.
Nerio Gladiating is a symbol of glory and of civilization itself. It brought prosperity to Septimont and became a cultural emblem we hold dear.
Nerio Whether it's hunting or gladiating, both are pillars of Septimont's traditions.
Nerio Gladiating is grueling, but it offers Gladiators a path to honor and fame. Hunting, by contrast, is rooted in duty.
Nerio If the Sanguis Plateaus were to fall, the Blightcloud would sweep in, unstoppable. It would devour all of Septimont in an instant, and the City of Glory would be lost to history.
Nerio That's why we train every day to prevent such a tragedy. With the Ephor leading us, I believe we stand ready. No calamity can shake us when we fight to protect our people.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Drusso]
Drusso An honor to talk to you, Champion of the Great Agon.
Drusso I watched the Final where you and Lupa fought side by side. That was a remarkable victory.
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you.
Drusso No need for modesty. Your strength as already proven itself.
[Dialogue Option]  The credit goes to Lupa.
Drusso Contender Lupa is a force to be recokoned with, but your prowess is unquestionable as well.
Drusso Speaking of which, I hear you're accompanying Her Excellency to the Sanguis Plateaus for the hunt?
Drusso Forgive my candor, but hunting and gladiating are not cut from the same cloth. A champion in the arena isn't necessarily a skilled hunter.
Drusso Agons are battles between people. But hunting? Hunting is a harsh contest of survival between humans and the Dark Tide creatures.
Drusso Those creatures are wilder and more vicious than any Gladiator. If you're truly set on joining the hunt, make sure you're well prepared.
Drusso May applause greet you. I'll be here, awaiting the triumphant return of you and Her Excellency.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Lumiel]
Lumiel May applause greet you, Champion. I'm a devoted admirer of yours, and it's an honor to finally meet you.
Lumiel I take it you've come to the Ephor's Palace to speak with her Excellency about the hunt?
[Dialogue Option]  How did you know that?
Lumiel It wasn't hard to guess. The nobility greatly admires what you've accomplished so far. We believe you'll help us usher in a new era for Septimont.
[Dialogue Option]  Nah, you're wrong.
Lumiel Hehe, very well then, I'll take your word for it.
Lumiel If I may offer a word of advice as a noble, don't grow too close to the Ephor. Best to keep a healthy distance.
Lumiel It's true that Ephor Augusta has had her share of accomplishments... but many still doubt her ability to lead all of Septimont.
Lumiel There are people who are more suitable for her position. Frankly speaking, many among the nobility see her merely as a seat warmer until the true Hero of Heroes appears.
Lumiel I don't entirely share their views, but as a noble myself... there's only so much I can say or do.
Lumiel Still, I do hope she proves them wrong and manages to change the old fools' minds in the Senate.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
subsection: Leave the Ephor's Palace and wait for the hunt
content:
[Objective: Leave the Ephor's Palace and wait for the hunt]
You accept Augusta's offer and stay in Septimont City with Abby, waiting for the looming storm. A few days later, out beyond the city walls...
Abby: Hic. I can't eat another bite... Hehe. That's another full stomach for Abby.
Abby: Huh? Hey, Rover. Look! Over there!
Rover: That's... a storm...
Rover: Which means it's about time to meet up with Augusta.
Rover: Tempest Cliffs. I remember that's where she told us to go.
Abby: Uh... Well... You better hurry!
Abby: Same as always, call me when you need me and I'll be out in a flash!

metadata.subsection: Leave the Ephor's Palace and wait for the hunt

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Head to Tempest Cliffs]
Rover: This... should be the right way...
???: If you're heading for Tempest Cliffs, head east. This path will take you straight to the courtyard of glory.
???: Or perhaps, would you care to travel with me?
???: After all, we share the same destination. Your reputation precedes you, honorable Rover.
Avidius: I am Gladiator Avidius. At your service.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you also here for the hunt?
Avidius: "Gladiating" and "hunting" are the very pillars upon which the glory of Septimont stands. I believe no Gladiator would refuse such an honor if invited.
Avidius: I, of course, am no exception.
Avidius: Please, if you'll follow me. Honored guest from afar.

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: Talk to Leonora]
Mars: Don't worry about me, Leonora. Augusta commands this hunt, and Avidius rides with us. Victory is assured.
Leonora: Still, this is your first time joining a hunt like this…
Mars: No Gladiator would deny themselves such an honor. We've trained all these years for this moment, haven't we?
Leonora: I wish I'd been chosen to go with you…
Mars: It'll be fine, Leonora. Bless me with your heart, and you'll be with me wherever I go.
Leonora: I'll wait for you right here till you return.
Leonora: Mars…

title: By Sun's Burning Hand
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Leonora again)]
Leonora: Forget the honor, just come back to me safe.
[Dialogue Option]  Trust him.
Leonora: This is all I can do now.
Leonora: You'll be out there with them, right?
Leonora: I'll be hoping for your safe return too.
