title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Head to Honami City)]
The Aetherfin shows you a holographic reconstruction of the event that occurred here—
You see a girl looking off into the distance, her eyes lost in the blue sky. What could she be thinking?

Peaceful Neighborhood
Never in memory has Honami been this quiet... Chisa, where are you?

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Peaceful Neighborhood
Never in memory has Honami been this quiet... Chisa, where are you?



Chisa: Rover, what are you doing here? Are you... looking for me?
[Dialogue Option]  There you are.
[Dialogue Option]  Well, someone left her sick bed, so I came to check on her.
Chisa: I'm sorry for not staying at the Black Shores and resting as I should.
[Dialogue Option]  What made you decide to come back?
Chisa: I'm in stable shape, and the Black Shores approved my temporary travel.
Chisa: But these are just conditions that made this possible. As for the true reason...
Chisa: I wanted to see what's become of Honami... since the loop ended.
Chisa: Strolling through the streets, I realize that this is my first time seeing the city as a tourist, despite being trapped here for months.
Chisa: No more worrying when the next Lament will come. No more desperate reach for Neon Tower. Now, I can simply wander around. No burdens.
Chisa: The Lament left scars. They won't fade. But what was once frozen in time... seems to be moving again.
Rover: This is the new future that we and everyone who once lived here forged together.
Chisa: A new... future, you say?
Chisa: By the way, I asked the Black Shores to help me verify the academy I once attended and dig into my records.
Chisa: They didn't reach the school directly, but... I found out something. I was in Honami for around two months. Outside, over twenty years have passed.
Chisa: Kuchiba Chisa... was a first-year student at  over twenty years ago.
[Dialogue Option]  ...Over twenty years ago?
Chisa: Yes. I had a feeling this would be the case when Sumika mentioned her findings, but I didn't expect such a huge time difference.
Chisa: The nice orientation ceremony... still feels recent. But my classmates I met have long since graduated.
Chisa: When I tried to contact my parents back home, I realized there was no way for me to reach them at all.
Chisa: Where are they? What have they been doing? How will they react if they find out that their daughter is still alive... I have no way of knowing.
Chisa: Now this place feels more like home than the world out there.
Rover: It just takes some time to get used to an unfamiliar enviornment.
Rover: Just ask the Black Shores to help you keep digging. With enough time, you're bound to find those connections again.
Chisa: Since you're here, would you walk with me? I'd like to see what Honami looks like now... together.
Rover: Any particular places you have in mind?
Chisa: I haven't come up with an exact plan yet. Specific routes, time of travel, rest locations... None.
Chisa: Just as I thought. I'm not my usual self today.
Rover: Hey, it's just a "weekend getaway." No plans needed. Just get up and go.
Chisa: If you put it that way...
Chisa: How about the lake surrounded by cherry blossoms?

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Take a stroll with Chisa)]
Chisa: I've never mentioned it before, but the buildings and infrastructure here... they remind me of the neighborhood I grew up in.
Rover: Brings back old memories?
Chisa: Yes. Even just walking around here brings back memories.
Chisa: That vending machine looks like it's still working.
Chisa: I'll buy you some juices as a thank you for the hassle you went through to find me.

Chisa: I think it got stuck inside...
[Dialogue Option]  Try and go for another one, maybe?
Chisa: I've got a better way to handle no-good vending machines like this.
[Dialogue Option]  I've seen this before. Just whack it a few times.
Chisa: Yep. You've read my mind.
[Dialogue Option]  Do something with your invincible scissors, Chisa.
Chisa: That may be a little too much. Here, watch this.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Do something with your invincible scissors, Chisa.
Chisa: That may be a little too much. Here, watch this.



Chisa: Here you go. Simplicity works best.
Chisa: ...Is something wrong.
[Dialogue Option]  Didn't have time for this kind of thing before.
Chisa: You're right. We were always running from something. Or chasing after something.
[Dialogue Option]  Just wondering if it's past its expiration date.
Chisa: Remember that canned fruit we had that one night? It's the same thing. I've never got an upset stomach from it, at least.
Chisa: Before I transfered to Startorch, I used to hide next to the vending machines behind my high school building all the time.
Chisa: No one else really went there. It was quiet. The sound of soda cans dropping down would make me feel relaxed.
[Dialogue Option]  Was life difficult back then?
[Dialogue Option]  Was it because you're a Resonator?
Chisa: Where I come from, discrimination and prejudice against Resonators are part of life. School was no exception.
Chisa: The gossip, the looks, the way people kept their distance... intentional or not, it still got to me.
Chisa: I tried to stand up for myself. I tried holding it in. Nothing changed. Just when I was close to breaking, I received an acceptance letter.
Chisa: And so, with my family's blessing, I left home and went to Startorch Academy, far away in the Lahai-Roi region.
Rover: Startorch Academy... What was it like?
Chisa: So it's true, you... No, it's nothing.
Chisa: It is a multinational school built specifically for Resonators. A metropolis of science and research.
Chisa: Even for a girl who couldn't face her own problems and chose to run away, they accepted me with a warm welcome. I met people who dreamed of reaching the stars.
Chisa: This swing... It's just like the one back home.
Chisa: Would you join me? There is room for one more.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Chisa: This swing... It's just like the one back home.
Chisa: Would you join me? There is room for one more.



Chisa: ...
[Dialogue Option]  Chisa?
[Dialogue Option]  Solaris to Chisa.
Chisa: I hear you. I'm just... enjoying the gentle sway. Especially... when someone's beside me.
Chisa: Everything feels so peacefull all of a sudden.
Chisa: When you're ready to move on, I'll get up.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Stay on swing for a while)]
Chisa: You don't have to wait for me. I think I've been on the swing long enough.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Go back on the swing)]
Chisa: Oh, you're back. Do you like sitting on the swing too?

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
subsection: (Move forward and get off the swing)
content:
[Objective: (Move forward and get off the swing)]
Chisa: I can already see our destination from here. Look at the cherry blossoms... they weren't blooming like this before.
[Dialogue Option]  They really are beautiful now.
Chisa: Like clouds floating above the water or like cotton poking through a torn couch... Sorry, I'm using weird analogies again.
[Dialogue Option]  They're the same as they were before.
Chisa: It could be that my mood is just different now than before.
Chisa: Luckily, a view like this can exist forever within this Sonoro Sphere.

Chisa: That fountain over there... it's been concealed by leftover Irideglow Crystals. Kind of a shame.
Rover: I'll take care of it. Just like back in Neon Tower.

metadata.subsection: (Move forward and get off the swing)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
subsection: (Restore the fountain frozen in Irideglow Crystal)
content:
[Objective: (Restore the fountain frozen in Irideglow Crystal)]
Chisa: There's something in the water...
Rover: Let's fish it out and see what it is.
Rover: This looks like a cassette tape.
Chisa: Ah, I know what it is.
Chisa:  Every Startorch Academy student has a frequency storage cassette like this inside their Terminals.
Rover: (I remember now. Galbrena once told me about them.)
Chisa: I also have one in my Terminal. They were given out during the orientation.
Rover: If it's a device unique to Lahai-Roi, what's it doing here?
Chisa: Random "castaways" often appear inside the Honami Sonoro Sphere. This must be one of those.
Chisa: I'll take this to Namipon. It should be able to help us find where it came from.
Chisa: Cherry blossoms.... Right in front of us. It's so beautiful.
[Dialogue Option]  Let's go over there and take a picture.
[Dialogue Option]  This right here is a photo moment.
Chisa: Sure. You and I together.

metadata.subsection: (Restore the fountain frozen in Irideglow Crystal)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Follow Chisa)]
Rover: Make sure you look towards the camera.
Chisa: I will.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Take a photo with Chisa)]
Chisa: When I was little, my parents once took me to a park full of cherry blossoms for a picnic. I made kirigami in all kinds of shapes and had them guess what they were.
Chisa: The kirigami didn't really look like anything, but when I told them, they'd always smile and pretend they understood.
Chisa: Those cherry blossoms... they looked just like they do now. After being away from home for so long, drifting around... I feel like I'm home again.
[Dialogue Option]  Welcome home, Chisa.
Chisa: Thank you, .
Chisa: They told me about you at the Black Shores. They you've lost some memories.
Chisa: This student ID card came into my possession by chance. It was in that Tower that I found—No, that I recognized who it belonged to.
Chisa: I never found the right moment to return this to you. Here, this belongs to you.
[Dialogue Option]  I was a student at Startorch Academy?
Chisa: We never met in person at school, but... I did read the course selection guide you wrote.
[Dialogue Option]  I don't remember anything.
Chisa: It's okay. Honami is where we first met each other.
Chisa: But I've been talking about myself this whole time. Why don't you tell me about your story so far? I'd like to know more about you.
Chisa: Rinascita... sounds like quite an adventure. Only someone like you, Senpai, could accomplish so much.
[Dialogue Option]  You can stop calling me that for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Hold on, that title takes a little getting used to.
Chisa: Alright. You always seem to find your way forward, no matter how uncertain things are. Like you did in Honami. But I...
Chisa: What comes next? Should I continue my studies at the Academy? Should I go home? Or should I do something else... I still haven't decided.
Rover: No need to rush your decision. You can take your time and stick around here for a while.
Rover: At least, you won't have to face the future alone anymore.
Chisa: You're right. We're partners.
Chisa: I received a precius gift while traveling with you—the courage to face reality and move on.
Chisa: There's something else I want to give you besides the ID card, Rover.
Chisa: I was out of inspiration towards the end, but finally managed to finish it after comimg back to Honami and getting some ideas.
[Dialogue Option]  So this is what you were working on during recovery.
Chisa: Yes. It's a pretty tricky piece, so I ended up using a lot of paper. Looks very much like Honami, don't you think?
Chisa: My hometown was built next to the Tacet Field created by Honami's fall. Even though the Lament still haunts us, some stubborn souls have rebuilt that familiar Tower again.
Chisa: We still reach for the sky. Still hope radio waves break through the blockade to connect the isolated regions left behind...
Chisa: The painful memories of home will never fade. But I won't turn away from the beautiful ones, either. Together... they are what make me Kuchiba Chisa.
Chisa: This is my thank-you gift to you. Something precious to me... A memory of my home.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll hold on to it.
Chisa: I just remembered... Namipon always said the cafe needed more life. Maybe now is the time to try?
Chisa: Like you said, I have time to "stick around" for a while. So would it be alright if I invite your friends from Black Shores here for a party?
Chisa: Before I make any decisions on what to do next, I want Shashou Cafe to celebrate a real "opening day."
Pink petals swirl upon the wind like drifting thoughts, gently filling the space between hearts.
Why not stay a little longer, in this long season, along the streets we once walked, here in Honami...

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Why not stay a little longer, in this long season, along the streets we once walked, here in Honami...



Chisa: So, do you want to hang around a bit longer, or shall we head back? I'll follow your lead.
[Dialogue Option]  There's something I want to ask.
Chisa: Is there something else you'd like to know? We've got plenty of time.
[Dialogue Option]  About your Overclocking symptoms...
Chisa: Are you worried about me? I'm feeling all right for the time being.
[Dialogue Option]  Not pretending to be okay, right?
Chisa: Not when I'm with you. The people at the Black Shores called it a miracle. That someone who was on the verge of Overclocking for so long could recover. But...
Chisa: When we passed through Honami's rift, I felt a warm frequency flowing towards me. I suspect that's what helped stabilize my Resonance energy.
[Dialogue Option]  Was it...
Chisa: It was the person who brought you to Honami... In the end, the same person pulled me back from the edge. Again.
[Dialogue Option]  About when I was a student at Startorch Academy...
Chisa: I'm sorry. I was only a first-year student in Engineering. I hadn't been around long enough. Everything I heard about you came from what others said.
Chisa: All I really heard was that you were popular. Always had friends around. If I hadn't been caught in the Honami incident, we probably wouldn't never met.
[Dialogue Option]  About that cassette tape...
Chisa: The ones from Startorch aren't the average cassettes that you normally see. They are specialized equipment used to store frequencies.
Chisa: One of the instructors described it as a frequency backup storage for the holder. It records the person's very "existence."
[Dialogue Option]  Why make backups of frequencies?
Chisa: It's one of the Acadeny's safety precautions against the . That is all that I know.
[Dialogue Option]  That's it for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Let's go for another walk.
[Dialogue Option]  It's getting late. Let's head back to the cafe.
Chisa: Come on, then. We should spruce the place up a bit to give our friends a warm welcome.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Chisa: Come on, then. We should spruce the place up a bit to give our friends a warm welcome.



Outside Shashou Cafe
A day later

Abby: Come to think of it, this is the first time I'm here at this cafe while wide awake.
Rover: You sure it's not because you've been putting in more nap hours lately?
Abby: Says who? I got locked out by the Sonoro Sphere right before the start, remember? I couldn't even get to you. And don't get me started on all the wacky frequencies that I got mixed in with...
Rover: You did a great job. Welcome to Shashou Cafe, Abby.
Abby: ...Whoa, why the formality all of a sudden? Ahem. So you asked Shorekeeper to invite the Black Shores gang over for a party. They should be here pretty soon, right?
Rover: Yep. Let's go check on Chisa and see how the decorating is going.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Enter the redecorated cafe)]
Abby: Gotta hand it to ya, I love what you guys did with place. Feels like a mini festival in here!
Chisa: Oh, you're here. Namipon and I are just making finishing touches to the party.
Chisa: Welcome aboard, Abby.
Abby: Well, hello there, Chisa. It's nice to see you again. You're all so kind, you know. Say, whatcha got on the menu—
Namipon: In the cozy cafe, vibrant lights dance on the walls. Soft chimes whisper. Glad to have you aboard again, Passenger.
Namipon: Chisa's the Acting Manager today, and she'll be our host for the opening party.
Abby: Wait a minute... Something smells funny about this guy!
Abby: This frequency isn't Echo or TD. Feels like it's hiding a whole mixed bag in its fuzzy tummy!
[Dialogue Option]  It's the cafe's mascot.
[Dialogue Option]  It's the guardian of Honami City.
Abby: You say that, but I don't trust it. Hey, ain't there a whole lot more of you around here too?
Namipon: Would you like to join us in putting up the decorations, Passenger?
[Dialogue Option]  Gladly.
[Dialogue Option]  Love to help.
Abby: And it's completely ignoring me! Now it even chats up Rover like they're old buddies or something...
Namipon: Ah, the place is starting to turn into a party now.
Chisa: Is something wrong with your friend?
[Dialogue Option]  No idea.
[Dialogue Option]  Abby's just a little excited today, that's all.
Chisa: After being an emergency shelter for so long, it's finally starting to become what it was supposed to be.
Chisa: I'll let you finish these last few decorations, Rover.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Chisa: I'll let you finish these last few decorations, Rover.



(Obtained: Menu Board and Cherry Blossom)
This appears to be a gallery set up by Chisa. It displays scenes from around Honami, and pictures she took with people she holds dear...

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Chisa)]
Chisa: Maintain eye contact... Smile... Greet everyone as they come in...
[Dialogue Option]  Feeling a bit nervous?
Chisa: A little bit. I'm... I'm just reviewing the basics of greeting guests.
[Dialogue Option]  Hello, Acting Manager. You there?
Chisa: I'm listening. I'm just reviewing the basics of greetings and guests.
Chisa: Shashou Cafe is like "home" to me in Honami. Honestly, i-it's been a long time since I hosted anyone at home.
Chisa: I think the last time was... sometime in high school.
[Dialogue Option]  You greeted me just fine.
[Dialogue Option]  Just greet everyone like you'd greet me.
Chisa: To me, you're different from everyone else.
[Dialogue Option]  Different?
Chisa: I-I didn't give it much thought at the time. Anyone... I need to pull myself together. A manager must stay composed.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Abby)]
[Dialogue Option]  Still grumpy about earlier?
Abby: As if! I told you, there's something off about that furball. It's like the frequencies of people emotions all got balled up together like a... like a wad of bubble gum.
Abby: But then again... I didn't pick up anything bad from it though.
[Dialogue Option]  Be nice to the mascot, Abby.
[Dialogue Option]  You'll get along just fine.
Abby: A-Alright, alright, if you say so. I guess a chat wouldn't hurt.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Investigate Amber)]
You see a glistening piece of amber on the bar counter. It reminds you of someone you once met.
Namipon: Ah, this was left here by Passenger 3.
[Dialogue Option]  Passenger 3?
Namipon: Passenger 1 is Chisa. You're Passenger 2. As for Passenger 3... Ahem...
Namipon: Passenger 3 is the relentless seeker of truth. She never game up her quest.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Listen to Radio)]
Radio: *Light, upbeat melody*
Radio: Good afternoon, Honami. You're tuned in to your city radio, broadcasting live on a warm summer breeze.
Radio: As the temps slowly climb, looks like that midsummer heat is comin' in hot. But don't sweat it. Up next, we've got a special announcement.
Radio: Our meteor trackers are lighting up. Looks like a shower is set to dazzle just after midnight tonight. For anyone up for a little stargazing, grab your friends and family to catch this "Midnight Summer Magic Show."
Radio: Coming up next, here's a list of the best viewing spots across the city...
Rover: (So the seasons in Honami that stood still are flowing again...)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Help decorate the cafe)]
Namipon: Passenger, Chisa was the one who proposed the party. She has put lots of effort into preparations.
Namipon: For this, I'd like to prepare a surprise—a special ornament just for her. Any recommendations?
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe something related to her?
Namipon: Agreed. It must be something that would let all the Passengers know Chisa is the manager of the day at first glance.
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe something that she likes?
Namipon: Ah, yes. It must be something that Chisa would fall in love with immediately.
And just like that, after a little tinkering here and some cuts there, Namipon hands you the ornament it just finished...
(Obtained: Mysterious Standee)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Place Namipon's mysterious decoration)]
Chisa: ...
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Chisa: What's... this?
Namipon: Oh, it's a standee of the cafe's manager. I made it with the lingering frequencies around.
Chisa: Rover, do you like... No, what do you think of it?
[Dialogue Option]  As stylish as the original.
Chisa: You even included my weapon... Let's leave it here then.
[Dialogue Option]  As cute as the original.
Chisa: Did you say... c-cute? Um, I guess just leave it like this, then.
[Dialogue Option]  Fits in perfectly with everything around it.
Chisa: If you think it fits, then... alright.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Namipon if you're ready)]
Namipon: Thank you for lending us a hand with decorations, Passenger. I'm sure the others will be very pleased.
[Dialogue Option]  (Wait  for your friends to arrive.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Have a look around the cafe.)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Dialogue Option]  (Wait  for your friends to arrive.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Have a look around the cafe.)



Shorekeeper: Rover, Chisa. I have arrived as scheduled.
Shorekeeper: I see you're all waiting here. Could I be mistaken about the time?
Chisa: No, not at all. We're glad you made it, Shorekeeper. Shasho Cafe welcomes you aboard!
Shorekeeper: I see.
Chisa: Mmm...
Namipon: Oh, say something, Passenger. This awkward silence is killing me...
Rover: Sounds like you two already met at the Black Shores.
Chisa: Yes. Shorekeeper personally oversaw all of the routine checkups during my recovery. She was very helpful.
Shorekeeper: Chisa remained on the verge of Overclocking for a prolonged period within a distorted temporal flow. Her case required a full evaluation by the Tethys System.
Namipon: Now it's suddenly turned into a conversation about work...
Buling: Hi, Boss! Heard you bought the whole place out?
[Dialogue Option]  She's the manager.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm just a customer like you are.
Buling: Very good lah! My reading for you said visitors from all around, wealthy coming in thick and fast. Super lucky day for an opening!
Chisa: You must be Buling?
Chisa: I've heard about you from Rover. You're the one who helped pinpoint Honami's rift. Thank you.
Buling: It's no biggie. Me and Boss, we go way back. Just treat me to good meal and we're even.
Buling: Good to meet you, Chisa. And this floating one here... Hmm...
Namipon: I'm the cafe's mascot. Call me Namipon.
Buling: Hello, Namipon. You show the way? Been walking until my legs go jelly. Need to sit and rest a while.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Buling: Hello, Namipon. You show the way? Been walking until my legs go jelly. Need to sit and rest a while.



Shorekeeper: ...
[Dialogue Option]  What's the matter?
[Dialogue Option]  Are the others on their way?
Shorekeeper: From the guest list you provided, only Encore, Buling, and myself were free to come. The others are either away or currently on assignment.
Shorekeeper: Encore... She locked herself in her room and insisted on finishing Tethy's assigned homework.
[Dialogue Option]  I can't imagine how much homework that must be...
Shorekeeper: Apologies. I didn't expect her to suddeny become so... competitive. It's a first, truly.
[Dialogue Option]  Tell her it's time for another holiday.
Shorekeeper: That I tried. Encore kept insisting she finish it, even remarking, "Your time has come, big bad homework!"
Rover: Yeah, that's Encore alright...
Chisa: Is Encore that little girl with pink hair? I helped her with some math problems over at the Haven of Sprouts once.
Chisa: She's a quick learner. She understood all the formulas I taught her in no time.
[Dialogue Option]  So you were Encore's new tutor.
[Dialogue Option]  That explains why she's picking fight with Tethys.
Chisa: There's still time before the party begins. Why don't we go inside and have a seat?

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
subsection: (Talk to everyone before the party begins)
content:
[Objective: (Talk to everyone before the party begins)]
Chisa: Would you like to start off with something to drink?
Shorekeeper: Anything would be fine, thank you.
Shorekeeper: Is that...?
Chisa: Oh... No need to mind that.
Shorekeeper: Very well. I shall follow the proper code of this cafe, and prevent eye contact with your standee.
Chisa: Wait, I... I didn't mean that.

metadata.subsection: (Talk to everyone before the party begins)

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Buling)]
[Dialogue Option]  Why not take a seat?
Buling: It's okay, I'm just admiring the feng shui. Mmm, bright and open, good for drawing in fortune. Hard to find one so lucky.
[Dialogue Option]  There's no safer place in all of Honami.
Buling: Speaking of Honami... I actually came to see if any special Reverberations were hiding in the city ruins.
Buling: But after coming here... It's really quiet. You won't find another place like this in the outside world.
[Dialogue Option]  Is that good or bad?
Buling: A good thing, of course.
Buling: It means that lots of "people" here let go of whatever they were holding onto. Just poof, all gone!
Buling: ...Oh yeah, the coffee beans haven't been changed in ages, right? Next time I'll bring some of my favorite blends for you to try.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Abby)]
Abby: Nom-nom-nom. Ya know, it must be really rough for you. Having your  frequency get split into pieces like that, and then clearing your head of all the clicking and buzzing.
Namipon: That's all in the past now. How's the Rice Dango?
Abby: Not bad, actually. Soft and chewy. Well... I guess I shouldn't have judged a Namipon by its smell.
Abby: Plus, you've been a big help to Rover these past few days. I'll come give you a hand after I'm done with this Dango.
Namipon: That's lovely! We'll take all the help we can get.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Little Namipons)]
Little Namipons: We... doing food prep for the party... Huge cake for opening... Keep up the good work... Yay...
[Dialogue Option]  Where did all this food come from?
Little Namipons: Big-pon helped gather them... All local pure Remnants... 100% natural... Additive free...

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Shorekeeper)]
Chisa: Here you go. I hope it's to your liking.
Shorekeeper: Thank you.
Shorekeeper: It's... a bit bitter. But nothing I can't bear.
[Dialogue Option]  Sounds like it needs more sugar.
Shorekeeper: It's all right. I rather think of it as a novelty.
[Dialogue Option]  How does it compare to the strong tea you had before?
Shorekeeper: I have to say that the tea was much more bitter.
Shorekeeper: Now then... Rover, Chisa. The Black Shores has conducted another investigation on Startorch Academy, the school that you both once attended.
Shorekeeper: As of now, we can confirm that the Academy, along with the entire region of Lahai-Roi, has been completely isolated from the rest of the world by the .
[Dialogue Option]  The Void Storm?
Shorekeeper: A Waveworn Phenomenon unique to Lahai-Roi. When it's active, any form of communication is blocked.
Chisa: So you're saying... right now there's no way for us to reach the Academy?
Shorekeeper nods.
Camellya: Oh, you're all here. How come I wasn't invited to the party?
[Dialogue Option]  I thought you couldn't make it?
Camellya: Don't be silly. Seeing you is always my No. 1 priority.
Shorekeeper: Cammellya, shouldn't you be on a mission?
Camellya: Got it done early. And I wouldn't finished it even sooner if someone had told me a city popped up off the coast of the Black Shores.
Camellya: So... you must be Chisa?
Chisa: ...Hello.
Camellya: I saw the report on Honami. Oh, it's such a shame I wasn't there for the excitement.
Camellya: You wouldn't mind having an extra girl at your party, would you? I'd like to make up for all the fun I missed.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
subsection: (Talk to everyone before the party begins)
content:
[Objective: (Talk to everyone before the party begins)]
Camellya: A city doomed to be  destroyed again and again. Irideglow that triggers Overclocking, and TDs tearing through the streets...
Camellya: But never mind that. You're here. I'm here. The two of us can dance... doesn't that sound a lot more fun?
Camellya: Oh, Rover. If I got pulled in too, how much more fun would that have been!
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Camellya: I'll take it as a yes, then.
[Dialogue Option]  Don't get ahead of yourself. The crisis is over.
Camellya: Fine, if you say so. I'll take those extra performances off the table, then.
Camellya: Anyway, pushing through the pain of Overclocking and mastering the shiver of death clawing at your spine... I spy with my little eye a promising seed.
Camellya: Interested in trying a little "germination test," Chisa? A little eval I host, just for the brave.
Chisa: Eval as in...?
Camellya: Defeat me, or be defeated.
Chisa: Is this... some kind of tradition in the Black Shores?
Camellya: Relax, dearie. Don't get worked up just yet. Hehe, you can show me your dance moves once you're fully recovered.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Listen to the radio while waiting)]
Radio: *Light, upbeat melody*
Radio: ...We have a special guest with us today—
Radio: Well hello to all the lovely listeners of the Pioneer Podcast. It's your old pal, Aalto.
Radio: Glad to have you. Mr. Aalto, why don't you start us off with the Lilyland incident?
Radio: It all happened during the Troupe of Fools' big tour. Tickets were already pretty cheap, but scalpers hogged them all and were ripping off unsuspecting fans.
Radio: Now the first time they've done something like this, actually.
Radio: After Brant, the head of the Troupe, found out about it, he put on a disguise one night and snuck into their hideout. "Retrieved" all the tickets and bills as evidence right under their noses.
Radio: It was bye-bye scalpers! Brant offered free tickets to all the fans that came to watch their play. Such a happy ending.
Radio: Well it sounds awfully like Brant did most of the work, Mr. Aalto. So... So what exactly was your role in all of this?
Radio: Ah-ha-ha... Well, I supplied Brant with intel on the hideout, of course. I was undercover and it all happened right in front of me.
Rover: ...
Rover: (So this radio can receive signals from outside of Honami now?)

Namipon: You're awake, dear Passenger.
[Dialogue Option]  Did I... fall asleep?
Namipon: Yes, you did. Everyone had a fantastic time last night.
Namipon: After saying goodbye to your friends, you got tired and decided to take a rest in the cafe.
Rover: (I did...?)
Rover: (The only thing I remember is what happened right before watching the meteor shower.)
Namipon: What's the matter? Did you not sleep well?
[Dialogue Option]  Where's Chisa?
Namipon: Chisa...
Namipon: Hehe, Chisa woke up before you. She tiptoed out for some fresh air. Said she didn't want to bother you.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Find Chisa)]
Namipon: Anything you'd like to know, Passenger? I'm here to help anytime.
[Dialogue Option]  About last night's view...
Namipon: Mmm, it was the surprise "we" prepared, and Honami's way of answering everyone's wishes.
Namipon: The city is free from its sorrow. Time isn't stuck anymore. That was... a little epilogue after the "real ending." And a happy one.
[Dialogue Option]  About what happened after the party...
Namipon: Actually... we had a big meteorite scare. Their original trajectory would have wiped out the whole Crossing.
Namipon: But you and Chisa gathered everyone's strength and turned that big scary rock... into a sky full of stardust...
Namipon: Then you curled up here in the cafe and took a nice, long nap. Chisa woke up first and watched you sleeping for a while.
[Dialogue Option]  You sure that's what happened?
[Dialogue Option]  Wait a minute, are you making this up?
Namipon: Oops, guess you got me there. But that last part is true, though.
[Dialogue Option]  That's it for now.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Namipon: Oops, guess you got me there. But that last part is true, though.
[Dialogue Option]  That's it for now.



The wall is covered with pictures from Shashou Cafe's opening day—
Although the time you spent with your friends was short, every moment was captured forever. Now it feels clear and close enough to  see and touch.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Although the time you spent with your friends was short, every moment was captured forever. Now it feels clear and close enough to  see and touch.



Chisa: Good morning, Rover.
[Dialogue Option]  Good morning, Chisa.
Chisa: It feels like we're back to our adventuring days in Honami.
[Dialogue Option]  Can I get you something to drink, Passenger?
Chisa: I already had a cup of coffee this morning. And please stop trying to be Namipon.
Chisa: That was a perfect wrap for our opening party. It was a very special night.
Chisa: A fitting conclusion for everything that's happened over the past two months, a celebration for the cafe's opening, and... a commemoration for meeting new friends.
Chisa: Even if we were to say farewell now, I wouldn't have any regrets.
[Dialogue Option]  Farewell?
[Dialogue Option]  So you've made a decision?
Chisa: Yes. I have decided what I'll do next.
Chisa: I will return home first and find my parents. After that, Startorch Academy, to complete my studies.
Chisa: Neither will be easy, but I will overcome whatever stands in my way, just like... how we did together in that Tower.
Chisa: "Nothing can trap me... I'll find my way back."
Rover: That's right. Nothing can stop you.
Chisa: We'll be going our separate ways for a while. But I'm sure when this is all over, you and I will see each other again.
Chisa: No... when the time comes, I promise I'll come looking for you.
Chisa: Then again, I won't be leaving right away. The Black Shores still wants me back for a few health checkups.
Chisa: What do you say I join the Black Shores during this time just like Camellya suggested?
Chisa: That one was a joke. Now comes the real part.
Chisa: Thank you, Rover... Thank you for everything you've done for me.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Chisa: That one was a joke. Now comes the real part.
Chisa: Thank you, Rover... Thank you for everything you've done for me.



(Cutscene plays)
Abby: Whoa, why are your frequencies leaking all over the place?!
Abby: Grrr!
Rover: It's like... something's pulling them out...
Chisa: Is that...
Chisa: Startorch Academy?

content:
Abby: Grrr!
Rover: It's like... something's pulling them out...
Chisa: Is that...
Chisa: Startorch Academy?
(Cutscene ends)



Shorekeeper: Your frequency loss has been contained for now. How are you feeling?
[Dialogue Option]  Much better.
Shorekeeper: I'm glad to hear that. Your vitals are also within normal parameters now.
Abby: ugh, this part of you feels completely empty. Let me check that out for you.
[Dialogue Option]  Abby's out cold. I think I'm next.
Shorekeeper: How can that be...? The readings tell me your vitals are within normal parameters now.
Abby: Hey, I'm still wide awake ya know, just a little beat. And this part of you feels completely empty.
Chisa: ...
Shorekeeper: The connection between your frequency and the rift has been cut off. You are out of immediate danger.
[Dialogue Option]  Why did my frequency start to dissipate?
[Dialogue Option]  What was trying to siphon my frequency?
Shorekeeper: We are unable to confirm at this time. But frequency signatures identical to the Void Storm were detected in the rift's proximity.
Shorekeeper: The most likely scenario is that this rift is acting as a conduit between here and the Lahai-Roi region, which is also where your frequency was drawn to.
Rover: Lahai-Roi is where it all started. Guess we'll need to pay the place a visit to find out the actual cause.
Chisa: The Void Storm at Startorch was what brought me to Honami in the first place. Now it's the other way around.
Chisa: Do you suppose this rift can take us straight to Lahai-Roi?
Shorekeeper: ...
[Dialogue Option]  Is that a viable option?
Shorekeeper: Theoretically, yes. However, the frequencies inside the rift are highly unstable, and you are likely to lose your way without proper navigation.
Shorekeeper: I'm afraid now is not the appropriate time.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Investigate the area around the rift)]
Fabio: "Safety risk, moderate. Further surveillance is needed." That'll do as the report for Valentina for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Notice anything unusual?
Fabio: The rift seems to be in a stasis. No Tacet Discords popping out of it, at least.
Fabio: But I've recognized a few flashing images within the rift.
[Dialogue Option]  Is it Startorch Academy?
Fabio: Yes. Most information about that school is highly classified.
Fabio: I only know what I do because a friend of mine is an instructor there, but we've been out of touch for a long time.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Investigate the area around the rift)]
Maki: Phew, never thought I'd actually be here, standing in the post-apocalyptic city from the storybooks I read when I was a kid.
[Dialogue Option]  Hello?
Maki: Hi, there, Bloom Bearer. I've collected some frequency samples and am analyzing them now.
[Dialogue Option]  Got anything so far?
Maki: Yep. Aside from the Void Storm readings we got around the rift, we also found scattered foreign frequencies in the vicinity.
Maki: What might have happened is that frequencies from another region got "spat out" into Honami when the rift was formed.
[Dialogue Option]  Another region... as in Lahai-Roi?
Maki: That's right. We still need to verify their exact origins, but the general areas are pretty much narrowed down.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Maki: That's right. We still need to verify their exact origins, but the general areas are pretty much narrowed down.



Namipon: So this is where the radio went...
Platya: What's with all that noise it's making?
Platya: Oh, you're here. Look what I found.
Platya: Spotted it next to the rift. Here, listen to this—
Radio: This time... we... as our guest.
Platya: The thing's not even turned on, but it's been playing these choppy sounds non-stop.
Namipon: I see the problem here... Try adjusting its receiver, Passenger.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Adjust the radio)]
Namipon: If not mistaken, the sounds will become clearer once you've adjusted it to the right frequency.
Rover: (Let's give this a try then.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Adjust the knob clockwise)
Namipon: Hmm, that doesn't seem right. Try the other way.
Rover: (In that case...)
[Dialogue Option]  (Adjust the knob counter-clockwise)
Namipon: Oh, oh! There you go!
Radio: *Static*... Mrs. Kuchiba, would you mind sharing with us why you chose this particular design... *static*... of the Academy's new uniform?
Chisa: Huh?
Radio: The inspiration came from... well, my daughter. She once made a cutout of this pattern from some old fabric at home...
Radio: ...Very interesting... *static*... It really captures the Academy's spirit...
Radio: *Static*... If it's this uniform, I thought... my little Chisa would love to wear it...
Radio: *Loud whistle*
Radio: *Complete silence*
Namipon: Something's probably broken inside. I'll take a look.
Chisa: Namipon, was that a live signal from Lahai-Roi?
Namipon: Yes, it was. That cassette we put inside lets it receive radio signals from the rift.
Namipon: With the right tweak, maybe I can track it. Like I did with Neon Tower's—
Chisa: It sounded like the Academy's radio talk show... But why did I hear my mother?
Chisa: Does that mean she's at Startorch? Why is she there? Is she... looking for me?
Namipon: Chisa?
Rover: (Chisa will need some time to process everything.)
Shorekeeper: I am detecting a unique frequency from this radio...
Namipon: It has formed a connection with Lahai-Roi on the other end of the rift.
Namipon: Once it's all fixed up, I can piggyback on this frequency and plot coordinates from there to Honami.
Shorekeeper: Understood. With established coordinates, you will be able to navigate your way within the rift.
Shorekeeper: The Black Shores will also assist with stabilizing the rift to ensure your safety as much as possible.
Shorekeeper: ...Should you decide to travel to Lahai-Roi. To Startorch Academy.
[Dialogue Option]  What do you know about Lahai-Roi
Shorekeeper: It is a region once forgotten, covered in snow most of the year and sparsely populated. No Sentinel is there to guide its civilization.
[Dialogue Option]  Lahai-Roi has been mentioned a lot in passing lately.
Shorekeeper: Beneath its ice fields lie Startorch Academy and numerous research facilities, built by a multinational alliance known as the Spacetrek Collective.
Shorekeeper: Startorch Academy enacts a strict access protocol for all personnel. I will have the necessary paperwork in place before your departure.
Chisa: Looks like I need to make changes to my plans...
Chisa: I want to go back to Startorch Academy.
Chisa: My family is there, and so are my instructors and classmates. The future may be uncertain, but I know what I have to do.
[Dialogue Option]  We'll find the missing frequencies.
[Dialogue Option]  We'll find out the truth.
[Dialogue Option]  We'll return to the Academy we attended.
Chisa: Now, we wait. And then...
Chisa: We get through this together.

content:
[Dialogue Option]  We'll return to the Academy we attended.

Chisa: We get through this together.



Radio: *Static noises*
Voice from the Silence: *Static*... The universe... has rejected us...
Voice from the Silence: ...Is this the answer you've been seeking, Rover?
Voice from the Silence: I hope to make you proud. I hope I haven't let you down...

(Quest complete: Flowing Starlight in the Iris)

Chisa: A voice from the radio? But isn't it broken?
[Dialogue Option]  I heard someone calling my name.
Chisa: You did? I'm right next to you, but... I didn't think I heard anything.
[Dialogue Option]  You sure you didn't hear anything strange?
Chisa: Yes. You must be exhausted. Should we go back to the cafe?
[Dialogue Option]  I guess I could use some rest.
[Dialogue Option]  No need. I'm fne.

Shorekeeper: No, to my ears the radio has been silent.
Shorekeeper: However, I was able to sense a peculiar frequency for a brief moment.

[Dialogue Option]  It'll be an investigation. We're not going to school.
Namipon: Okay, okay. When you get to Lahai-Roi, take care of each other, alright?
[Dialogue Option]  Are you really not coming with us?
[Dialogue Option]  That's a strange unit of measurement...
Namipon: It means I'm trying really hard.
Namipon: Nope. I'm a Namipon from Honami. This is where I stay.
Namipon: I'll look after the cafe while you're away. It'll always be here when you need to rest.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
[Objective: (Talk to Platya)]
Platya: I remember this Crossing. When I was little, my younger sister and I once snuck out to play in the shopping mall. Oh, we had a blast that whole afternoon...
[Dialogue Option]  So Honami is your hometown?
Platya: Yes, it is. I was on a train leaving Honami when the Lament struck. I, uh... I had a fight with my parents.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm sorry.
Platya: Oh, don't be. That was years ago.
[Dialogue Option]  You still look really young...
Platya: My Resonance ability might not be the strongest out there, but it gives me plenty of time to feel the world.
Platya: In the real world, all that's left of Honami is this giant Tacet Field. But inside this Sonoro Sphere, it still exists.
Platya: To me, the things I need to do stay the same. Collect Reverberations, analyze traces of the Lament, and then... search for the truth.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content:
Startorch Academy - Startorch Academy is a comprehensive research facility that doesn't belong to any country, built with the goal of collaborative scientific research. It is an academic metroplis driven solely by educational and research pursuits. Compared to its official title of "Startorch Academy," the people of Solaris prefer to call it the "Resonator Academy."

Spacetrek Collective - An international scientific organization jointly established by various nations and organizations of Solaris. It oversees the research, development, and construction work in Lahai-Roi. It was the Spacetrek Collective that built the Research Institute and the Startorch Academy in the vast space beneath the frostlands.

Void Storm - The regional Waveworn Phenomenon of Lahai-Roi that disrupts the frequencies of anything around it. It happens in a somewhat cyclical pattern.

title: Flowing Starlight in the Iris
content: Waveworn Phenomena - The Lament's power causes destructive waves across the land of Solaris. Manifestations like the "Tacet Fields," "Tacet Discord Outbreaks," and the enigmatic "Tacetite" are part of what is collectively known as the "Waveworn Phenomena."

title: Chapter III
section: Act I - What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content: Quest Objective: To reach Lahal-Roi in the midst of a Void Storm, you dive into the spatial tunnel, which pulls you into a strange dimension... Upon arriving in Lahai-Roi, you chance upon Lynae, a student who leads you to Startorch Academy. As you begin enrollment, everything about this "academic metropolis" unfolds before your eyes. Meanwhile, shadows stir beneath the Vold Storm...

metadata.section: Act I - What Burns Beneath Frostlands

title: Chapter III
section: Act II - Ode to the Second Sunrise
content: Quest Objective: With the Voldworm threat gone for now, and the commencement of the New Solar Ceremony, Mornye, a Research Institute project lead, invites you to witness the rise of the new sun. However, a distress signal tells you that not everyone is looking forward to this ceremony. To uncover the truth, you and Mornye set off for the Bjartr Woods...

metadata.section: Act II - Ode to the Second Sunrise

title: Chapter III
section: Act III - The Star That Voyages Far
content: Quest Objective: To find the Exostrider and uncover the truth behind your frequency loss, you step into the falling snow and venture toward the silent, pale expanse of the frostlands. Following the traces she had left behind, you pass by a calm and ordinary lake, where the Exostrider in the frostlands is awaiting your arrival. The road trip movie is nearing its end, and your journey together has truly made her happy and content.

metadata.section: Act III - The Star That Voyages Far

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: To reach your goal, you delve deeper into the Exostrider plan, all the while, anomalies hidden in the frostlands reveal themselves.

title: Chapter III
section: Act IV - Gold Suspended in Shadows
content: Quest Objective: The New Solar Celebration is just around the corner. Yet, President Lucilla detects a mysterious frequency appearing in the Academy's Dark Side—one that does not belong to the Academy. You suspect it may be the "reward" once mentioned by the Grand Architect of the Fractsidus. Determined to uncover the truth behind this anomaly, you venture into the Dark Side alongside Sigrika, a student you encountered there...

metadata.section: Act IV - Gold Suspended in Shadows

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: After the New Solar Celebration comes to an end, Lucilla sends you a WaveLine message, saying that the root of the Dark Side anomaly remains unresolved. She hopes you can help her uncover the truth...

title: Chapter III
section: Segue - The Flaming Red from Tomorrow
content: Quest Objective: After the Dark Side incident comes to an end, Lucilla meets with Hiyuki at the auditorium. Lucilla suspects that the Fractsidus may be plotting something far more dangerous behind the scenes...

metadata.section: Segue - The Flaming Red from Tomorrow

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: Voidmatter concentration in Lahai-Roi is intensifying. Before assigning Hiyuki her next mission, Lucilla hoped Hiyuki would take a trip back to Honami... But once there, Hiyuki met...

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: Take action... for the hopes of many, and for the paper plane that once slipped through your fingers.

title: Chapter III
section: Segue - Wishes in the Bell: Epilogue
content: Quest Objective: With the events of Lahai-Roi over... Hiyuki returns to Honami. After all, she must complete the final Purge.

metadata.section: Segue - Wishes in the Bell: Epilogue

title: Chapter III
section: Segue - Beneath a Melting Night Sky
content: Quest Objective: Not long after the Stridergate incident, the Spacetrek Collective informs you that Denia is awake and being kept in isolation. To learn the Fractsidus's next step and open new directions for future research, you head to the infirmary to negotiate with Denia. There, she offers you a "deal." In exchange, you'll need to stay with her for her birthday...

metadata.section: Segue - Beneath a Melting Night Sky

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: A Somnoire door has suddenly appeared in the Academy. Mornye has asked for your help investigating it.

title: Chapter III
content: Quest Objective: Though the Threnodian Aleph-1 was banished, Lucilla finds herself in yet another predicament. In the absence of the Exostrider, funders are questioning whether the Synchronist program—and even the Rabelle College itself—should continue to exist. As both a professor and the head of the Academy, Lucilla must now choose between harsh reality and her ideals.

title: When the Unknown Thrums
content:
Quest Objective: The gateway to Lahai-Roi is now open! What burns beneath the frostlands is waiting for your return!

Shorekeeper: Rover, how are you feeling?
Shorekeeper: The spatial tunnel to Lahai-Roi has stabilized. You may depart whenever you're ready.
Shorekeeper: Meet me at the Shashou Cafe once you've made all necessary preparations.
Shorekeeper: I will be here, waiting.

title: When the Unknown Thrums
content:
[Objective: Talk to Shorekeeper]
Shorekeeper: Rover, you have come.
[Dialogue Option]  I can go to Lahai-Roi now?
Shorekeeper: Yes. Thanks to Namipon's efforts, the Black Shores has confirmed Lahai-Roi's relative coordinates to Honami City and stabilized a one-way tunnel.
Shorekeeper: You may set out whenever you wish.
Rover: What is it?
Shorekeeper: This? Chisa taught me how to make this beverage. I find it tastes better with more milk and sugar...
Shorekeeper: I just made a cup. Would you... like to try it?
[Dialogue Option]  ...Why not?
Shorekeeper: Hm, very well.
(The aroma is rich, but it doesn't taste like coffee at all.)
Rover: Were you worried about something just now?
[Dialogue Option]  I meant that you looked troubled.
Shorekeeper: Yes.
Shorekeeper: Your frequency still fluctuates. It's barely detectable, but... enough to concern me.
Shorekeeper: About Lahai-Roi, the current Void Storm is lasting longer than usual.
Shorekeeper: This is an uncommon state, and for now, the Black Shores can glean little else from what lies beyond the rift.
[Dialogue Option]  Do you think something's happened there?
Shorekeeper: Unlike other regions on Solaris, Lahai-Roi has no Sentinel to guide its civilization. Once considered naught but a forsaken frostland, it remained hidden until the Spacetrek Collective, an international research organization, discovered it.
Shorekeeper: Yet the Threnodian has always lurked in the shadows of this frostland, causing Waveworn Phenomena such as the Void Storm.
Shorekeeper: Exposure to a Void Storm drains human frequencies until they vanish. I suspect that your own frequency loss is linked to this abnormal Storm cycle.
Shorekeeper: The Spacetrek Collective is at the forefront of frequency-stabilization research. Once there, you will undergo a full examination and receive treatment.
Rover: So the source of the problem and its solution can only be found there.
Shorekeeper: Yes. The way to Lahai-Roi is open. It's time for you to return.
[Dialogue Option]  This is...
Shorekeeper: The paperwork for entry into Startorch Academy. Access to Lahai-Roi requires strict clearance, so the Black Shores arranged for you to enter as a "student."
Shorekeeper: This acceptance letter belonged to your past self. It's still valid and will grant you access. Please keep it safe.
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you for preparing all this.
Rover: So this trip's theme is "Back to School," huh?
Shorekeeper: Once you enter Lahai-Roi, I won't be able to contact you, but I will be here as always, awaiting your return with new stories to share.
[Dialogue Option]  Don't worry. Everything will go fine.
Shorekeeper: Yes... Take care of yourself.
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe I'll find a way to teleport back to you.
Shorekeeper: Hmm...? If only that were true.
Chisa: My apologies. I'm late.
Shorekeeper: It's time to set out.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
As soon as you enter the Academy, your frequency begins to stabilize. Lynae, still concerned,  mentions that where you fell was right in the middle of an active Voidworm zone.
When you ask her why she was in such a zone, she pleads for you to keep what happened a secret, saying she can't afford another mark of absence on her record. Just then, her classmate messages her about a study matter. She promises to meet you later at the infirmary before rushing off.

On the way to the infirmary, Abby notes that while your frequency has stabilized, the lost portion is still missing. It suspects the Voidworm absorbed it, since the creature carries the same Threnodian scent as the "eyeball" you saw in the strange spatial domain you passed through to reach Lahai-Roi.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
You decide to fix your fading frequency first, then find out more about the girl you saw in the spatial domain. Not far away, Lynae quietly shuts off a machine that seems to be monitoring you. She clearly knows more about you than she's letting on.
You arrive at the infirmary, and Lynae hurries in shortly after. A medical robot named N.A.N.A. greets you and performs a checkup.
Aside from a few scratches, she immediately notes your abnormal frequency loss. After hearing your situation, she says Dr. Herssen will give the final diagnosis.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Dr. Luuk Herssen reviews your report: your frequency is stable and you're not in immediate danger, but the portion already lost cannot be traced. The Research Institute, he says, has more thorough scanning equipment than the infirmary. He suggests you finish enrolling at the Academy to obtain a "Cassette," a permit and ID needed to enter the Institute.
Curiously, he whispers "Welcome back" as you leave.

Outside the faculty office, you overhear teachers discussing the unusual Voidworm activity and the Academy's countermeasures. Inside, a teacher named Voss confirms your identity and assigns Lynae to guide you through enrollment procedures: registering your personal information and taking an ID photo.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
After everything is complete, Voss hands you a student ID card. You are officially a Startorch Academy student.
She explains that the Academy's goal with the Exostrider is to take on Aleph-1, a Threnodian contained beyond the Stridergate by the Exostrider's giant sword.
With your student card, you can now visit the Research Institute and have your Cassette burned.

Lynae brings you to the loading bay to pick up your ride. The stern Signal Intelligent Guidance & Management Automaton, S.I.G.M.A., insists you read the Safety Regulations before driving it, and scolds Lynae for her speeding and constant bending of modification rules. Lynae argues back while dragging you away.

Taking a short break on the roadside, you both admire Lahai-Roi's scenery. Lynae remarks that although the sky is artificial, she's found more freedom under it than anywhere else.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
After seeing the incident in the tunnel, Lynae seems preoccupied. She leads you to the station below the Research Institute and tells you that the Startorch Express will take you straight there. She wants to join you, but absolutely cannot skip her afternoon class. After parting with her, you board the train alone.
Watching from afar, Lynae's expression turns cold. "...Time to take care of my own business.'

You enter the Cassette Depository and accidentally activate a memory server. Amid the data of the deceased appears a researcher named Mornye. She stabilizes your overloaded frequency and calmly guides you to the burning room, though you catch a brief, fleeting look of shock in her eyes when she first sees you.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
During the burning process, your memories materialize as data projections. You see everything you've experienced since arriving in Solaris, along with scenes you don't recall, scenes featuring Mornye.

After the burning is complete, a researcher discovers your frequency code matches a deleted, anonymous entry in the database. However, Mornye tells the researcher to override it instead of dwelling further into it.

Mornye hands you the finished Cassette tape, explaining that it serves as your ID and a Terminal that warns of Void Storms. These storms disintegrate the frequencies of any living thing they touch, and the Cassette can slow that effect to some extent. As for recovering the frequency you've already lost, she cannot make any promises.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
A sudden call interrupts the conversation: two professors are arguing over the artificial sun's launch procedure, and Mornye is urgently needed. You follow her to the Artificial Sun Lab.

In the Artificial Sun Lab, Researchers Warren and Anslem are in a heated dispute. Warren supports following the Roya's predicted launch window for the New Solar Ceremony, while Anslem refuses to trust their calculations. Mornye mediates, siding with the original plan. Warren stresses that the Hyvatia Detector's measurements are critical, and Anslem leaves after issuing a warning.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Mornye invites you to join the ceremony, and smiles when you agree. At that moment— a Void Storm corrupts Hyvatia, the Reactor Drive's surface detector for inspection and maintenance, triggering it to lose control. It now targets the Institute itself. On the surveillance feed, you see Lynae, who was supposedly in class, standing before it.
The crisis looms. You race off on the institute backup motorbike.

Lynae receives a message from a "liaison" who should be dead. Tracing the signal to its final location, she encounters contaminated Exoswarm.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Lynae receives a message from a "liaison" who should be dead. Tracing the signal to its final location, she encounters contaminated Exoswarm.



Lynae follows the trail and finds the Fractsidus liaison holding a strange device in front of the Hyvatia Detector. He mocks her for wavering between "fugitive" and "guardian," claiming her indecision has caused him trouble. Threatening to expose her identity, he forces her to choose a side.
As Lynae refuses, he activates the device, corrupting the Hyvatia Detector and escaping.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
As Lynae refuses, he activates the device, corrupting the Hyvatia Detector and escaping.



You and Lynae work together to stop Hyvatia's rampage. When you ask why she was there, she hesitates to explain.
Warren arrives and is horrified by the damage. He demands to know why she was at the Institute during class hours and suspects her involvement. Lynae remains silent, as if holding something back.
Just as she prepares to use her Forte to escape, you intervene. You point out that she helped prevent a catastrophe and had no motive for sabotage, calling Warren's accusation premature. Ultimately, he orders you both back to the Academy for a formal investigation.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Back at the Academy, Lynae is questioned by Warren and other faculty. She recounts the Hyvatia malfunction, but you notice she omits any mention of the "liaison." Warren points out that her testimony about the "contaminated Exoswarm" doesn't match the scene investigation or surveillance footage. He questions her motives, especially in light of a recent security breach in the Institute's database. Although you and Voss speak in her defense, Lynae cannot explain the key inconsistencies.
After everyone leaves, you ask her directly why she didn't tell the whole truth. After a pause, she asks to continue the conversation somewhere quieter.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Lynae finally reveals her true identity: she is a former government-hired mercenary from the New Federation's "Lawless Zone." During a mission, she found an admission letter in one of the dead's belongings. Seeing a chance to escape her old life, she took on the dead girl's name and identity to enroll in Startorch Academy.
What she didn't expect was that the dead girl, the real "Lynae," had been a Fractsidus plant, sent to infiltrate the Academy. Wanting to stay in the place she's come to call home, she asks to work with you to uncover the truth and thwart the Fractsidus's plans.
She then takes out the device that caused Hyvatia's malfunction and prepares to investigate its origin in the Department of Engineering.
speakers: Lynae finally reveals her true identity
Lynae finally reveals her true identity

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
She then takes out the device that caused Hyvatia's malfunction and prepares to investigate its origin in the Department of Engineering.



After examining the mysterious device disguised as a calibrator, Lynae discovers it can store and amplify Void Storm frequencies, triggering malfunctions in any creation connected to the Exostrider. The maker is likely someone inside the Academy, capable of remotely activating it at any moment. Handing it over to the authorities might just return it to the Fractsidus mole. To stop this, Lynae decides to overwrite the device's permissions and take control of it herself.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
With you providing cover, the overwrite is successful. During the process, she finds evidence of admin-level access to the Academy's mechs and the Voidmatter Barrier security logs. The device contains three frequency waveforms. One belongs to Hyvatia, and the other two are unidentifiable.
You both decide to investigate the source of these waveforms at the Spacetrek Archive.

At the Archive, with help from the AI administrator I.R.I.S., you search for information tied to the waveform data. The search eventually narrows to two keywords: Void Storm and Exoswarm Contamination.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content: Based on your findings, you conclude that the Fractsidus intends to use the device to trigger a Voidworm rampage, with the most likely target being the Research Institute. You decide to alert the Institute immediately. Lynae chooses to stay behind and prepare a backup plan to boost the device's power, thereby luring the Voidworm toward the Spacetrek Collective's defensive systems. Unbeknownst to you, her overwrite of the device has already been detected by the Fractsidus "contact."

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
The Academy teacher finds Lynae again for a second round of investigation about the Hyvatia incident. They present an anonymous report accusing her of falsifying her admission records, linking her to a criminal record under the name "Lynae." Lynae calmly accepts the investigation and is placed under dormitory confinement. Before she is led away, she secretly passes you a message, entrusting the next phase of the plan to you.

You seek out Dr. Herssen and share your suspicion that Fractsidus agents have infiltrated Startorch Academy. Surprised by your trust, he doesn't confirm your theory outright but promises to liaise with the Research Institute and support your investigation.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
You visit Lynae in her dorm to tell her that you've already warned the Institute. She listens calmly, invites you to sit, and begins talking about her past. She describes her bleak life as a mercenary in the New Federation and how everything became brighter and freer since coming to the Academy. But her life here is ending. She tells you what her disciplinary result is—expulsion and repatriation to the New Federation.
With a bitter smile, she says, "This stolen school life was always gonna end," and bids you farewell. She refuses to accept being sent back and plans to leave on her own.
Just as you ask what she truly wants, a Void Storm strikes. You realize the Voidworm that was supposed to target the Research Institute is now heading straight for the Academy. When you look up, Lynae is already gone.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
You are contacted by Mornye, who you quickly brief her on your plans into giving you the locations of the Institute's anti-Voidworm defenses. Mornye warns that the defence arrays need to be manually activated on-site due to remote access being down from the Void Storm. You decide to stick to the plan and lure the creature away from the Academy.

You meet up with Lynae who was found protecting another student from the Voidworm and trying to seal the barrier. Before she gets attacked by the contaminated Exoswarm, you save her in the nick of time and quickly fill her in on your plans while luring the Voidworm away from the Academy. At the Institute's anti-Voidworm defense area, you and Lynae split up. While you activate the other arrays, Lynae went to distract the Voidworm to buy you time.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
content:
Lynae burns her Resonance power to keep the Voidworm distracted, she reaches her limit and the Voidworm then head towards Rover activating the defense arrays. However, you activate the final array just in time, trapping the Voidworm. You and Lynae work together once more, to take it down once and for all.

You and Lynae are surrounded by excited students and reporters. Amid the questions, Lynae, normally so unflappable, shows a rare, nervous smile. Just then, an Academy officer approaches. Prepared for expulsion, Lynae is instead met with a decision that fills her with joy: due to her bravery, the Academy will allow her to take the entrance exam under her real identity. Lynae accepts, and you watch her cheerful figure depart. Just then, a faint, familiar voice whispers in your ear: "...Protect the sun."
It seems the crisis is far from over.

Ms. Voss: We do have the Exostrider's Drive to thank for this underground haven. But to fight the Threnodian, it must be re-integrated with the Exostrider.
Ms. Voss: That's why we're building an artificial sun. So the Drive can be restored to the Exostrider's mecha.
Ms. Voss: It's a long-term project. The details are... complicated. So I won't cover them here.
Ms. Voss: If you're curious, you can ask Professor Mornye. She's our lead designer on it.
Ms. Voss: Any more questions?
[Dialogue Option]  Not for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Still a few things I don't quite get…
[Dialogue Option]  Not for now.
[Dialogue Option]  Still a few things I don't quite get...

Rover: How do we get to the Research Institute?
Lynae: Usually, I'd take the Startorch Express or get my own ride...
Lynae: Since you're now officially a Startorch student, you get an Academy-issued vehicle. Rare chance, wanna give it a try?
Rover: You bet.
Lynae: Alright, let's go pick up your ride!
Lynae: By the way, have you ever been to school before?
[Dialogue Option]  Can't really remember.
Lynae: Ah, one of those "cram it and dump it" types. Got it.
[Dialogue Option]  I was usually the one teaching.

S.I.G.M.A.: Zero tolerance for traffic violations. Zero tolerance for risking lives. Signal Intelligent Guidance & Management Automaton—S.I.G.M.A.—at your service.
Lynae: Huh? That's it? Pretty underwhelming intro today.
S.I.G.M.A.: This week's student poll ranked it number one. Miss Lynae, perfect timing. I noticed that your vehicle has...
Lynae: AHEM! Mr. S.I.G.M.A., we're here for the new student's ride. We need to get to the Research Institute for Cassette burning. Top priority, you know.

content:
Startorch Traffic Safety Regulations



[Dialogue Option]  (Just sign it!)
S.I.G.M.A.: Please read carefully. Traffic safety is not a game. Speed is a privilege. Protection is a duty. Rules are law.
[Dialogue Option]  (...Read it thoroughly.)
S.I.G.M.A.: Please complete your signature in 5… 4… 3… 2… 1… Confirmed. Safe travels.
[Dialogue Option]  (Read it thoroughly.)
S.I.G.M.A.: ...Confirmed. Thank you for your cooperation. Safe travels.
Lynae: Great. Let's go!
S.I.G.M.A.: Please wait. Resuming dialogue. Scans indicate your vehicle has had thirteen speeding incidents within the last twenty days. Drive safely and comply with the Academy's Traffic Safety Rules.
S.I.G.M.A.: Additionally, your unauthorized modifications fall into a gray area of the Vehicle Management Code. For your own safety, I strongly advise discontinuing all such modifications.
Lynae: Ahem, Mr. S.I.G.M.A, all I did was add a turbocharger, tweak the suspension, and upgrade the brakes. Hardly a violation, wouldn't you say?
Lynae: Besides, compared to seniors strapping missiles and anti-gravity wheels on, I'm practically a model student.
[Dialogue Option]  Missiles and... anti-gravity wheels?
Lynae: Yep. One senior even turned his bike into a light tank for a project. Drove it straight into an active Voidworm zone.
[Dialogue Option]  Everyone here is that wild?
[Dialogue Option]  That's some terrifying engineering skills.
S.I.G.M.A.: I must note that the student committed major Vehicle Management Code violations and breached dozens of school regulations. Severe disciplinary action was taken.
Lynae: ...Which was revoked when he brought back critical Voidworm data.
S.I.G.M.A.: Hm—
Lynae: Now's our chance. Go, go!

content:
[Objective: Head to the Research Institute with Lynae]
Lynae: See that? That's the lift to the surface. We call it the Starward Riseway.
Lynae: It was built alongside the giant sword left behind by the Exostrider and is one of the most important structures in Lahai-Roi.
Lynae: The Research Institute is right at the top.
Lynae: Ahem… So, the scattered mech components of the Exostrider eventually turned into “creatures.” Those Exoswarm we’ve been seeing along the way.
Lynae: They’re part of what makes Lahai-Roi’s ecosystem so unique. For example, the ones living in the underground rivers—
Rover: …It kind of feels like you’re reciting a textbook.
Lynae: Lahai-Roi Ecology, Chapter 2, Section 4.
Lynae: Mm, pretty sure I nailed that one.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
subsection: Head to the Research Institute with Lynae
content:
Lynae: Lahai-Roi Ecology, Chapter 2, Section 4.
Lynae: Mm, pretty sure I nailed that one.



Lynae: The weather's really nice today.
Lynae: How do you feel? Settling in alright?
[Dialogue Option]  Not bad. The wind feels nice.
Lynae: Yeah. Not bad, huh?
[Dialogue Option]  You flirted with the speed limit the entire way...
Lynae: Heh, I'll take that as a compliment on my driving skills…
Lynae: But honestly, it's been ages since I last raced with someone else. Getting to take you for a ride like this? Makes my day!
Rover: You like racing that much?
Lynae: Uh-huh. The roar of the engine, wind in my face... It's like I've got my destination and I'm the one calling the shots.
Lynae: Look... Lahai-Roi's sky might be artificial, but I found more freedom under it than I've ever known anywhere else.
[Dialogue Option]  Freedom?
Lynae: Yeah. I mean, you've only got one life, right? Might as well live it the way you want. When to brake, hit the gas. Hell, even the paint job of your ride. Doesn't matter if you're a normie or a Resonator, everyone should have that choice.
Lynae: That's what Startorch Academy is to me. Before I came here, I never imagined a place like this could exist. Full of people so pure, so driven...
Lynae: With the resolve to burn in the search for answers. With the belief they can actually end the Void Storm and the Threnodian... and maybe break through the Etheric Sea to find what true freedom really looks like.
Lynae: It's beautiful, isn't it?
Lynae: Watching them chase their dreams… It's hard not to want that for yourself.
Rover: But you're already a student here. You have what it takes to chase your dreams too.
Lynae: Yeah, you're right.
Lynae: …But I've gotta say, things are plenty good enough right now.
Lynae: Ah, almost forgot—
Lynae: Welcome! You're now officially a Startorch Academy student!
Lynae: My first introduction was too rushed, so I'm doing it properly this time. I'm Lynae, a second-year in the Preparatory Program.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm Rover from Rabelle College.
Lynae: Time flies. Feels like I just got here, and now I'm a second-year. Hehe, you could call me Miss Lynae, if you want.
Rover: Well then, pleased to meet you... Miss Lynae?
Lynae: ...
Lynae: Maybe just stick with Lynae, haha. Not really used to the whole formality thing.
Lynae: All right, let's get moving! Time to hit the road!

Lynae: Yeah… But it's still kinda weird. Normally, the maintenance bots clear stuff up pretty quick.
Lynae: But seriously, your driving's amazing! You were smooth as butter dodging all that!

content:
[Objective: Head to the Research Institute platform]
Rover: Lynae?
Lynae: What?
Rover: Something on your mind?
Lynae: Not really. Just… on the way here, I thought I saw more Void Storm zones than usual. Makes you wonder.
Lynae: But that's not for me to worry about. Priority's getting your Cassette burned.
Lynae: Look over there—
Lynae: See that floating structure along the track? That's the Spacetrek Collective. From here, you can take the Startorch Express straight inside.
[Dialogue Option]  Like the trains we saw earlier?
Lynae: Yep. They connect Lahai-Roi to the surface frostlands. But with all these Void Storms, surface trips—except for the supply runs—are on hold. Every train turns back here once it reaches the Institute.
Lynae: Well, my mission's done. Once you're inside, someone will take you to the Cassette burning room.
Lynae: If you have questions, find Professor Mornye. She looks aloof, but trust me, she's cool. And she's one of the few willing to race me.
Lynae: I'd love to stick around, but I can't skip another afternoon class.
[Dialogue Option]  No worries. Thanks for bringing me here.
Lynae: Don't sweat it. It's the right thing to do. When I first arrived, the seniors showed me the ropes, just like this.
[Dialogue Option]  So I was just your excuse to skip class?
Lynae: No! I'm not the type to bail on someone after crashing into them, after all.
Lynae: Go on! When you're done, I'll give you a tour of the campus.
Lynae: Well, time to take care of my own business.

Mornye: You came to burn your Cassette, right? I'll take you.

Mornye: I know.

title: What Burns Beneath Frostlands
subsection: Follow Mornye to the Cassette burning room
content:
[Objective: Follow Mornye to the Cassette burning room]
Rover: What was that just now...?
Mornye: Recollections. Recollections of past Spacetrek researchers, staff, and students.
[Dialogue Option]  Recollections?
Mornye: Data stored in the Cassettes. More precisely, memories. They're crucial to the continuity of self-aware consciousness. It's what makes us truly "human."
Mornye: Lahai-Roi is constantly shrouded in the Void Storm, a byproduct of the Voidborne Threnodian. It has the power to disintegrate the frequency of any living being.
Mornye: To counter this, the Institute produced Cassettes, devices designed to capture and preserve a person's frequency and memories, safeguarding their very existence.
Mornye: The Cassettes of the deceased are kept here.
[Dialogue Option]  Then why did they suddenly start playing?
Mornye: You likely resonated with one of the stored frequencies.
Mornye: It happens occasionally, but...
Mornye: Anyway. For now, let's get you to the burning room.

content:

Rover: (Those were… my memories? But the last one…)
Mornye: Something wrong? Feeling unwell?
Rover: ...No, I'm fine. So, this is a ?
Mornye: Yes. Your frequency has been copied and transcribed into it.
Mornye: But before it can be put into service, it needs calibration. Would you hand it over for a moment?
Burning Room Researcher: Hm? So that noise earlier wasn't an error. This frequency code… I've seen the exact same one in the database.
[Dialogue Option]  What's going on?
Burning Room Researcher: Identical codes caused a conflict during transcribing. Normally, Resonators from similar origins have close matches. But a perfect match? That's almost unheard of.
Burning Room Researcher: And stranger still, it's not in any official archive. The file is… empty.
[Dialogue Option]  Are you sure nothing else is in there?
Burning Room Researcher: Just some unreadable data. Not corruption. More like… someone deleted it.
[Dialogue Option]  What if you rename it to Rover (1)?
Burning Room Researcher: ...Hm?
[Dialogue Option]  Just a joke...
[Dialogue Option]  (Could it be... the past me?)
Rover: (Could it have been me who left it behind? But if I deleted it myself… why leave any trace?)
Mornye: Just a data error. Overwriting should solve it.
Burning Room Researcher: Ah, understood, Professor Mornye.
Mornye: This , or FCR, will alert you when a Void Storm appears. It also dampens the effects of the Storm and stabilizes your existence here in Lahai-Roi.
Mornye: So keep it on you at all times.
[Dialogue Option]  Understood.
Mornye: But without adequate precautions, it still won't fully protect you from the Void Storm's effects. Many surveyors and students have had their frequencies erased this way.
Rover: Professor Mornye, about my frequency...
Mornye: …Mm, I have read your report. You're stable for now. Compared to your enrollment check-up, your Rabelle's Curve has leveled out. But yes, your frequency still shows signs of past loss.
Mornye: As for the Voidworm, there's no precedent... No one's ever survived having their frequency devoured. Whether yours can be restored is unknown.
Mornye: So don't take unnecessary risks. That's rule number one.
[Dialogue Option]  I came here to find out what happened to my frequency.
Mornye: I understand. I'll keep watch for anything that might help.
[Dialogue Option]  I don't know much about this place yet.
Mornye: Ask me anything you need to know.
