title: All That Sunlight Touches
content: Completing the quest awards the Rover's Journey III Trophy Taste of Sweetness

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content: Quest Objective: To reach your goal, you delve deeper into the Exostrider plan, all the while, anomalies hidden in the frostlands reveal themselves.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Return to Startorch Academy]
Rover: (Luuk texted me to go over the Exostrider plan at the infirmary. Better get going.)

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Head to the infirmary]
Rover: (Nivora... Has she been staying here to recover?)

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Greet Nivora]
Rover: How are you recovering from your injuries, Nivora?
Nivora: Oh, i-it's you, Rover. Uh, yes. I'm feeling much better.
Nivora: Dr. Herssen took very good care of me. I just did what he said and rested for a few days here, and I barely feel any pain now.
Nivora: Are you here to visit him?
Rover: Yes, we have something to discuss. Is he here?
Nivora: He's in the counseling room next door. Um... My friend Sigrika is in there. It might take a while.
Rover: Thanks. Take care of yourself.
Luuk Herssen: How to put this... I think you can have more faith in yourself, Sigrika.
Sigrika: Faith in myself...
Luuk Herssen: You see, people can be more perceptive than you might realize, including those you care about. So try not to take everything to heart. Go a little easier on yourself.
Luuk Herssen: Good or bad, true or false, these things have a way of coming to light. And as your friend Denia said, sometimes a little distraction is good for your health.
Sigrika: Yeah… I'll give it a try! Thank you, Dr. Herssen.
Luuk Herssen: You're welcome. Again, don't push yourself too hard.
Luuk Herssen: I'd take it you're the type who'd suddenly bolt up in bed at night, wide awake, worrying about an exam. And that'd probably go on for a whole week.
Sigrika: Huh?! Is it really that obvious?!
Luuk Herssen: Hahaha! Only my conjecture.
Luuk Herssen: Would you like some candy? Sweets help keep a smile.
Sigrika: Sure! And... is it okay for me to come back some other time, Dr. Herssen?
Luuk Herssen: Why, of course. Feel free to visit my office any time, Sigrika.
Rover: So, about that Exostrider plan you mentioned. Let's get into it.
Luuk Herssen: All in good time. Let's start with something lighter first.
Rover: Something lighter?
Luuk Herssen: Any topic at all. But let's slow the tempo a little.
Luuk Herssen: You're too eager, Rover. Your emotions are clouding your judgment. You must feel it too.
Luuk Herssen: Here. A piece of candy? It'll help take the edge off and lighten the mood.
Rover: ...No, thanks.
Luuk Herssen: I understand your anxiety over Aemeath's situation. You've always held her dear. But it's taken more out of you than you realize.
Luuk Herssen: Things are best taken one step at a time. The Exostrider hasn't awakened yet. The key is to pace ourselves. Slow and steady, right?
Rover: Okay, you're right. Let's table the Exostrider for now. Let's talk about you, Luuk.
Rover: I trust Aemeath. What we experienced together proved she was telling me the truth. And there's a connection there I can't ignore.
Rover: But you and me? We might be "strangers in passing who became confidants" as you put it, but it feels like every conversation we've had just skims the surface.
Rover: I prefer to know who I'm working with before jumping into something as big as opening the Stridergate. It'll affect the entire Lahai-Roi region.
Luuk Herssen: Hehe. Point taken. It seems a proper introduction is long overdue.
Luuk Herssen: Please, ask me anything. I'll answer as candidly as I can.
Rover: Are you a Consultant from the Black Shores?
Luuk Herssen: That, I am not. Work that leaves documented trails doesn't suit my style. But I am acquainted with quite a few Bloom Bearers.
Rover: Aemeath said she didn't know you well, but that I could trust you. You also know about the bond between me and her. How?
Luuk Herssen: Aemeath is a sharp girl. Even though you never introduced me to her, she could read between the lines of your actions.
Luuk Herssen: She's a lot like you. Smart, driven, good at bearing burdens. Though she's proven to be even more stubborn than you are.
Luuk Herssen: After you left Lahai-Roi, she came to see me a few times in the name of counseling... to learn about you.
Rover: You didn't tell her anything.
Luuk Herssen: I didn't. You had other tasks for me here in Lahai-Roi. You didn't let us properly get to know each other because you wanted to shield her from my line of work.
Luuk Herssen: She later stopped these visits after realizing that.
Luuk Herssen: Still… I really hoped she would have opened up to me more. You both tend to keep things to yourselves, and that's never good for anyone.
Rover: One last question.
Rover: What do you mean by "I had other tasks for you"?
Luuk Herssen: That is a key topic, but not suitable for discussion here.
Luuk Herssen: The Spacetrek Collective is backed by a number of different nations and powers. Their internal politics are of no concern to us. There are many watching eyes among the support staff.
Luuk Herssen: The infirmary is, after all, a public space. Why don't we take this somewhere more private?
Rover: To where?
Luuk Herssen: I have a place in mind. Just come with me, golden boy.
N.A.N.A.: More personal business to attend to again, Dr. Herssen?
Luuk Herssen: Shh, just a quick break, N.A.N.A. Mind holding down the fort? The next shift will be here soon.
N.A.N.A.: Take care, Doctor. Do try to return in one piece.
Luuk Herssen: Don't worry, I have Rover with me today.
Rover: Sundermere?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. I keep a "small workspace" of my own here.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Defeat the enemies]
Luuk Herssen: Leave them to me. Let's not waste any more time.
Luuk Herssen: The Exostrider's sword emits a unique frequency. It shields my "workspace" from most long-range detection methods.
Rover: You picked a good spot.

"A Small Workspace" Here, fading voices and hidden trails are woven into a web, and the rationale of liquid gold is patiently unraveled…

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Talk to Luuk Herssen]
Rover: Quite a stash.
Luuk Herssen: Heh. This is what a secret room is about.
Luuk Herssen: Now, where were we?
Luuk Herssen: Let's start with the conclusion, before we get into all the details: You asked me to come to Lahai-Roi to watch for any Fractsidus activity.
Luuk Herssen: Warren was the first Fractsidus mole you uncovered, and he certainly won't be the last.
Luuk Herssen: Think of the Spacetrek Collective as a web of competing powers. It's as much a haven of independence as a playground for agendas.
Luuk Herssen: An isolated polar region, rich with Exoswarm and the potential for technological breakthrough. Lahai-Roi is a gold mine.
Luuk Herssen: Even for the Fractsidus.
Rover: You're saying the fall of Helios wasn't their real goal?
Luuk Herssen: It was one of several. After your journey in Huanglong and Rinascita, I'm sure you've come to realize their true aim.
Rover: The Threnodian. Aleph-1.
Luuk Herssen: Correct. Given the Threnodian's unique nature, it's sure to catch their attention. Moreover, Aleph-1 is closely linked to the Stridergate, which may be our ticket to outer space.
Rover: Spying on the Fractsidus is risky. Why would I have chosen you for this task?
Luuk Herssen: Well, that is a bit of a long story.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Rover: Spying on the Fractsidus is risky. Why would I have chosen you for this task?
Luuk Herssen: Well, that is a bit of a long story.



Luuk Herssen: You've always preferred to see things for yourself. Please, follow me to that table.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
subsection: Inspect the container on the table
content:
[Objective: Inspect the container on the table]
You examine the transparent container, which appears to have some kind of liquid inside.
There is a golden hue quietly contained inside.
You realize it looks identical to the blood that flowed from Luuk's hand during your fight in the space station.
Luuk Herssen: The "Golden Serum" developed by the Novialle Group. But I prefer its other name—.
Luuk Herssen: My father started it as a medication for rare diseases. But as research progressed, it came to represent something far more ambitious—the "drug of evolution."
Rover: Evolution? Sounds like something the Fractsidus would like.
Luuk Herssen: Well, on paper, it worked. I became its Resonator, so it would be unfair to say it was entirely useless.
Luuk Herssen: But I was a rare case who survived. All it cost me was excruciating pain and my color vision. Most test subjects like me didn't make it.
Luuk Herssen: It wasn't until I met you that I realized there was more to the story.

metadata.subsection: Inspect the container on the table

title: All That Sunlight Touches
subsection: Inspect the container on the table
content:
Luuk Herssen: It wasn't until I met you that I realized there was more to the story.



Luuk Herssen: The rest is in my study. Shall we?

metadata.subsection: Inspect the container on the table

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Examine the drawing]
The picture is a child's drawing of a family, rendered in simple, earnest lines.
A father and an older and younger brother... each one wearing a big, happy smile.
On the back of the framed picture, a scribbled note reads: "Always happy! —Rhein Herssen"
It must have been drawn years ago, but the frame is carefully preserved and shows little wear.
Luuk Herssen: My brother Rhein drew this picture.
Luuk Herssen: We're not related by blood. Father took us both in after his own children passed away from a rare illness long ago.
Luuk Herssen: Rhein never could handle pain, but he was easy to cheer up.  Whenever the grown-ups would give me candy, I'd save it all for him.
Rover: (So that's why he always has candy with him.)
Luuk Herssen: For a while, I tried to be the perfect son Father wanted. It never worked, so eventually I stopped trying.
Luuk Herssen: It only got worse from there. What Father tried to do to Rhein was unforgivable. And then came that accident...
Luuk Herssen: I thought what my father did was a rather mundane story. A cliché, someone trying to atone for past guilt, only to cause greater harm.
Luuk Herssen: Until your hints made me suspect it was someone's staged finale. So I had my father's grave exhumed. It was empty.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Examine the damaged report]
You examine the burnt page. Many parts of it are illegible due to the burns.
It appears to have been salvaged from a fire.
Judging by the legible contents, it's a report.
It mentions Lahai-Roi and Voidmatter, and was originally destined for the New Federation.
At the bottom of the report, you find a signature... the Fractsidus's insignia.
Luuk Herssen: The entire Lollo Logistics carrier was already blown to smithereens by the time I recovered this page.
Luuk Herssen: I managed a quick glimpse before the fire consumed most of the page. Hehe, it is a report from an Overseer.
Rover: A Fractsidus Overseer's report on its way to the New Federation?
Luuk Herssen: Yes, tucked away in a Lollo Logistics delivery box.
Luuk Herssen: The recipient is "Eris" in the New Federation.
Rover: Those three items you just showed me... Did the Fractsidus get into  work after learning about the  potential for "evolution"?
Luuk Herssen: They didn't just "get into" our work. They went a step further—replacement.
Luuk Herssen: Have you ever met the Fractsidus's Grand Architect?
Rover: The "thousand-faced survivor." We met near the "Styx Lake" deep within the Dark Tide.
Rover: Wait... Does this mean your father was...?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. My father was just another face the Grand Architect borrowed. Though, looking back now, I can't recall the moment the real him was taken.
Luuk Herssen: I think the Grand Architect sees life and death as a game. I wouldn't be surprised if "Father" was even smiling in his coffin as we buried him in that downpour!
Luuk Herssen: So, that's your answer. Why did you choose me? Because I have a very personal reason to go after the Fractsidus—hatred.
Rover: Hatred... Even now?
Luuk Herssen: Now, it has become something of a habit.
Luuk Herssen: Continue this train of investigation and you'll see for yourself what they are. But before you do, there's something I should share.
Luuk Herssen: My friends in the Black Shores told me you've already had a few run-ins with certain Overseers. Is that right?
Rover: Three: Cristoforo, Phrolova, and Scar. Plus the Grand Architect you mentioned.
Luuk Herssen: Ah, those names do ring a bell. Phrolova is codenamed Hecate. Cristoforo? Arachnos. Intriguing, isn't it? The flair they have for their own branding.
Luuk Herssen: But it's a telling detail. A codename can reveal its owner's style, personal tastes, and even ambitions.
Luuk Herssen: Think about it. A powerful Resonator who causes chaos at random leaves no trail to follow. But give them a preference, a pattern, and we can start to build a profile from the pieces.
Luuk Herssen: I've been compiling reports on the Overseers for years. Allow me to share what I've learned so far.
Luuk Herssen: I've reactivated your access. You'll find the door controls right over there.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Head to the farthest room]
Luuk Herssen: The Fractsidus is loosely organized. Most of its members have only undergone basic, artificially-induced body modification. They're not terribly difficult to neutralize.
Luuk Herssen: But if you encounter Artificers with more... creative modifications,  you're likely looking at the handiwork of "Hydra."
Luuk Herssen: Hydra is their leading mind on human evolution and body modifications. Whoever they are, they often work in tandem with "Siren."
Luuk Herssen: In other words, if you spot one, be on guard in case the other is lurking close by.
Luuk Herssen: Zashiki-warashi won't require much of your attention. This Overseer primarily operates in Ashinohara, a region that's been largely destroyed by the Lament.
Rover: Ashinohara... I've heard of it somewhere before.
Luuk Herssen: The girl we had in the infirmary for a while, Chisa, I remember? The city that trapped her, Honami, is part of Ashinohara.
Luuk Herssen: Now, on to two key pieces of the puzzle.
Luuk Herssen: I did say the Fractsidus was a loose organization, but even the most scattered cells still need funding to function.
Luuk Herssen: Remember that report from earlier? It's only a matter of time before you go to the New Federation. And based on the intel I've gathered...
Luuk Herssen: That's their most critical base of operations, and where you'll find "Eris."
Rover: How critical? Do they operate in the open?
Luuk Herssen: Not exactly. But in a place where money talks, they must have members in the highest echelons of government and business. Key members.
Luuk Herssen: Their foothold in the New Federation has given them immense leverage. With that endless stream of wealth, the Fractsidus operates with impunity across the planet.
Luuk Herssen: Speaking of which, Startorch Academy is also heavily funded by the New Federation. To be blunt, they're the Spacetrek Collective's single largest donor.
Rover: Eris, huh? Duly noted. I'm assuming the other key piece is the Grand Architect?
Luuk Herssen: The Fractsidus Grand Architect. Their true name is unknown. They only appear through borrowed identities: Real people, legendary beings, and even the phantoms of the dead from others' memories.
Luuk Herssen: I did brush shoulders with them once. It was a shame I had no idea at the time and missed my shot.
Luuk Herssen: This pen was the only thing I brought back from that great fire.
Luuk Herssen: I have yet to discipher the lettering, but it shows one thing for sure: the Grand Architect has been around for a very, very long time.
Luuk Herssen: It's a pity you called me to Lahai-Roi. Otherwise, I would've continued following that trail. But you always have good reason. Right?
Rover: You uncovered all this by yourself?
Luuk Herssen: More or less. I did have some help along the way.
Rover: To get your hands on one of the Grand Architect's personal items. You did more than just follow a trail. You infiltrated them.
Luuk Herssen: Playing along with them isn't that difficult once you get the hang of it. Like I said, they are a loose organization.
Rover: Knowing the Fractsidus, stealing all that intel on the Overseers is risky, no matter how loose they are. Each infiltration will only be more dangerous than the last.
Rover: Luuk, how can a doctor who doesn't value his own life save anyone else's?
Luuk Herssen: You know, this is the second time you've said those words to me.
Luuk Herssen: They got away again.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Luuk Herssen: You know, this is the second time you've said those words to me.
Luuk Herssen: They got away again.



Luuk Herssen: (If I hadn't been so cautious, I could've "taken care" of them this time.)
Luuk Herssen: (I should send today's findings to Rover. It's been two years. I suppose I'm due for a report.)
Luuk Herssen: Good, you got the intel. Would've been a shame if I got myself killed for nothing.
Luuk Herssen: You want me to go to Lahai-Roi? Why?

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Luuk Herssen: Good, you got the intel. Would've been a shame if I got myself killed for nothing.
Luuk Herssen: You want me to go to Lahai-Roi? Why?



Past Rover: There's evidence of their activity in Lahai-Roi. I need you to keep an eye on things. And frankly, you need a break.
Luuk Herssen: Now is not the right time.
Past Rover: You've already drawn enough attention. Do we really have to wait for you to get killed to decide it's "the right time"?
Past Rover: How can a doctor save anyone else's life if he doesn't value his own?  Keep pushing like this and you'll be no different from them.
Luuk Herssen: Not pulling any punches, are you?
Past Rover: Trust me, that's only the warm up. Lahai-Roi is a nice place, Luuk. Bright, passionate students, beautiful snow. Perfect for slowing things down.
Past Rover: Listen to me on this. Come.
Luuk Herssen: ...
Luuk Herssen: Very well. As you wish.
Luuk Herssen: So I've led a leisurely life in Lahai-Roi ever since. No need to worry, I know my limits.
Luuk Herssen: Let's set aside the Fractsidus for now. We should discuss the Exostrider plan. But first, tell me what happened to you and Aemeath in the frostlands.
[Dialogue Option]  (You briefly recount to Luuk the events in the frostlands.)
Luuk Herssen: I see. Aemeath, she... No wonder you're in such a state.
Rover: I understand her reasons. She was fighting for her dream, for Lahai-Roi, in the only way she knew how. And I respect that. The fate she chose for herself.
Rover: But I won't accept it. There's more I haven't tried. I'm not done fighting for her.
Luuk Herssen: Of course. I wouldn't expect you to give up so easily.
Luuk Herssen: Now, about the Exostrider... It started with the Spacetrek Collective finding a "giant Soliskin root network" in Bjartr Woods. They identified it as the "lid" sealing the Stridergate, so to speak.
Luuk Herssen: It keeps the Threnodian's fractured forms sealed on both sides of the Stridergate. Break it, and these forms will reunite. That wouldn't just spell Lahai-Roi's doomsday, but the entire world.
Luuk Herssen: But the Collective still yearned to open that gateway, to explore the unknown. So, they created the Synchronists. The idea was to use Augmented Resonance to amplify the Exostrider's power, hoping that would keep the Threnodian suppressed.
Luuk Herssen: But lately, the Threnodian's attacks on the seal have been increasing. I'm afraid the Fractsidus is also getting ready to make a move.
Luuk Herssen: With the Reactor Core returned, all you need now is a little patience. Wait for the Exostrider to awaken. Then we can focus on how to use it to find Aemeath.
Luuk Herssen: You were a Synchronist in the Academy once before. I'll speak with Lucilla about getting you piloting access.
Rover: Then I'll wait for your news, Luuk.
Luuk Herssen: Certainly. But our immediate priority should be the Fractsidus. I have a feeling they're planning to sabotage our plans for the Exostrider.
Luuk Herssen: (Rover said he'd like to check on the Exostrider in the frostlands before he left. Well, it could be a way to take his mind off things.)
Luuk Herssen: (Now then—)
Lucilla: Dr. Herssen. Is something the matter?
Luuk Herssen: Must you always assume the worst, Lucilla? Can't I just call to chat?
Lucilla: I find that highly unlikely, Doctor. Let's skip the preamble. What is it?
Luuk Herssen: Rover.
Lucilla: Ah. So this is about "Aemeath." He was so tight-lipped with me about what happened in the frostlands, yet he spoke to you.
Luuk Herssen: Sitting on our hands won't fix anything, and he was willing to open up. If a friend runs into trouble, I'll naturally step in to listen.
Luuk Herssen: Besides, what I have to share today benefits the Academy. It could help us... get ahead of a few potential issues.
Lucilla: Very well. Let's hear it then. Meet me at the Institute, the usual spot.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
subsection: Meet Lucilla at your usual spot
content:
[Objective: Meet Lucilla at your usual spot]
Tired Student: Urgh... My head's spinning...
Tired Student: No, not now. I have to finish my thesis... I can faint after the paper's done!

metadata.subsection: Meet Lucilla at your usual spot

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Talk to the students]
Tired Student: Oh... Dr. Herssen... It's good to see you...
Luuk Herssen: Athan, you looked fine not long ago. What happened to you?
Tired Student: M-My thesis... My spot at the...
Luuk Herssen: Hold on, I recall you coming by the infirmary with good news earlier. Something about an Institute professor recruiting you for your top marks?
Luuk Herssen: Is this the price you have to pay for that? Careful, you might get talked out of the job over health issues.
Tired Student: No! I will get that position at the Institute! I'll crawl there if I have to! I'll... I'll come back from the dead if I die first!
Luuk Herssen: Sigh. Now you're just delirious. I know getting this opportunity wasn't easy, and you can't exactly just ask for time off. Come by my office later. I'll write you a sick note.
Luuk Herssen: You can't run yourself like an Exoswarm, thinking you'll recharge the moment the sun comes up. It's not how we humans work.
Tired Student: Oh, thank you, Doctor! Good things are bound to come your way! Ah, this takes me back. I always got my best sleep passed out in your infirmary...

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Continue onward]
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: Let's see here. Who's still skipping their physical check-up...
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: Do these people not believe in a proper work-life balance?! So irresponsible!

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Talk to the Senior Doctor]
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: Ah, young Luuk! What brings you to the Institute today?
Luuk Herssen: Just here to discuss something with someone. How have your shifts been treating you these past few months?
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: Not bad. You know these researchers, getting them in for a check-up is like pulling their teeth. I have to hunt them down myself.
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: What do you say we grab a drink after my shift? The meal plans here are all "nutritional efficiency." Tastes like chewed-up cardboard!
Luuk Herssen: Of course. Why don't I show you that scout drone model I just finished while we're at it?
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: You work fast! You really do enjoy that sort of tinkering.
Luuk Herssen: Taking things apart and putting them back together again is quite stress-relieving. It's a nice way to unwind after a day's work.
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: So... Whaddya say we sneak over to Rogan's place when we get a minute and... liberate the cannon barrel from that precious bot of his?
Slacking Off Senior Doctor: We can put it back after he's had a good meltdown!
Luuk Herssen: Huh. I'd rather not be an accomplice to that. It's unethical. And I can't believe you're still holding a grudge over that fish he stewed behind your back.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Continue onward]
Lucilla: Have a seat, Doctor.
Lucilla: Shame. I thought Rover would come with you.
Luuk Herssen: He's been here before. But things are different now. I prefer not to have him tangled in the Collective's trivial matters.
Lucilla: Fair enough. But I'm not like those stubborn old goats you're used to dealing with. I don't chase after pride or rank. All I care about is Startorch Academy.
Lucilla: Now go on. Give me the highlights, Dr. Herssen.
Lucilla: The Fractsidus. Hmm, I understand. I'll keep a closer watch.
Lucilla: As for piloting the Exostrider, if Rover is capable, that's fine by me. The Research Institute will see to the preparations.
Lucilla: That said, we can't ignore the risks that come with opening the Stridergate. I have someone in mind who could help. But first, let me have a quick word with her.
Lucilla: The Threnodian concerns every one of us at Lahai-Roi. I'll handle the board as you've asked. You focus on Rover and the matters here on campus.
Luuk Herssen: Thank you for your understanding, Lucilla—President.
Luuk Herssen: Our conversation went more smoothly than I expected. I thought you might think I had a hidden agenda.
Luuk Herssen: As a thank you, care for some candy?
Lucilla: I'll pass. I'm well aware of your candy outreach program across campus. I've had my fill of sweets over the years.
Lucilla: As for what you said earlier. I've been here long enough to know exactly who you are.
Lucilla: Thanks to your efforts in uncovering those moles, the Academy is safer, and we have far fewer headaches to worry about.
Lucilla: What truly surprised us was your choice to stay all these years and become one of Lahai-Roi's steadfast guardians.
Luuk Herssen: Oh, I'm just glad the President doesn't see me as some busybody.
Lucilla: Heh. You're the right kind of busybody. The kind we're happy to have.
Luuk Herssen: A friend of mine sold me on this place. Went on and on about the beautiful snow and the bright, passionate students. Convinced me to come.
Luuk Herssen: But when I actually got here? Heh, nothing like the brochure he described. Turns out, eight out of ten staff members were planted here by different factions!
Luuk Herssen: Our students dream of reaching the stars, all while living in a gilded cage. Meanwhile, we have Roya dealing in Exoswarm parts and colluding with New Federation smugglers.
Luuk Herssen: I know that these students aren't fools. They're the best minds from across the nations. If even I can see what's going on, how could they be blind to it?
Luuk Herssen: It's their ideals, their hope for the future that lets them endure the ugly realities of this place without becoming cynical.
Luuk Herssen: I only came to Lahai-Roi because a friend recommended it. But now—
Lucilla: Now you've grown to like it here, right?
Luuk Herssen: Haha, yes. Same as you, Madam President!
Luuk Herssen: An urgent transmission from N.A.N.A.? If you'll excuse me.
N.A.N.A.: Dr. Herss... *static*... en. There was a break-in at the... infirmary.
N.A.N.A.: Nivora's been kidnapped... by the one we previously detained... *static*... Warren.
Luuk Herssen: What is your status? Are you severely damaged?
N.A.N.A.: No need... to worry. Just need... time to repair.
Luuk Herssen: Understood. Prioritize damage control after this call. Notify the Academy's security department.
Luuk Herssen: It'll take time for them to respond. I'll go after Warren. Which direction did he take her?
N.A.N.A.: Received... *static*... message from the Academy. They're heading towards the SkyArk Space Station in the frostlands.
Luuk Herssen: (It's the Court of Savantae space station Rover and I discovered before.)
Luuk Herssen: I'm on my way.
Luuk Herssen: Warren has escaped. He's taken a student and is heading for one of the debris fields in the frostlands.
Lucilla: What do you plan to do?
Luuk Herssen: I'm going after him. I'd like you to set up a perimeter there to cut off his escape and prevent any further risks to the Academy.
Lucilla: You want me to secure a perimeter while you go in alone to handle Warren?
Luuk Herssen: I have a... hypothesis. One I'd like to verify by myself.
Lucilla: Very well. Your track record warrants it. Go, Dr. Herssen, I'll expect good news.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Enter the SkyArk Space Station]
Luuk Herssen: (Nivora... Why now?)

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Continue onward and gather intel]

title: All That Sunlight Touches
subsection: Defeat the enemies summoned by Warren
content:
Luuk Herssen: (SkyArk's data room. There must be a reason.)
Luuk Herssen: (Was that just impulse... or perhaps...)



Nivora: No!
Nivora: Oh... Dr. Herssen... Warren, is he—
Luuk Herssen: He's only unconscious. Everything's okay, Nivora. How are you feeling?
Nivora: Ugh... I'm... fine. It's just that he struck me in the back of the neck. It really hurts.
Nivora: I'm... really scared.
Luuk Herssen: It's okay. Don't force yourself to hold it in. After a shock like that, it's much better if you let it out. Keeping it bottled up is stressful in itself.
Luuk Herssen: Take your time. Tell me what happened when you're ready.
Nivora: Okay... I'll try... I just... I need a moment...
Luuk Herssen: Then rest here for now. I'll go check on Warren.
Nivora: I fell asleep on the hospital bed. When I woke up and opened my eyes, Warren was pointing a gun at my head.
Nivora: He was frantic. Grilled me non-stop about SkyArk. And when he found out I'd been to the station before, he forced me to bring him.
Nivora: Wait! Those researchers by the door—
Luuk Herssen: One of them didn't make it. The other two are still alive.
Nivora: I see. As for what else happened, I don't really remember.
Luuk Herssen: That's alright. I've already formed a rough theory about his motives now. You should rest, Nivora. We'll handle things from here.
Nivora: Is that so? Then, Dr. Herssen, care to share your theory?

metadata.subsection: Defeat the enemies summoned by Warren

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Nivora: My, my. Played me for a fool, didn't you?
Nivora: I was going to kill you for a little one-on-one time with Rover. Shame.
Kharon: Regrettable, that you evaded what was meant for you.
"Triss": But it's okay. Uncle Warren's dead. Nice and clean!
Devoted Watcher: Being caught out in the open, and still he thought he could just vanish from Lahai-Roi and get away with this fiasco? The naivety is remarkable.
Nivora: Anyway, I got back what I wanted too, so I'm a happy girl.
Luuk Herssen: On my way here, I kept wondering why you acted so quickly. It didn't fit your usual style of staying in character until the very end.
Luuk Herssen: Just as I thought... You were after this pen.
Nivora: Ah, yes. My precious. I couldn't find it anywhere! So it was you who took it from me.
Nivora: This is the first time someone's taken something from me! Oh, I almost forgot to ask, when did you begin to suspect?
Luuk Herssen: If you must know, my suspicions began to deepen during our last visit to the space station. When you feigned that injury.
Luuk Herssen: Your "acting" had been flawless, Grand Architect. But even you cannot mimic what you don't understand.
Luuk Herssen: Death itself.
Luuk Herssen: To an immortal like you, no matter how many times you die, it's just another lost identity. And I happened to have "seen" you (my father) die before.
Nivora: Oh? Is this why you've had your eye on me all this time?
Nivora: Let me think... Hmm, whoops? Can't seem to remember. My bad.
Nivora: My real favorite things are the ones that are really old and far, far away.
Nivora: But you... you're something special, Dr. Herssen! You're the first person in forever to ever come this close.
Nivora: Without you, the game in Lahai-Roi would be so boring! So, you get prizes!
Nivora: And I promise, it's right up your alley.
Nivora: Now, for the first one. At the upcoming New Solar Celebration, among all the lovely students, stands a member of the Fractsidus.
Nivora: I'm so looking forward to that child's performance!
Rover: Telling us this doesn't do your spy any good.
Nivora: But that's what makes it fun! It's a cat-and-mouse game. The mouse needs to know the cat is coming, or how else will it run fast enough on its little wheel?
Nivora: To win, you just have to be the hunter.
Nivora: And if you do end up catching that child, that just proves they were useless anyway!
Luuk Herssen: That was only the first. What's the next one?
Nivora: The next prize is right here in this data room. You're so smart, Dr. Herssen. I bet you've already figured it out, no?
Nivora: I had so much fun on this little trip to the SkyArk. So, Rover, how did you feel seeing the Etheric Sea?
Nivora: Oh, home, sweet home! Your faraway home, the one you can never, ever go back to!
Rover: ...!
Nivora: Mmm! Leading you there wasn't all for nothing. The look on your face was the sweetest treat.
Nivora: Let's be sure to have more fun like this in the future. Until next time, you two!
Nivora: I wish you a pleasant past, present, and future!

title: All That Sunlight Touches
subsection: Discuss your options with Luuk Herssen
content:
[Objective: Discuss your options with Luuk Herssen]
Rover: Why did you stop me? You think we couldn't have stopped her here?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. My goal was to gather intelligence, not apprehend the Fractsidus's Grand Architect.
Luuk Herssen: When we dug up my "father's" empty grave, I realized that it is no simple feat to find an immortal who leaves no trail.
Luuk Herssen: The Grand Architect may appear to act on a whim, but in my observation, that playfulness is just another layer of disguise. There's a purpose behind it.
Luuk Herssen: When N.A.N.A. called earlier, something felt off. Warren is a researcher himself. Why would he need to take a student hostage to investigate a debris field?
Luuk Herssen: Even if he did, breaking into the infirmary and letting N.A.N.A. send a distress call was a sloppy strategy. Of course, I'd be the first person she contacted.
Rover: So that's why you called me afterwards.
Rover: I did hear Nivora say you've had her in the infirmary all this time. You were keeping an eye on her, then?
Luuk Herssen: I was waiting for her to show her hand. Until then, it was all speculation. I needed to see her end the "act" to be sure.
Luuk Herssen: Immortal. A thousand faces... We've managed to gather quite a bit of intel on the Grand Architect.
Luuk Herssen: If I'm not mistaken, there should be something more important hidden in this room.
Luuk Herssen: Otherwise, she wouldn't have called it a prize.

metadata.subsection: Discuss your options with Luuk Herssen

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Investigate the data room]
Luuk Herssen: These are... the personnel files from the SkyArk Space Station.
Luuk Herssen: This lettering—
Luuk Herssen: Do you recall the lead researcher on the Etheric Sea Initiative, Rover? The one we saw in the hologram during our first visit.
Rover: Professor Junxi?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. During his lecture, he mentioned a scholar who had just joined the project, Weiying. But his introduction was cut short.
Luuk Herssen: I've found that scholar's record in the system. And her name.
Luuk Herssen: The letters of this name are a perfect match with those engraved on that pen.
Rover: Are you saying that scholar is the Grand Architect?
Luuk Herssen: According to these records, the Etheric Sea Initiative was stalled due to a lack of funding until she joined. Then it was pushed back on track.
Luuk Herssen: Her involvement influenced the CSC's (Court of Savantae) decision on this project.
Luuk Herssen: But everything else about her birthplace, employment history, or academic background is missing.
Rover: Sounds like another identity borrowed by the Grand Architect.
Luuk Herssen: Indeed. It seems we've just traced this thousand-faced individual back to an even earlier point in Solaris's history.
Luuk Herssen: These records also show Weiying took great interest in the CSC and Etheric Sea Initiative during that period. That must be why she infiltrated the SkyArk Space Station.
Nivora: The universe… What secrets is it hiding, behind all those infinite stars?
Nivora: I really want to know.
Luuk Herssen: And about that footage—No, no need to explain. The fewer people who know about your secret, the better.
Luuk Herssen: It just occurred to me that this wasn't a coincidence. If her goal in the past involved you, then it's something to keep in mind on your journey ahead.
Rover: (The Etheric Sea. That might've been my entry point to Solaris after leaving my distant homeland.)
Rover: (Weiying was interested in the Etheric Sea before its planet-wide spread. Did she want to use it as a medium to reach somewhere beyond?)
Rover: I will. Given her nature, it's only a matter of time before we meet again.
Rover: The more she appears, the more she gives away. If she enjoys "playing games," then it means she'll follow some rules at least.
Rover: Otherwise, she'd die of boredom.
Luuk Herssen: Hah, exactly. And as I've said before, sometimes style, personal taste, and ambition can be more revealing than intended.
Luuk Herssen: The Fractsidus has more than one base in Solaris, and I'm far from the only one with a grudge or an interest in their activities. Until now, the Grand Architect has been like a reflection in water. "She" never appears as her own person, only by the faces of the already dead.
Luuk Herssen: But now, her fascination with what lies "beyond all those infinite stars" is a thread we can pull. We can start identifying which schemes bear her signature.
Luuk Herssen: And the Court of Savantae... since our Grand Architect has taken interest in them before, a trip to Mengzhou may be worth a visit.
Rover: The Court of Savantae was active in Mengzhou?
Luuk Herssen: Just a rumor. They say a city was built there under their direction. There may be clues there.
Luuk Herssen: As for the New Federation, you'll likely end up there eventually if you plan to counter the Fractsidus's operations in the future.
Luuk Herssen: But not now. Things are too complicated over there, and they handle Resonators differently. Even with the Black Shores' backing, going in unprepared would be serious risk.
Rover: I'll be cautious. Before Nivora, did you find any other traces of this Grand Architect in Lahai-Roi?
Luuk Herssen: Yes. There is this one thing. But it's only speculation.
Luuk Herssen: About how Aemeath disappeared, from what you told me, she died from Overclocking trying to stop the Threnodian over a decade ago.
Luuk Herssen: After that incident, the Academy detected cracks on the Threnodian seal in the depths of Bjartr Woods. The damage seemed... intentional.
Rover: You mean...
Luuk Herssen: I believe it was the Grand Architect who damaged the seal. And that led to Aemeath's death.
Rover: ...
Luuk Herssen: Lucilla's people will handle things here now. We should leave, Rover.
Rover: To where?
Luuk Herssen: Let's go clear our minds. You shouldn't sit with this alone.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: Continue onward through the blizzard]
Luuk Herssen: Penny for your thoughts?
Rover: There's too many to count.
Luuk Herssen: Feel like talking about it?
Rover: Maybe a little.
Rover: I keep wondering if the choices I made in the past were the right ones.
Rover: I still don't know why I chose to erase my memories. That one decision cost me my grip on everything. It made me leave so many people behind.
Rover: You, Aemeath, those at the Black Shores, and probably more I don't even know or remember now.
Rover: I pulled everyone into my grand plan to "save the world," and when it mattered most, I wasn't even there.
Rover: If we can't save Aemeath, she'll just be... forgotten. Left to drift in the void forever.
Luuk Herssen: Even if that hadn't happened, your path was always destined to diverge from most of ours.
Luuk Herssen: You know your lifespan is immense. Barring some accident, most of us will leave this world long before you.
Luuk Herssen: Death and goodbyes are a final lesson no one escapes. But for you, it's a question that lingers... for an exceptionally long time.
Rover: You're right.
Luuk Herssen: Since you already know that, you should also see that everyone else has already given their answer.
Luuk Herssen: You're still the same person you were before. Just as resilient. Still bringing hope to others. That's why, after all these years, we're still willing to stand with you.
Luuk Herssen: And it's not because you're a supposed savior. It's because you've always been you.
Luuk Herssen: And... we're not just doing this for you. We're doing it for Solaris. For the future we all chose to fight for.
Luuk Herssen: We chose this path ourselves. You have nothing to feel guilty for.
Luuk Herssen: One can only move forward by making peace with what's lost—You taught me that a long time ago.
Past Luuk Herssen: In the end... I failed to find my father's murderer. I failed to protect Rhein... failed to protect my own family.
Past Rover: But your brother is still alive. You're alive. There's still hope. You did everything you could.
Past Luuk Herssen: Who knows when... I'll wake up next time.
Past Rover: Then we'll make a promise, Luuk.
Past Rover: We'll see each other again next winter. You'll open your eyes, and I'll be standing right here, just like today.
Luuk Herssen: Come now. Enough with that face, Rover. Some candy?
Rover: You always carry candy with you... You sure they really work?
Luuk Herssen: As in?
Rover: "It'll help take the edge off and lighten the mood." Your words.
Luuk Herssen: Ah, that. Honestly, not really. It's become more of a habit of mine.
Luuk Herssen: As a boy, I'd have one whenever things felt too big to handle. The sweetness was a distraction, something to look forward to.
Luuk Herssen: Later, after I inherited , I realized there were still so many things I couldn't control. So I'd eat them to cope, especially when I was up to my neck in trouble thanks to my business associates.
Luuk Herssen: Even after I left the company and set out to follow the Fractsidus's trail on my own, I'd be chewing on one while I watched those who helped me die right in front of me. Still powerless, it seems.
Luuk Herssen: So I've come to believe that no matter how strong a person becomes, not everything can be done perfectly. In life, many things are beyond our control.
Rover: ...
Luuk Herssen: But I still enjoy candy. It reminds me that meeting people is still a gift, even if I know I might lose them one day.
Luuk Herssen: If you let grief and anger burn you out, you become obsessed with results. You forget the joy you felt along the way.
Luuk Herssen: A little sweetness helps keep the numbness at bay.
Rover: I'll have one of your candies.
Luuk Herssen: How does it taste?
Rover: Luuk, my chances of saving Aemeath... They're pretty slim, aren't they?
Luuk Herssen: They are. You'll need a miracle. But you've always been good at making those happen.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Luuk Herssen: They are. You'll need a miracle. But you've always been good at making those happen.



Rover: Thanks for the candy.
Luuk Herssen: You're very welcome.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: (Cat magazine)]
A niche edition of "The Minimalist Approach to Cat Psychology," a magazine that the infirmary has a subscription to.
The subscriber doesn't own a cat. Rumor says he's not even good with them. Others have seen him late at night, holding a copy and staring into space.
It was Rhein, Luuk Herssen's younger brother, who loved this magazine series. The good doctor took over the subscription after him and, even years after leaving home, has never canceled it.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: (Frozen Soil Sample Vial)]
Luuk Herssen gathered this dirt from the "place where he rests."
Few know of its significance, yet Luuk places it in the sunlight every day. No one knows why he studies and measures this frozen mound of dirt that never thaws.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: (First Interaction)]
Luuk Herssen: Rover? What a rare guest. Are you just stopping by... or did you come seeking an old friend?
[Dialogue Option]  I was just stopping by.
[Dialogue Option]  I came to see you.
Luuk Herssen: Your timing couldn't be better. I've just filed the week's medical records and was mulling over what to do next. A book or my student's suggestion—It's sprouting season, you see. Perhaps a stroll would be nice?
[Dialogue Option]  Before coming to the Academy, where did you travel to?
Luuk Herssen: Before this? Quite a few. There was an observatory up north. Freezing cold at night, but the view of the river of stars stretching across the dome was not to be missed for the world.
Luuk Herssen: I also stayed in a coastal city, where salty breezes blew through the year. I learned how to brew wine with golden berries… Unfortunately, it turned out far too sweet for my taste, so I gifted the entire batch to my neighbors instead.
Luuk Herssen: See? You have to see the world before you find your stops.
Luuk Herssen: That's how I feel now. Life at the Academy is peaceful. The students can be a handful sometimes, but I'd never change their vibrant spirits. To be able to share a casual conversation with you like this... I couldn't feel more at home.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm glad to hear that.
Luuk Herssen: Yes... It's a long life. A new season is only beginning. So many possibilities lie ahead, within reach. Sprouting trees, melting snow. Little changes like these... They're signs.
Luuk Herssen: By the way, I'm usually here. Whenever you're tired, bored… or just need someone to talk to, come find me.
Luuk Herssen: After all, even when we're talking about such small nothings, we'd find ourselves healing.
Luuk Herssen: I hope you have a happy, fulfilling day, golden boy.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
[Objective: (Second Interaction)]
Luuk Herssen: Rover? How are you doing? Still busy saving the world?
[Dialogue Option]  I'm doing fine. Not too busy.
Luuk Herssen: That's good to hear. Keeping your own pace matters.
[Dialogue Option]  Too many things on my plate…
Luuk Herssen: Then it sounds like it's time you gave yourself a proper break.
Luuk Herssen: In fact, you're not alone. I meant to tidy up my room once I wrapped up my work… but somehow, one thing after another kept getting in the way.
Luuk Herssen: I suppose that's just life. Plans rarely keep up with change. All we can really do is find a way to breathe comfortably in the spaces between the chaos.

title: All That Sunlight Touches
content:
Novialle Regenerative Group - A pharmaceutical corporation based in the New Federation. Its core technology originates from the development of Ichor, a groundbreaking medical advancement shadowed by perpetual controversy

Ichor - A special pharmaceutical substance developed for extremely rare diseases. However, its severe side effects make it intolerable for most, keeping it under ongoing research and validation. In its natural form, Ichor is a volatile golden liquid that radiates intense heat at room temperature. In rare cases, it can be controlled and stabilized into a solid form.

Abby: The  and riddles… Hm, sounds like a blast!
Abby: Here I was thinkin' we could use this chance to relax, but that Architect guy from the Fractsidus mentioned it too…
Rover:  Yes. The Grand Architect treats everything happening here in Lahai-Roi as a game.
Nivora: Without you, the game in Lahai-Roi would be so boring! So... you get prizes!
Nivora: At the upcoming New Solar Celebration, among all the lovely students... stands a member of the Fractsidus.
Rover:  A Fractsidus agent is hiding among the students, biding their time to strike during the celebration.
Rover:  Maybe that's what President Lucilla wants to discuss.
Abby: Makes sense! But what's with the "one from afar" bit?
Rover:  Probably a riddle.
Rover:  Let's go see the President and find out what she's planning.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
subsection: Enter the dormitory and find Lucilla
content:
[Objective: Enter the dormitory and find Lucilla]
Lucilla:  Mm, I see. I'll count on you, then, Dr. Luuk.
Lucilla:  Ah, Rover's here. I'll brief him on the situation.
Abby: President Lucilla! Whaddya need us for? And what did you mean by "the one from afar who touches 'truth'"?
Lucilla:  Why don't you take a guess? It means exactly what it says.
Rover:  ...The one from afar is me.
Rover:  And the "truth" that reveals the door of dreams is...?
Lucilla:  The "truth" has waited for you here for a very long time.
[Dialogue Option]  That pillow is truth? Seriously?
Lucilla:  You need a good pillow for a good sleep. When it comes to "dreams," that is the absolute truth.
[Dialogue Option]  What's that for? A nice nap?
Lucilla:  Oh, quite. When it comes to "dreams," that is the absolute truth.
Lucilla:  A simple riddle, isn't it?
Abby: Okay... but what's that got to do with us? You didn't call us here to solve a riddle, right?
Lucilla:  You're here because I'd like you to investigate the "." We believe the Grand Architect's next move is tied to it.
[Dialogue Option]  The Academy's Dark Side?
Lucilla:  Think of it as the "Academy's reflection." It's a special Sonoro Sphere formed from the collective emotions of the student body.
Lucilla:  It's an inseparable part of this place, a mirror into the thoughts of every student here... a reflection of their "youth."
Lucilla:  "Youth"... a fascinating concept. So full of ideals and passion, but also anxiety and sorrow.
Lucilla:  The Dark Side absorbs it all, reflecting their truest selves back at them. And that's not all.
Lucilla:  Imagine the Dark Side as a vortex. Negative emotions like anxiety and sorrow form its eye.
Rover:  They swell and collide, seeping into the students' minds. Over time, they come to affect the Academy itself.
Lucilla:  Exactly. It's been troubling the Academy for some time.
Lucilla:  Many of our students were hailed as "geniuses" back home, only to discover they're just one of many here. They've given their all, yet find the peak they once stood upon is now out of reach.
Lucilla:  The Dark Side forces these young minds to face that "truth."
Lucilla:  A harsh reality that can be difficult to accept.
Lucilla:  In the end, the Research Institute found a way to confine the Dark Side within "riddles," turning it into a harmless game that students look forward to each year.
Lucilla:  Solve a riddle, face your problems, and process the emotions festering in the Dark Side. That was the original purpose.
Lucilla:  But recently, something's changed. Dr. Luuk has reported a sharp decline in students' mental states, as if they've been influenced somehow.
Lucilla:  At the same time, I've detected a frequency in the Dark Side that doesn't belong to the Academy. It can't be traced or analyzed.
Lucilla:  We need more information, but we're stretched thin. Between hunting for the Fractsidus agent, the celebration approaching, and dealing with the students' deteriorating mental health, it's not looking good.
Rover:  The Grand Architect intends to create chaos in the Academy to conceal their true objective.
Rover:  Looks like we'll have to investigate the Academy's Dark Side ourselves.
Rover:  So this pillow… is the key to getting in?
Abby: Hehe, I see! This is our starting line!
Lucilla:  Yes. Head in whenever you're ready.
Lucilla:  I'll stay outside and keep in touch.

The monsters beneath the shadows are drawn to the light. Perhaps they are being nourished by it.
Sigrika:  Look at where the student is standing. Hmm, I think I recognize this spot...
Rover:  What's she drawing?
Sigrika:  Runes. This one represents the "sun." It's super important to us Roya.
Sigrika:  The sun blesses the land with its light. Everyone, from the past to the future, gets to bask in its warmth.
Rover:  But this sun seems to be feeding the monsters in the shadows, too.
Rover:  Doesn't that seem wrong?

Sigrika:  Through me, seek the "gift"... seek the...
Sigrika:  ...I've got it!
Sigrika:  I think... it's telling us to find this sun.
Sigrika:  For us (the Roya), the very first rune we ever learn, the most familiar one, is the sun.
Sigrika:  To bathe in the blessing of sunlight is its own kind of inheritance (gift).
Rover:  In other words, finding the sun rune is our way into the Dark Side.
Sigrika:  That's right. It's just like a game I played when I was little.
Sigrika:  The elders of our tribe would hide runes all over Bjartr Woods, each one leading to the next.
Sigrika:  All we had to do was follow the trail to find our way out of the forest.
Sigrika:  And now, the sun is the first rune in our trail!
Sigrika:  To solve this riddle, you're going to need a guide who really knows Royan runes.

[Dialogue Option]  One…
Sigrika:  Say cheese!

Academy's Dark Side - Classroom
Ambition, passion, anxiety, sorrow… the Academy’s Dark Side absorbs them all without distinction, reflecting the student’s rawest and most unguarded thoughts.
If left unchanneled, these accumulated negative emotions gather within the domain, eventually spilling into reality.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Talk to Sigrika]
Do you really believe in yourself? Do others trust you?
Stay here, just stay here... stay with these feelings...
Everything will feel so simple. So simple. So simple...
Rover:  What was that noise...
Sigrika:  I heard it too. Not sure who was speaking, but… it made me feel uncomfortable.
Rover:  Let's head that way and see what's going on.

Sigrika:  Follow me. I’ve been here a few times.
Rover:  …There’s a black hole on the blackboard.
Sigrika:  Oh, that one. It’s proof of all the tired students dozing off during early 8 o’clock lectures.
(Obtained Trophy: Another)

content:

Sigrika:  We can teleport from here now.

metadata.subsection: :This blackboard is just like a black hole… Sucking my brain into it…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Follow Sigrika]
Is that her? One of the successors of the Heliodic Six?
She looks so young. Are the Roya really just going to entrust their future to her…?
Just wait and see how she handles those questions.
Rover:  These are Reflections created by the Dark Side.
Sigrika:  The deepest truths within them… So that's how they see me.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Solve the first riddle]
Gentle Mother:  Come, my sweet Sigrika. Solve this riddle.
Sigrika:  Mother?
Gentle Mother:  Use the ability that brings you such pride. Waiting is the path to your "gift."
Sigrika:  ...
Sigrika:  I never expected to see my mother's  here.
Sigrika:  She's always been proud of me… I won't let her down.
Rover:  Let's take a look at this riddle together then.
Sigrika:  Yes! We should be able to teleport from here. But… the Flow of its True Name is reversed.
Sigrika:  I know… let's try this! This rune can correct it for you!

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Pass through the Switchgate]

Sigrika:  We need to correct them.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: (Idle)]
Sigrika:  Are you alright? Just keep trying to correct it.
Sigrika: That’s it!
Sigrika:  That rune looks similar to the one I saw yesterday.
Sigrika:  I'll go decipher it.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Explore the classroom]
The riddle is solved! I knew you two could do it!
No puzzle can stand against the two of you!
Go for it! I’m rooting for you!
Gentle Mother:  Forward you must go, my child.
Gentle Mother:  Solve all the riddles, and an excellent Solsworn you will become.
Sigrika:  …I understand.
Sigrika:  No matter what the next riddle is, I will solve it.

Sigrika:  I solved it! But why…
Gentle Mother?:  Too slow, Sigrika… You should have done better.
Gentle Mother?:  Are you feeling unwell?
Sigrika:  I…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Defeat the enemies]
Rover:  We've already solved this riddle. Nothing for you here, Tacet Discords.
Sigrika:  So this is what Mother thought when I wasn't good enough.
Sigrika:  I don't want to disappoint her...
Rover:  You are good enough.
Rover:  We've solved the riddles. We already know our next move now.

Excited Friend:  You're finally here, Sigrika! I've been waiting for you!
Rover:  (Nivora… another Reflection tied to Sigrika.)
Sigrika:  Sorry…
Excited Friend:  It's fine, I'm used to it by now. So, figured out your wish yet? Once we crack these last riddles, we can make it come true!

Excited Friend?:  Time's ticking, Sigrika—
Rover:  (These Reflections keep pressuring her.)
Sigrika:  Sorry, I—
Rover:  Don't worry, Sigrika. You're not in this alone.
Sigrika:  Riddle solved!

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Sigrika:  Sorry, I—
Rover:  Don't worry, Sigrika. You're not in this alone.
Sigrika:  Riddle solved!



Excited Friend?:  Still too slow, Sigrika. You spend all your time deciphering runes. When do you ever have time for us...
Excited Friend?:  Or is it that you don't even have a wish? Is that why you can't focus?
Sigrika:  I'm sorry… I'll try to be faster…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: (Defeat the enemies)]
Rover:  Breathe, Sigrika.
Sigrika:  I am breathing. I just... if I can adjust the resonance equations, I can speed this up. Then the Tacet Discords won't show up, and I—
Rover:  Even if they do, we'll deal with them together.
Sigrika:  But Mother and Nivora… I'm letting them down.
Sigrika:  If that's what they really think of me, then I have to—
Rover:  It doesn't matter. They're only Reflections born of the Dark Side.
Rover:  They've been targeting you from the start. Don't give them what they want.
Rover:  See? The path is still forming, even with the Tacet Discords here.
Rover:  That proves we're on the right track.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Follow Sigrika]
Serious Senior:  With your gifts, you should be much faster than this...
Sigrika:  ...
Serious Senior:  Sigrika... You can do it...
Sigrika: Faster this time... I have to be faster...
Sigrika:  Yes, Sigrika, you can do this. These runes won't beat you...

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Remove the disruptive Runes]
Sigrika:  Why are the runes interrupted... Am I too slow?
Sigrika:  I need to clear the interruptions. But how should I do it...
Rover:  I can help. It seems we can smash down from mid-air to clear the interruptions.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
subsection: Use the Gravity Grapple Rune to alter gravity
content:
[Objective: Use the Gravity Grapple Rune to alter gravity]

subsection: Use Plunging Attacks to remove the disruptive Runes
content:
[Objective: Use Plunging Attacks to remove the disruptive Runes]
Sigrika:  By the Flow of their True Name... I will make this path!
Excited Friend?:  Are you sure you can?
Gentle Mother?:  You're pushing yourself too hard, my dear…
Serious Senior?:  Do not waste your gifts.

(Cutscene plays)
Sigrika:  …Ugh!
Sigrika:  Are you alright, Senior?
Sigrika:  Did you get hurt?
(Cutscene ends)
Rover:  I'm fine. Are you?
Sigrika:  I'm okay… but why did the rune explode? I… I lost control…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Solve the last riddle]
Excited Friend?:  Hmph... It's already the final riddle. Your last chance to prove yourself...
Serious Senior?:  Tell me, what does a gift, or an endowment, mean to the Roya? I want to hear your answer.
Gentle Mother?:  You can do this, my sweet child...
Sigrika:  Hm... the answer is...
[Dialogue Option]  I believe in you.
[Dialogue Option]  Just follow your heart.
Sigrika:  To us Roya, the sun is an endowment. For me, the sun is also the first rune I ever learned.
Sigrika:  So it has to be the key to unlocking any gift.
Sigrika:  That's it. I believe in my choice.
Sigrika:  The answer... is the sun.
Sigrika:  It's wrong? But why...?
A Voice That Doesn't Belong Here: A child who fails does not get to leave.
Rover:  That voice again.
A Voice That Doesn't Belong Here: Sorrow, disappointment, self-doubt... Why do you still keep going...
Sigrika:  No... my runes! They're not responding?!
Rover:  Our attacks are useless. It's feeding on the surrounding energy!
Lucilla:  There you are.
???: See? My little pet performed wonderfully, don't you think?
???:  So, Rover, what will you do with all these emotions?
???:  I'll be watching. I'm going to cherish every second... of the time you've bought me.
speakers: A Voice That Doesn't Belong Here
A Voice That Doesn't Belong Here

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
???:  So, Rover, what will you do with all these emotions?
???:  I'll be watching. I'm going to cherish every second... of the time you've bought me.



Luuk Herssen:  All clear. No lasting harm. If the runes didn't answer, it's likely because your heart wasn't quite in the right place to call them.
Luuk Herssen:  Do you still remember what I told you last time, Sigrika?
Sigrika:  You said I should have more faith in myself.
Luuk Herssen:  And not to push yourself too hard. Here, have a candy.
Rover:  That song we heard… it felt nostalgic.
Lucilla:  You liked it?
[Dialogue Option]  It was beautiful.
[Dialogue Option]  It was effective.
Lucilla:  Fleet Snowfluff's songs always do bring a little warmth to the soul.
Rover:  Aemeath...
Lucilla:  When we tried to enter the Dark Side to help you, we found our frequencies denied. That thing hijacked it. Only students were allowed in.
Lucilla:  So we had to get creative. Luckily, it can't control the emotions already inside.
Lucilla:  Every emotion leaves a mark. The fan meeting you held not long ago left the students with plenty of happy memories. That song helped guide you right through that thing's blockade.
Sigrika:  It's no ordinary Tacet Discord. What exactly is that thing?
Sigrika:  I want to know what I saw in there.
Sigrika:  Please trust me, Professor… and you too, Senior. I really want to help.
[Dialogue Option]  Let’s share what we know so far.
[Dialogue Option]  We need the full picture to act.
Lucilla:  What we can confirm is that the Tacet Discord was sent by the Fractsidus.
Sigrika:  The Fractsidus?
Rover:  Their Grand Architect tipped us off about their plans in Lahai-Roi, that he will play a game with us.
Luuk Herssen:  It seems the "game" she referred to is this riddle event our students are so fond of.
Luuk Herssen:  We've already tracked the participants. The effects of these riddles are already spilling into their real lives.
Luuk Herssen:  Some abandoned their research projects. Others are lashing out at classmates... and a few have lost control entirely.
Luuk Herssen:  These students have all become pawns in the Fractsidus's little show.
Rover:  You're one of them, Sigrika.
Sigrika:  Me?
Rover:  Those riddles and Tacet Discords we encountered in the Dark Side were clearly targeting you.
Rover:  I thought you might've been linked to the recent disturbances, but now I see you're just another victim.
Sigrika:  What kind of game would do something like this?! We have to stop it. I can help you solve these strange riddles.
Sigrika:  Professor, Senior, please let me...
Lucilla:  You need to rest, Sigrika.
Sigrika:  Why? Because I'm not good enough?
Lucilla:  Because it's dangerous.
Lucilla:  I see how determined you are. But I won't risk my students' safety.
[Dialogue Option]  (Comfort her.)
Rover:  Just take it easy for now, Sigrika.
[Dialogue Option]  (Support Lucilla.)
Rover:  The President is right. The Dark Side is too volatile right now. Just take it easy.
Sigrika:  Senior...
Sigrika:  ...I see.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Rover:  The President is right. The Dark Side is too volatile right now. Just take it easy.
Sigrika:  Senior...
Sigrika:  ...I see.



Luuk Herssen:  I still think we should let her in on our plan. You know how desperately that girl craves validation.
Lucilla:  We can. But not while she's like this.
Lucilla:  You once said she lacks confidence, Dr. Luuk.
Lucilla:  From where I'm standing, she has too much of it.
Lucilla:  I see that she's a fighter. She believes she's capable of living up to everyone's expectations.
Lucilla:  Or rather, she thinks she must. She may as well be walking a tightrope.
Lucilla:  I've seen many students like her.
Lucilla:  Every single one believed they could always be the best. That failure wasn't an option. So they pushed, and pushed…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Lucilla:  Every single one believed they could always be the best. That failure wasn't an option. So they pushed, and pushed…



Lucilla:  Remember that student I mentioned, Rover? The one with the flawed but brilliant hypotheses?
Lucilla:  She didn't just leave Startorch Academy.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Lucilla:  She didn't just leave Startorch Academy.



Lucilla:  The Academy... lost her for good.
Lucilla:  She lost her balance on that wire.
Lucilla:  That is exactly what the Fractsidus wants to dig their claws into.
Denia:  Here you are, Siggy. Where's that new friend of yours? Let me guess... they're off planning something big, but didn't want you in on it?
Sigrika:  I just wasn't good enough.
Denia:  Here. Dusk Honeypot flavor. I know it's your favorite.
Denia:  What if we just dropped the whole riddle thing? Or... is it about proving worthy of being a future Heliodic Six successor?
Sigrika:  I just... don't want to let anyone down.
Lucilla:  Every single student came to the Academy with a heart full of promise.
Lucilla:  That promise is what keeps this Academy standing.
Luuk Herssen:  We will not sit back and watch the Fractsidus exploit that. And let's not forget, the knowledge these students hold can shape the future of Lahai-Roi itself.
Rover:  Which means we're in a race against time. That Tacet Discord was feeding on energy. If the Dark Side is a vortex of emotion, then that thing is the eye of the storm.
Rover:  We have to find it.
Lucilla:  You may want to stock up on the candy, Dr. Luuk.
Luuk Herssen:  Can I apply for reimbursement?
Luuk Herssen:  Anyway, Rover, just get some rest. We'll keep an eye on the Dark Side.
Luuk Herssen:  Don't worry. This game won't end the way the Fractsidus intends.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Luuk Herssen:  Don't worry. This game won't end the way the Fractsidus intends.



For now, things have settled. While you wait for the next riddle, you've got some "free time" to yourself.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
subsection: Go participate in the New Solar Celebration
content:
[Objective: Go participate in the New Solar Celebration]
Sigrika:  Senior, you're here!
Sigrika:  I bought this for you. As a thank-you for your help lately.
Sigrika:  Here, it's all yours!
[Dialogue Option]  This is…
[Dialogue Option]  …Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks?
Sigrika:  That's right! This one is made specially for the New Solar Celebration. I had to wait in line forever to get it.
Sigrika:  You never know what funny effect you're going to get! It's different each time. But it's supposed to help with relaxing.
Sigrika: Go on, give it a try!
[Dialogue Option]  (Take one boldly.)
Rover:  …It actually tastes pretty good. Wait—is that my voice?!
[Dialogue Option]  (Take one hesitantly.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Return it to Sigrika.)
Sigrika:  Are you sure? Oh, look—a big rabbit over there!
Rover:  Rabbit—?
[Sigrika pops a candy into Rover's mouth.]
Sigrika:  Can this really be?!
Sigrika:  Let me try one too...
Sigrika:  This one… tastes kind of weird—hic! Oh no—no, I wasn't—hic! Excuse me!
Sigrika:  I have lungs, not gills—hic!
Sigrika:  I—I can't—hic—make it stop!
Rover:  ...
Rover:  Abby.
Abby: Huh? Think you can just summon—Hey, what did ya just give me—?!
Abby: Chuuu?!
Sigrika:  Hic—you sound like a Soliskin now!
Sigrika:  This is so much fun! Maybe we should share them with others too!

metadata.subsection: Go participate in the New Solar Celebration

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: Find Denia]
Sigrika:  Hic… Don’t worry, it won’t last long and—hic!
Rover:  I’m okay. But you’d better take it easy…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
Denia:  ...If you're looking for a particular stall, find Lynae. If you're hurt, call N.A.N.A. If you lost something, bother that one running around in computers. Just don't bother me, kay?
Sigrika:  But I'm here for you, Nia—hic!
Denia:  Give me a break, Siggy. Can't a girl just enjoy the fresh air on a beautiful, class-free morning?
Denia:  Oh, never mind. Your... excessive cheerfulness just ruined the vibe. Surprised you bounced back so fast. What do you want?
Sigrika:  We want to—hic!
Denia:  ...Do you want some water?
Rover:  Sigrika wants you to try this.
Denia:  Why does your voice sound like that?
Sigrika:  Just try it, Denia! Please?
Denia:  …I refuse. The last time I tried your candy, I was shooting rainbow beams out of my eyes and mouth for four minutes and thirty-five seconds.
Sigrika:  That was a research sample! This is real! Just trust me and try—hic!
Denia:  Case in point. Can someone just solve the riddle of who made these strange candies in the first place?
Denia:  If you must find someone to try it, look for Lynae. She'd probably love this stuff. Here, take your tickets.
Denia:  Now shoo. See you.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
subsection: Walk around the venue to see if you can meet your friends
content:
[Objective: Walk around the venue to see if you can meet your friends]
Lynae: Hi, Rover! Hi, Sigrika!
Sigrika:  Hello, Lynae—Hic!
Lynae: Why are you hiccuping, Sigrika?
Rover:  We just had some Rainbow Bean Pop Rocks. Want to try?
Lynae: No way! Your voice is totally different! Gimme one, I gotta try this!
Lynae takes the candy under your watchful eyes.
Lynae: Oh, that's "awful"!
Lynae: Wait, that "is" what I meant...? Everything is "the same as" what I want to say... Huh?
Rover:  It's making you say the opposite of what you're trying to say...
Lynae: Hahaha! This is "not" interesting, how "boring" is this!
Lynae: Oh, by the way, how's that thing from the other day going?
[Dialogue Option]  Still working on it.
[Dialogue Option]  I’ll make sure it gets handled.
Lynae: Aha, so you're taking a break, huh?
Lynae: In that case, you need to take a "bad" rest! Here, I "don't think you should " try this game I co-developed. We "shouldn't" play ten rounds!
Sigrika:  I want to try it! What do you say?
[Dialogue Option]  Tend rounds it is!
Lynae: Raiding time!!!
[Dialogue Option]  I’m good. You two play it.
Lynae: Alright. It's gaming time, Sigrika!
You watch them play. Lynae's hands fly across the screen with ease, while Sigrika scrambles to keep up. It's a welcome moment of peace.
Lynae: Phew, I always "hate" playing games.
Lynae: Ahem, I mean... Never mind. You know what I was trying to say.
Sigrika:  You can't talk normally, Lynae.
Sigrika:  But don't worry, the effect won't last long. I've already stopped hiccuping.
Lynae: "It's not okay," talking like this is actually really "boring." I'm having a "terrible" time!
Lynae: …I'll wait for it to wear off before I say anything else.
Lynae: By the way, do you still have any candies left?
Sigrika:  Of course! I bought plenty. Here.
Lynae: Thanks! This candy is "the worst." I want some other people to try it too, you know, share the "frowns"!
Lynae: Have a "bad" day, you two!
Sigrika:  We will. Enjoy your day!

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
subsection: Talk to Lynae invested in the Game
content:
Sigrika:  Have a "bad" day... Have a good day...
Sigrika:  Different words, but you can tell what she means. I guess it's because Lynae always speaks from the heart.
Sigrika:  That's really nice.
Rover:  So? Did you have a good day?
Sigrika:  Hm? Your voice is back to normal.
Sigrika:  Well, I guess I had quite a "terrible" rest.
Sigrika:  Everyone's enjoying the celebration.
Sigrika:  When I close my eyes, I can hear all kinds of voices around me.
Sigrika:  Vendors calling out new kinds of Pop Rocks, students cheering about new records...
Sigrika:  Some are singing, others are just laughing... It's so nice.
Sigrika:  But... besides all that, I still hear other voices.
Sigrika:  The ones from the Dark Side, when I let everyone down... they made me feel so lost.
Sigrika:  After we got out, you told me to walk away. For my own safety.
Sigrika:  But when I was alone, I remembered all the encouraging things people have always said to me.
Sigrika:  "You're going to do great things." "You can solve any riddle." "You can do it." "You can prove yourself"...
Sigrika:  Their words shone like molten gold. So radiant, and so... warm.
Sigrika:  I don't want to be the one to drop them.
Sigrika:  So many voices... When you hear so many voices in your head, Senior, what do you do?
[Dialogue Option]  I listen to what my own heart is saying.
Sigrika:  Hehe, I like that. The voice of my heart... I've never thought of that before.
[Dialogue Option]  I try to live up to their expectations.
Sigrika:  Right... Living up to their expectations!
Rover:  But sometimes, you don't need to overthink what you do.
Sigrika:  Don't overthink what to do… So you mean just—
Rover:  Just do it.
Sigrika:  ...
Lucilla:  We have an emergency, Rover. Multiple students are trapped in the Dark Side.
Lucilla:  I've already sent the coordinates.
Rover:  The Fractsidus are making their move. The situation is serious.
Sigrika:  I'm coming with you.
Rover:  Alright. Let's go.

metadata.subsection: Talk to Lynae invested in the Game

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: (Idle)]
Is that President Lucilla? What happened?
Heard someone went missing. Ha… I really hope everything’s alright.

She was right there in front of me, and then she just… Ngh…
Don’t worry, the professors will sort this out.

This has never happened before. I’ve got a bad feeling about this.
Like a gut feeling?! Well, let’s just steer clear of riddles for now then…

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
This has never happened before. I’ve got a bad feeling about this.
Like a gut feeling?! Well, let’s just steer clear of riddles for now then…



Lucilla:  Good, you're here, Rover. And... Sigrika.
Sigrika:  Professor Lucilla...
Lucilla:  I know you want to prove yourself. But in your current state, I'm afraid I can't authorize it.
Lucilla:  You must understand how dangerous this mission is. Our enemies hide in the dark, and we still don't know that Tacet Discord's weakness.
Sigrika:  No, Professor. Please let me join.
Sigrika:  I know you're worried, but I know the Dark Side better than anyone. How can I stand by when my classmates are trapped in there?
Sigrika:  I can help you decipher the runes. I can be useful.
Sigrika:  This isn't about proving myself anymore. It's about doing what's right.
[Dialogue Option]  She’s made up her mind.
[Dialogue Option]  She can contribute to the mission.
Lucilla:  These are the students whose signals vanished while in the Dark Side.
Rover:  Chisa...? She's trapped in there too?
Sigrika:  And also Isla?! Why would she...
Lucilla:  They were all in the dormitory hall. Someone must have activated a riddle, and the Dark Side pulled everyone in.
Lucilla:  Mornye is already on it. I have her searching for the students' locations.
Lucilla:  And this is what I found.

title: Gold Suspended in Shadows
content:
[Objective: (Inspect item)]
The girl in the picture cradles the runes. The runes radiate light.
A line of tiny glyphs.
Yet she is bound by chains. Is this light a blessing or a curse?
Sigrika:  Another runic riddle.
Rover:  "Receive the sunlight's blessing"... What could it mean?
Sigrika:  It's referring to our rite of passage.
Sigrika:  When a Roya is deemed ready to bear the tribe's expectations, we go to the Reactor Drive to be Imprinted.
Sigrika:  The Drive leaves markings on our bodies. It is a blessing for the next stage of our lives.
Sigrika:  See these? They are the sunlight's Imprints.
[Dialogue Option]  So… you’re already considered an adult?
Sigrika:  Yes! Three years ahead of schedule. Impressive, right?
Lucilla:  The Roya value the gifted and the strong. Adulthood is defined by passing the Imprinting Trial. It's a rite of great importance.
Sigrika:  Yes, it's true. I still remember how thrilled I was the night before my Imprinting.
Sigrika:  "I will be an adult." "Does that mean everything will finally come easier?"
Sigrika:  I wonder if the girl in this picture thought the same. But it doesn't look like she's receiving a blessing... more like she's being chained by it.
Sigrika:  What is the person who made this riddle trying to say?
Lucilla:  Check the back.
[Dialogue Option]  (Flip it over.)
Rover:  (Just as I thought, there's something written on the back.)
Sigrika:  "Don't think, don't look. To escape from emotion, one must break the chains of expectation."
Rover:  "The chains of expectation"... That fits the picture. What if this rune is another ticket into the Dark Side?
Rover:  Sigrika, can you decipher it and find the entrance?
Sigrika:  No problem.
Rover:  Then we're going in and bringing everyone back.
Lucilla:  Wait.

Isla: I don't have to think. I don't have to look at anything.
Isla: You saw it, right? The projects, the assignments... an endless chain. One after another after another.
Isla: I'm so tired of it all.
Isla: I keep asking myself, why does it all have to fall on me?
Isla: "You're so capable." "You're so important." "You're so talented." "You can handle it." Blah, blah, blah... How am I supposed to be all of that at once?
Isla: Hey, I'm talking to you... "future Heliodic Six successor." You hear those voices too, don't you? So tell me. What's your answer?
Sigrika:  ...I will live up to everyone's expectations.

Isla: How do you expect to keep living up to everyone's expectations, Sigrika?
Isla: I've been meaning to ask you. As a future Heliodic Six successor, you're expected to attend all classes, research every rune, and calculate the sun's path… Don't you ever get tired?
Isla: And then I saw you in the Dark Side.

Isla: Sorrow, disappointment, self-doubt… Those emotions didn't just fade away, even after passing the Imprinting Trial. And when everyone's expectations keep piling up, higher and higher… they start feeling like heavy chains.
Isla: I heard you say it. You said you wished you could let it all go.

Isla: Why are you trying to drag me back? Answer me. All these chains... how do you intend to break them?!
Sigrika:  ...What's the right thing to do? I...
Rover:  There's no perfect answer to that.

Oh, Heliodic Six successor
surely you've heard this story before.
Long ago, the children of Bjartr Woods played an interesting game.
The elders strung runes into chains of stars
turning the forest into a maze of riddles.
“Each rune leads to the next.”
“Find the first, and you'll know where to find the next.”
In the end, one girl made it through the forest.
The applause washed over her—
Your friend said you could pluck the stars hidden within runes
and forge their frequencies into gold.
Your mother said you would bathe in the blessing of sunlight early
that the Imprints were proof of your gift.
So you kept drawing those runes, again and again
pushing yourself to always be the best.

Our future Heliodic Six successor!
