Lucilla (Actress): Our home world, see? Just a pale blue dot.
Arrogant Student: So what's the point?
Lucilla (Actress): Excuse me?
Arrogant Student: I mean, what's the point of taking that photo? Looking at it only makes us feel small.
Arrogant Student: That tiny dot only makes all of us on it feel more insignificant, pathetic even. That so-called golden age of exploration and the great astronomy before the Lament... All they bring is loneliness.
Arrogant Student: We're all lonely in that endless darkness, just like Startorch Academy now. Tell me, Professor, does our so-called "exploration" here even matter?
Lucilla (Actress): I... I don't know...
Hah. First time I've ever seen you speechless, Professor.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
Lucilla (Actress): I... I don't know...
Hah. First time I've ever seen you speechless, Professor.



Stern Professor: About your request, I have the right to reject it.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Talk to the Stern Professor]
Stern Professor: Absurd! You want to withdraw now, at the most critical stage of the experiment? Who could possibly take your place?
Lucilla (Actress): I-I'm just... scared. Scared to touch those instruments again. Scared of seeing results that don't match what we hoped for.
Stern Professor: Afraid of the risks? Then switch to theoretical work! Are you really going to let everything you've built amount to nothing?

Resident: Professor Lucilla just ran out of the room, clutching her head... like she's lost it.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: What are they looking at?]
Stern Professor: How long has she been locking herself in there?
Arrogant Student: No clue. We just heard stuff breaking... and someone crying.
Worried Student: Could it be... she's having another episode?
Worried Student: The madness caused by memory confusion...

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
subsection: Return to the room on the other side of the window
content:
[Objective: Return to the room on the other side of the window]
Stern Professor: Are you really quitting the project, Lucilla? You've made up your mind?
Lucilla: ...Yes.

metadata.subsection: Return to the room on the other side of the window

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Keep exploring]
This will be my final lecture. I've already filed to close the course next term.
Thank you all for your support. I've gone as far as I can.
I'm sure you'll all go farther than I ever could...

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Approach "her"]
???: She said nothing. Deep down, she'd already accepted her own mediocrity... and stopped moving forward.
???: The girl who once forced herself to stand tall now teeters on the edge. Her curtain's about to fall.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
???: The girl who once forced herself to stand tall now teeters on the edge. Her curtain's about to fall.



Lucilla (Actress): Hah... Did the others' memories bleed into mine again? How long was I out? The meeting's already over...
Lucilla (Actress): What's happening to me... I just want to forget. To erase this wretched Forte.
Lucilla (Actress): Erase... right. If I erase the memory of my Forte itself, maybe then, everything will go back to normal.
Lucilla (Actress): I'm done with all of it.
Stern Professor: She abandoned her title, her right to explore, and now even her own Forte.
Sevi (Dark Side): She chose to kill the person she used to be, like someone who had drowned, losing both her air and shadow.
Arrogant Student: A different choice, a brand-new life. Tell me, our dear audience, isn't this fascinating?
Arrogant Student: If everything's destined to fade away, why not just wait it out? Enjoy the last bit of pleasure and revel in the beautiful memories before the end.
Sevi (Dark Side): After all, fleeting joy feels far more real than some unreachable truth.
Cheerful Student: You only need to come a little closer, and take my hand.
Cheerful Student: Our lives can trade places. No more pain, only warmth and bliss. The curtain's about to fall, and the choice is yours.
Lucilla: Done with your performance?
Lucilla: All that noise for one purpose, the same trick you used on Sevi. Stirring fear, pressing old wounds.
Lucilla: Let me guess what you're after. Targeting Sigrika was just a diversion. You wanted the Academy to intervene.
Lucilla: Next, the memory-type Resonators affected in the Dark Side, and you knew I'd see it. That was your invitation.
Lucilla: So this little play? It was meant for me and all the memory-type Resonators. You're afraid of something in us, aren't you? Something that threatens your grand scheme.
Lucilla: You put on quite a hilarious show, I'll give you that. But you came to the wrong audience. You can ramble about pasts and futures all you like, but I only focus on the present.
Lucilla: And that's exactly why your "message" in that film disgusts me.
Lucilla: I don't deny the doubt, the struggle, or the pain we face in our search. Every soul in Startorch Academy has endured those.
Lucilla: But the weight of civilization demands shoulders to bear it. And we, right from the beginning, are a flock walking willingly toward our own end.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
Lucilla: If the campfire's dying out, then these lambs you mock will burn themselves, just to walk one more mile before the final breath.
Lucilla: No glory sought. No remembrance needed. We'll lie down here, leaving not a trace.
Lucilla (Actress): But what's the point of it all?!
Lucilla: The point? You who watch us burn... You're the proof. You, and everyone behind you, that's our meaning.
Lucilla: And one more thing. Whether I deserve to be the President... That's not for your cheap words or your lousy films to decide.
Lucilla: If you're so desperate to tear me down, that only proves I'm doing something right.
Lucilla: Tell me, who's the real desperate one here?
Lucilla: Hehe, you're not the only one with backup. Checkmate.

(Cutscene plays)
Lucilla: You're here.
Hiyuki: Go after it. I'll handle the rest.
Lucilla: Come on. We've still got work to do.
(Cutscene ends)

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Follow Lucilla to explore ahead]
Lucilla: Stay sharp, Rover. It can take the form of anything in the Dark Side.
Lucilla: There's only one passage here. It must still be around. Stay close.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Talk to Lucilla]
Lucilla: No sign of it here either. Rover, let's split up.
Lucilla: I'll check this room. You take the one before.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Return to the meeting room]
Lucilla stands on the otherside of the window, but she's not acting like her usual self...
[Dialogue Option]

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
Lucilla: Told you... It's checkmate this time.
[Dialogue Option]  According to our plan...
[Dialogue Option]  Should we...
Lucilla: Hmm... We still haven't figured out what the Fractsidus wants with the Dark Side.
Lucilla: For now, this little one's our only lead. Let me try reading its memory first.
Lucilla: Oh? Looks like I don't even need to use my Forte.
I suppose this counts as our first proper meeting, Madam Lucilla?
Lucilla: Proper meeting? You're talking to me through a rabbit from your little hideout. That's what you call "proper"?
Lucilla: Still... thanks for the film. It was tasteless and trashy, but I'll admit, it added a little fun to my job.
Lucilla: You knew I'd catch this rabbit from the start.
Strange Rabbit: And didn't you already know it was a trap meant for you? We both have what the other wants.
Lucilla: What are you trying to do in Lahai-Roi?
Strange Rabbit: Uh-uh. As an educator, you of all people should know better. Finding the answer is the asker's job, you know.
Strange Rabbit: Still... congratulations. You've won this round.
Lucilla: Won? I never agreed to play your little game. And neither did my students. Right, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  That's right!
[Dialogue Option]  You're just flattering yourself!
Strange Rabbit: Flattering myself? That hurts. I worked very hard setting up those trials for you.
Strange Rabbit: If you didn't enjoy them, don't worry. There'll be a next round. And I promise, it'll be far more thrilling.
Strange Rabbit: Because next time, we'll be betting on the very fate of Lahai-Roi. Will it go boom and vanish... or will the flames of Startorch keep burning?
Strange Rabbit: I can't wait. Truly... I can't wait for our next meeting.
Lucilla: Next meeting...
[Dialogue Option]  We almost had it...
Lucilla: It's alright. At least we dealt with the source of the Dark Side's anomaly.
[Dialogue Option]  Who's the miko just now?
Lucilla: I know you've got many questions, but let's get out of here first.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Dialogue Option]  Who's the miko just now?
Lucilla: I know you've got many questions, but let's get out of here first.



Denia: You said the things in the Dark Side wouldn't hurt them.
Nivora: Didn't I do what you asked? You wanted to help Sigrika, so I tweaked the Dark Side to help her see herself clearly.
Nivora: Besides… no one got hurt, right? Your friend, your teacher… and Rover.
Nivora: I should thank you, actually. You helped me finish an experiment…
Denia: Experiment?
Nivora: The opposite of the void… How far can memory-type Resonators go before "its" power consumes them?
Nivora: And what other tricks is this petty Academy hiding?
Nivora: A miko wielding a sword, hehe…
Nivora: Come, my sweet darling. We've still got much to do.
Denia: What about the rabbit? Isn't it your pet?
Nivora: We don't keep trash. We dump it.
Nivora: So… please try hard to be useful, if you don't want to be disposable.

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
Nivora: We don't keep trash. We dump it.
Nivora: So… please try hard to be useful, if you don't want to be disposable.



Lucilla: Sorry, Rover. I've kept you busy all day.
[Dialogue Option]  You do owe me an apology.
[Dialogue Option]  But not for that.
Rover: From the moment you came to me, you already knew this was a trap set by the Fractsidus. Yet, you planned to walk right into it.
Lucilla: All in a day's work for your President. Besides... it worked out pretty well, don't you think?
[Dialogue Option]  But what if something had gone wrong?
Lucilla: Don't worry. I know the Dark Side pulls people toward what they fear and try to escape from. But I learned to face my past honestly long ago.
[Dialogue Option]  Then… what exactly happened to you back there?
Lucilla: You want to know?
Rover: Didn't you say you wanted to introduce a new course, Startorch Guidelines: From Strangers to Confidants?
Rover: Students and teachers should get to know each other, right? Maybe this counts as our first class.
Lucilla: Sigh... I really set myself up for that one. Well...
Lucilla: Before I turned twenty, I couldn't tell which memories were mine and which belonged to the ones I had read.
Lucilla: As I absorbed more and more of them, I saw too many births and deaths… I started to feel how small and ignorant I really was.
Lucilla: That's exactly what the Dark Side preyed on. It then recreated the predicament I once lived through. The Fractsidus was questioning me, the representative of Startorch Academy…
Lucilla: "When the future offers no answers, and existence itself is destined to fade… can anything we do, in our brief and ignorant lives, truly matter?
Lucilla: As a student of Startorch Academy, what do you think, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  If there's no answer, then we create one.
Lucilla: Haha, that's the kind of answer you'd say.
Lucilla: Back then, I joined the Spacetrek Collective without a real purpose, but luckily, just like you, I met a good teacher.
Lucilla: My teacher was an ordinary man, a Roya in charge of observation in the frostlands. We both spent our days watching and recording, each in our own realm…
Lucilla: But he never saw himself as just an observer. Again and again, he made connections with people and the things he studied and built bridges between them.
Lucilla: It was like how we draw lines between the stars now. In these perilous frostlands, each person is a point of light for another.
Lucilla: Maybe I used to stand too high, never stooping to feel the emotions in those memories… the ones that needed time to settle for an ordinary person.
Lucilla: When I revisited the memories I once read, I realized they all shared one thing in common—everyone spends their whole life searching for answers.
Lucilla: And it's those very answers that give meaning to our journey toward the future, even if we might find nothing in the end.
[Dialogue Option]  Then, have you found your answers?
Lucilla: No… I'm still searching. In that sense, I'm the same as all of you, just another student on the path.
Lucilla: So don't worry. Until I find it, the Fractsidus won't be able to shake me. Also, about that miko lady you're curious about…
Lucilla: My lips are sealed on that, I'm afraid. A President has her principles, not to mention the Academy's safety protocol. But one day, you'll see her again.
Lucilla: Anyway, I still have to write a full report on the Dark Side. Leave the rest to the adults now. It's getting late, Rover. I'll see you in class.
Lucilla: …Has this game truly ended?
(Quest complete: Rabbit Reflected in Shades)

title: Rabbit Reflected in Shades
content:
[Objective: Talk to Lucilla]
Lucilla: Hmm? Still something you want to say?
[Dialogue Option]  I'd like to hear more about your past.
Lucilla: Oh? But Startorch Guidelines: From Strangers to Confidants is designed for both teachers and students, isn't it?
Lucilla: If you want to hear mine, you'll have to share your stories before coming to Lahai-Roi first.
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell her part of your story in Jinzhou)
You tell Lucilla part of your story in Jinzhou. She nods occasionally, respectful of the people there.
Lucilla: People everywhere are protecting their homes in their own ways. The Fractsidus's claim that it's all meaningless is the greatest insult to our era.
Lucilla: And your pen pal sounds like a sincere, kind girl. It's a blessing, in times like these, to have someone you can truly talk to.
[Dialogue Option]  I hope I get to meet her again.
Lucilla: You will. Human connections are stronger than you think.
[Dialogue Option]  (Tell her part of your story in Rinascita)
You tell Lucilla part of your story in Rinascita. Curiosity flickers in her eyes.
Lucilla: I've only read about Rinascita in textbooks. Their culture of living alongside Echoes reminds me a bit of the Roya.
Lucilla: If I ever get the chance, I'd love to visit there and hear their bards perform in person.
Lucilla: All right, since you shared, I'll tell you something you wanted to know. Let's start with my Royan teacher.
Lucilla: During an expedition in the frostlands, I got caught in a storm and was separated from the others. Due to my chaotic memories, I barely understood the concept of death.
Lucilla: An old Royan observer rescued me and brought me back to his outpost.
Lucilla: When he learned of my ability, he asked me to help him recall the memories he'd long forgotten.
Lucilla: In that small cabin, I read the joys and sorrows of his past.
Lucilla: He studied the behavior of Exoswarm alone, danced the Royan dances there, and shared laughter with passing researchers.
Lucilla: He was never lonely. I began to follow his example and actively reached out to the memories I once read. I wanted to show my respect and experience them anew.
Lucilla: Guess what I felt then?
[Dialogue Option]  Awakening?
Lucilla: No. It was the fear of death… For the first time, I truly feared death. I felt their most genuine human emotions facing the jaws of death.
Lucilla: When I realized that, I knew I was finally waking up from the nightmare of those memories.

title: The Flaming Red from Tomorrow
content: Completing the quest awards the Rover's Journey III Trophy The Danger Within.

title: The Flaming Red from Tomorrow
content: Quest Objective: After the Dark Side incident comes to an end, Lucilla meets with Hiyuki at the auditorium. Lucilla suspects that the Fractsidus may be plotting something far more dangerous behind the scenes…

title: The Flaming Red from Tomorrow
content:
[Objective: Head to the auditorium]
Lucilla: It's just the two of us now. No need for all the formality, Hiyuki.
Lucilla: Oh, and just so you know, the maintenance fee for that blade will be coming out of your paycheck this month.
Hiyuki: Which blade?
Lucilla: The one you used in the Dark Side. That makes it the fourth you've broken so far. Try to be gentler the next time, will you?
Hiyuki: Sure. What about my own sword?
Lucilla: Its maintenance is mostly done. Don't worry, you'll have it back soon.
Lucilla: Want to try one? It's pretty popular among the students.
Hiyuki: Not hungry.
Lucilla: Candy's supposed to be eaten when you're not hungry. That's what makes it taste good. Go on, try it.
Lucilla: Have you swallowed it?
Hiyuki: Umm-hmm. A bit sour… and my tongue's tingling. Not my favorite.
Lucilla: Huh? No reaction at all? That's odd. When Sigrika and the others ate theirs, they…
Hiyuki: What?
Lucilla: You're no fun.
Hiyuki: He saw me. Does that affect your plan?
Lucilla: It's fine. The Fractsidus didn't just set the trap for me. It was meant to draw you out as well.
Lucilla: They've noticed your existence.
Lucilla: I'm sorry for keeping you confined… for trying to hide your power. In the end, it still came to light.
Hiyuki: We both knew this day would come sooner or later.
Lucilla: So… would you consider moving back to the Academy for now? If anything happens, you can respond right away.
Lucilla: The Fractsidus went to great lengths to tamper with the Dark Side, but it poses little actual threat to the Academy.
Lucilla: At worst, this anomaly might be tied to the power of the Threnodian, too. It seems they're already preparing their next phase.
Hiyuki: What do you need me to do?
Lucilla: Now's not the time.
Lucilla: You should know that the Spacetrek Collective was built atop the Threnodian. That's why we've prepared countless contingency plans.
Lucilla: Even if every single one failed… even if the Threnodian completely consumed the Collective, we still have a final card to play.
Lucilla: The wish-granting miko, you—

title: The Flaming Red from Tomorrow
content:
[Objective: Read Lucilla's WavesLine message]
Lucilla: Long story short, we've found traces of Aemeath's frequency.
[Choice]  Huh?
(Rover): Huh?
[Choice]  Where?
(Rover): Where?
Lucilla: In the active Voidmatter zone beneath Lahai-Roi. Do you remember that white-haired miko you met, the one with the blade?
Lucilla: Her name is Hiyuki. She's been helping the Collective survey the active Voidmatter zone. Simply put, she's in charge of protecting researchers and students who aren't equipped for a fight.
Lucilla: She's been helping us out with the investigation lately. Like you, she's trying to track down any sign of Aemeath.
Lucilla: Frankly, progress has been slow. She ran it by me and decided to head deeper underground to make some progress—into the high-risk section of the Voidmatter zone.
Lucilla: And we've seen some progress. She's found traces of Aemeath's frequency.
Lucilla: This means we may actually have a chance in bringing back Aemeath—which is why Hiyuki took a risk, and used her familiar to probe deeper into the Voidmatter zone.
[Choice]  That's too much risk.
(Rover): That's too much risk... We all know what Aleph-1 is capable of. I should join her.
[Choice]  Will she be all right on her own?
(Rover): Will she be all right on her own? I should join her.
Lucilla: Oh, no. That won't be necessary. She's already back.
Lucilla: She's fine. She just needs to rest. That said, we've detected unusual Voidmatter activity. Until proper preparations are made, nobody's going down there again.
Lucilla: That's it for now. I'll update you as soon as we know more.
}}
(Quest complete: The Flaming Red from Tomorrow)
(Obtained Trophy: The Danger Within)

title: Wishes in the Bell
subsection: Hiyuki has been invited to the Frostlands
content:
[Objective: Hiyuki has been invited to the Frostlands]
Hiyuki: What are you looking at?
Lucilla: Ah, there you are. Nothing really. I've just been wondering... if I wanted to land another astronomical investment to study all the Exoswarm coming off this giant mech...
Lucilla: What kind of pitch would it take to make every major player in Solaris nod along and funnel Credits into my pocket, year after year?
Hiyuki: Have you figured it out?
Lucilla: Not yet. My conscience won't let me think that far. Luckily, the man who can figure it out is back.
Hiyuki: ...The old man who promised me the blade? The head of the Spacetrek Collective?
Lucilla: The very same, but don't let the quick agreement fool you. He's already thinking ten steps ahead. If Ashinohara wasn't in such dire straits, he wouldn't have agreed to forge that blade for you so easily.
Lucilla: Or at the very least, he'd have made sure he got his pound of flesh in return.
Hiyuki: ...I couldn't find the child. Time and space in that dimension are too fractured. My familiar lost its way.
Lucilla: Hm... then we need something that can hold out longer. A better way to search?
Hiyuki: Voidmatter reactivity has been high lately. A clear sign to follow would be best.
Lucilla: That child is the Exostrider's Resonator. There's no clearer sign than that.
Lucilla: Looks like it's time the Exostrider was reactivated. When that happens, whether you're an annoying adult or the one meant to pilot it, I'm sure everyone will be on board, don't you think?
Lucilla: Ooh, what if we used footage of the Exostrider activating to pitch for funding?
Hiyuki: And the confidentiality agreements?
Lucilla: No sympathy for my chronic funding anxiety?
Lucilla: Fine. Go to Honami. I already approved your leave of absence.
Hiyuki: Why?
Lucilla: To... test the blade?
Lucilla: Even once the Exostrider awakens, there's still a chance it fails. If it does, what you sealed in the  becomes a liability...
Lucilla: But it could also be our ace in the hole.
Lucilla: So before I give you the thankless task of guarding those plains, go deal with matters of the heart first.
Hiyuki: ...Understood. I will return in one day.
Lucilla: Take two. Give yourself a day to look around.
Lucilla: Go on. A Black Shores member will meet you there. Hmph... I still have all of Dr. Luuk's mess to clean up.
Hiyuki: Understood. I am at your call should you require it.
Lucilla: Yes, I'm listening...
Lucilla: So it's about Denia... I see. Let's discuss it in person.

title: Wishes in the Bell
content:
[Objective: Head to Honami]
Black Shores Contact: Lady Miko, can you hear me?
Hiyuki: Yes. You may call me Hiyuki.
Black Shores Contact: Understood, Lady Hiyuki.
Hiyuki: ...Mmm.
Black Shores Contact: Most of the Left Behind in Honami City have been relocated. But a few, the ones whose regrets run deepest, still roam the danger zones.
Black Shores Contact: Their unfulfilled desires concentrate the Lament's power. An incident just waiting to happen.
Black Shores Contact: With you here, I feel better about the situation. We didn't expect you to take this on yourself...
Hiyuki: Protecting Honami is the duty of the Miko of Flaming Sakura. I thank you for your support.
Hiyuki: Actually, I have a favor to ask.
Black Shores Contact: Oh, is it about Gyokuro, the former miko? We've already found traces that may belong to her, but nothing we can confirm yet.
Black Shores Contact: We're in the process of narrowing down her location. As soon as we learn anything, you'll be the first to know.
Hiyuki: I am in your debt.
Black Shores Contact: Oh, it's nothing. If it weren't for you back then, I would have... Anyway, I'll leave this area to you!
Hiyuki: You can rely on me.
Hiyuki: …Was there something else you wanted to say?
Black Shores Contact: ...N-Nothing! Lady Hiyuki, it's just... Ugh, thank you for everything you do! Goodbye!

title: Wishes in the Bell
content:
[Objective: Purge the Left Behind]
Impassioned Youth: You... You are...!
Hiyuki: Yes.
Impassioned Youth: Miko of Flaming Sakura, you're back! I knew those monsters wouldn't stand a chance!
Impassioned Youth: Everyone else thought we were done for, but I told them, "Don't worry. Lady Miko will come and save us!"
Hiyuki: ...I'm sorry. I was too late.
Impassioned Youth: It doesn't matter! You're here now, aren't you?
Impassioned Youth: Please, just say it. Say the Miko of Flaming Sakura has returned, and that those monsters are finished…!
Hiyuki: The Threnodian has retreated, but I couldn't... I couldn't save you...
Impassioned Youth: But you defeated it. Again. And one day, you'll drive it away from Ashinohara for good!
Hiyuki: Yes, I hear your wish. And I promise, one day...
[Dialogue Option]  Purge the Left Behind.
Hiyuki: (I... failed their hopes.)
Hiyuki: (No matter how many times we drive it back, the Threnodian always returns.)
Hiyuki: (When will we be freed from this nightmare, Ashinohara…?)
Sorrowful Man: This is all your fault! "Eternal Miko," huh? …You're all useless! Every last one of you!
Hiyuki: ...
Sorrowful Man: How do you even dare show your face in Honami…!
Sorrowful Man: They're dead! Everyone's dead! Hahaha… I knew it. I knew the Threnodian couldn't be defeated… I should've run away as far as I could…
Sorrowful Man: Lady Miko... Lady Miko! Please! Do something! Anything?
Hiyuki: I...
Sorrowful Man: Powerful people like you won't die even if you lose. What about us? What about ordinary people? Just wait to be torn apart?
Sorrowful Man: ...I knew you couldn't hold the line. I knew it couldn't be killed, but... how do we go on from here?
Sorrowful Man: Lady Miko... Heroes...! Tell me, what should we do?!
Hiyuki: If you need someone to hate, let it be me.
Hiyuki: It's alright. Place all your pain, all your resentment upon me. May your soul be granted a moment of peace.
[Dialogue Option]  Purge the Left Behind.
Hiyuki: (If I had been stronger… could I have saved them?)
Hiyuki: (If only I had more power...)
Nervous Girl: Lady Miko... Are you the Lady Miko?
Nervous Girl: Oh! You are! You're the miko who once talked to Lady Gyokuro!
Nervous Girl: She told me about you. She said you're her most treasured family, just like my big sister and I! Your name is... um, it's...
Hiyuki: Hiyuki.
Nervous Girl: Yes! Hiyuki, that's it! Such a pretty name, just like Lady Gyokuro's!
Nervous Girl: My sister said if I hid here and prayed with all my heart, Lady Miko would come and save us. So… I've been waiting.
Hiyuki: Little one, what's your name? Your hands are cold. Have you been waiting long?
Nervous Girl: Kanna. My sister calls me Kanna.
Kanna: Lady Miko... you're finally here, but my sister... She...
Hiyuki: It's alright. I'm listening.
Hiyuki: She asked you to wait here, didn't she? She must have trusted you very much to give you such an important task.
Kanna: A... task?
Hiyuki: Yes, a task. If not for you, I would never have found this place.
Hiyuki: You did well, Kanna. You completed your task perfectly.
Kanna: Lady Miko, are you here to save Honami? Then… is Honami safe now?
Hiyuki: …Mm, Honami will be fine.
Kanna: Sister said you carry everyone's wishes. That you're the strongest! I knew you'd come and fix everything!
Kanna: Um… Lady Miko, can you help me find my sister?
Hiyuki: Of course. We'll both get to see our sisters again soon.
[Dialogue Option]  Purge the Left Behind.
Kanna: When we find her, let's eat red bean pudding! We make the best red bean pudding in the whole world! If you come try it, everyone will want some!
Hiyuki: Then you'll need to make a lot of it. Can you manage that?
Kanna: Pinky promise! We'll make lots and lots of pudding!
Kanna: Then even if the Threnodian comes back, we'll have something to eat, and we won't be scared anymore!
Hiyuki: It's a promise then. We'll make a lot of pudding.
Hiyuki: ...
Hiyuki: (Red bean pudding... Gyokuro always did have a weakness for sweets like that.)
Hiyuki: (This time... will I find her traces and truly set her free?)
Lively Woman: Hello, Lady Miko. I've been waiting for you for a very long time.
Lively Woman: My final wish… was simply to see you one last time.
Hiyuki: ...Your final wish?
Lively Woman: Yes. It's alright. I know I'm dead. I know I'm what they call a "Left Behind" now.
Lively Woman: But I thought if I'm going to remain like this anyway, I may as well get what I wanted before I disappear, right?
Hiyuki: I've heard of cases where the Left Behind remain aware of their state, sustained by powerful desires… But for such a simple wish…
Hiyuki: You truly only wished to see me again?
Lively Woman: Hehe. I mean, you are a legend. You've been the Miko of Flaming Sakura since my great-grandmother's time.
Lively Woman: When I heard Honami was in danger and that the Miko of Flaming Sakura would meet the vanguard, I rushed here just to see you.
Hiyuki: You shouldn't have taken such a risk. If you wished to see me, you could have gone to the Flaming Sakura.
Lively Woman: I know, I know. Everyone says you can just write your wish on the plaque and Lady Miko will see it… but I worried. What if it never reached you?
Lively Woman: So I came all this way to make the wish in person. I wanted to see whether it would come true.
Hiyuki: Very well. Then tell me, what is your true wish?
Lively Woman: I wish for world peace. For people to stop living in fear of the Lament. I want everyone to survive it—
Lively Woman: Lady Miko, my wish is... "That there will never be another Miko of Flaming Sakura."
Hiyuki: ...
Hiyuki: I see. Then I promise you. This wish will be fulfilled.
Lively Woman: I know it will.
Grand Architect: After all, you are the Eternal Miko—
Grand Architect: Now, now. No need for that, Lady Miko.
Grand Architect: If you wished, you could cut down this avatar at any moment. But… I think you'll find this far more interesting.
Hiyuki: Gyokuro's Shiratori (white bird).
Grand Architect: I know the Fractsidus has caused Ashinohara its fair share of grief. But personally? I hold no ill will toward you.
Grand Architect: I had dealings with the previous miko. It wasn't exactly a pleasant chat, but I promise you, her death was not by my hand.
Grand Architect: Just as you once witnessed, she met the fate all Mikos of Flaming Sakura share. She died burning her future to ash to pay for the present.
Grand Architect: Aren't you even a little curious? About what I showed her?
Grand Architect: If this makes you uncomfortable, feel free to cut through space and leave. This face of mine, of course, is entirely at your mercy.
Hiyuki: No need to dull my blade.
Grand Architect: Hmph... She wears the exact same expression as the previous miko. I suppose one day, she too will be reduced to ashes by her own wish.
Grand Architect: Oh, Eternal Miko... is she simply arrogant? Or just a coward?

title: Wishes in the Bell
subsection: See who that familiar silhouette belongs to...
content:
[Objective: See who that familiar silhouette belongs to...]
Kanna: Lady Gyokuro, guess what? No math homework today!
Kanna: My parents and my big sister finally taught me how to make red bean pudding. Want to try mine?
Gyokuro: I'd love to! You know I can't resist red bean pudding. Wouldn't miss your special batch for the world, little Kanna.
Kanna: Yay! I'll go make it right now—
Hiyuki: Aneue (Older sister), I'm here. What is it?
Gyokuro: My, my. Can't a sister just want to see her favorite girl without a reason?
Hiyuki: ...That's not what I meant.
Gyokuro: Hehe. There's that serious little face. I just wanted to chat. Always relaxes me.
Gyokuro: So? How are things at the Flaming Sakura?
Hiyuki: The usual. Many came to make wishes.
Gyokuro: The Threnodian's active cycle is almost here. Death will be a frequent visitor to Ashinohara once more.
Gyokuro: Prayers for safety, peace, victory… they pile up thickest at times like this.
Gyokuro: The Miko of Flaming Sakura is the bridge between people and the divine. A "wish jar" for all their hopes. We must listen to every single one.
Hiyuki: ...Lately, I've been hearing you ring the Suzu (ritual bell).
Hiyuki: To grant those wishes, you burn your future using the Suzu's power. Continue... and one day there'll be nothing left to burn.
Hiyuki: You should have stepped down already, Aneue (older sister). Let me become the Miko of Flaming Sakura. Let me inherit the Suzu.
Gyokuro: Oh, I'm perfectly fine! I've got futures to spare, you know?
Gyokuro: You tell me, little Hiyuki. What's got you so fixated on this? Don't tell me you're secretly in awe watching my heroics on the battlefield, and—
Hiyuki: Yes. I want to be just like you.
Gyokuro: Heh... you wish! You're a hundred years too early for that, you little blockhead.
Gyokuro: Enough about the Suzu! Stay and have some pudding with me instead. I know a wonderful little shop.
Gyokuro: Always practicing archery under that sakura tree. What a bore! A girl your age should be out living a little!
Hiyuki: ...Here we go again. You know I don't care about any of that.
Hiyuki: I'm going back.
Gyokuro: You sure? Come on, consider granting your big sister's wish.
Hiyuki: I only came because you called. I put my work on hold. I can't stay too long.
Hiyuki: Besides... I don't like red bean pudding.
Gyokuro: Huh?! I keep forgetting you have the world's most boring palate. What a shame.
Gyokuro: I'll just have to enjoy it all by my lonesome, then!
Hiyuki: Gyokuro never once spoke of her own wishes. She lived only to grant the wishes of others.
Hiyuki: If only... I had chosen to go with her.

title: Wishes in the Bell
subsection: Listen to what the Grand Architect has to say
content:
[Objective: Listen to what the Grand Architect has to say]
Grand Architect: Thoughts on the show?
Hiyuki: You showed me all this... because the Fractsidus wants to replicate the "assimilation" within the Blessed Maiden herself?
Hiyuki: You want me for the possibility that I could become the Threnodian's Resonator in the future.
Grand Architect: I won't deny it. After all, among all the Mikos of Flaming Sakura, only you can see through that Suzu and see a future so clearly entwined with the Threnodian's.
Grand Architect: That is your gift. Your talent.
Hiyuki: It is a dangerous curse.
Grand Architect: From Ashinohara's legends and the Spacetrek Collective's investigative reports, you know who Rover is by now.
Grand Architect: As a "savior" yourself, what do you think of his capabilities?
Hiyuki: Rover... He's strong.
Grand Architect: Hehe, you can afford to be more effusive. Unlike you, who failed Ashinohara time and again, he is the perfect "savior."
Grand Architect: But let's be brutally honest. This world doesn't have a second Rover. He saved Jinzhou and Rinascita... but what about Honami?
Grand Architect: Solaris is full of dark corners like Honami, places the savior's light will never reach.
Grand Architect: You, Miko of Flaming Sakura, have a gift. You might not fear the curse of the Threnodian or Lament.
Grand Architect: But what of "them?" The weak, those not blessed by fate? And yet, is it really fair to place the weight of an entire world on a single pair of shoulders?
Grand Architect: Solaris needs more saviors, doesn't it?
Grand Architect: I'm just using the Threnodian to bring more of them into this world.
Hiyuki: You mean... You want to use its power, the way Rover once did?
Grand Architect: I've tried before. But a miracle like Fleurdelys requires a billion coincidences. And Mya? Nothing but the delusional ravings of Leviathan.
Grand Architect: Even the one that appeared in Rinascita at the end... was just a hollow, mute shell.
Grand Architect: But with your help? Everything changes. You could wield the Threnodian's power just as Rover did.
Grand Architect: Honami would not be a ruin. And Ashinohara would finally have its true "savior."
Hiyuki: ...
Hiyuki: I have to admit your proposition is tempting.
Hiyuki: I desire vengeance against the Threnodian. That is why I seek greater strength. I stayed in Lahai-Roi to forge a blade sharp enough to kill it.
Hiyuki: But I will not discard my dignity as a human for it. I will not become the very horror I hate. Not even for retribution.
Grand Architect: You stand on Honami's soil. You stand on a graveyard of millions.
Grand Architect: Go on. Ask them if your "dignity as a human" matters... I think they'd tell you that simply staying alive is what matters.
Grand Architect: Eternal Miko... you know your limits.
Grand Architect: You've crawled through countless defeats, barely protecting Ashinohara from the Threnodian's assault. But what of the future? You are no savior like Rover.
Grand Architect: When you fall, who will take up the Suzu? Who will walk this lonely, futile path next?
Hiyuki: ...
Grand Architect: We could always talk about the former miko... The bodies of the Left Behind are ephemeral. You'll find I have a far more durable proposal...

Excitiable Child: The author is obviously someone from inside the Flaming Sakura! That manga's basically a history book!



Today's the anniversary of Threnodian's defeat, so we're getting off early. Dinner?
I need to pick up some Miko of Flaming Sakura merch. Plus a commemorative booklet. You know, for the little one at home.
Oh, please. We both know it's for yourself.

Ugh... that's so bitter. How do you even drink this?
Excuse you! The tea you drink is way worse. These are imported coffee beans!
Oh oh, so she's been hiding the good tea, has she? She just ordered two tins of top-grade gyokuro.
Hey, hey, don't! I was saving that for her birthday...

Loading Screen
Photo Studio —Scrawled across a message board in uneven strokes— "Do not forget the regret that brought you here."-->

title: Wishes in the Bell
content:
Gyokuro translated to Jade Dew or Jeweled Dew
There is a green tea called gyokuro, which is grown in the shade compared to standard sencha, which is grown in the sun.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content: Quest Objective: Some progress has been made in activating the Exostrider...

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Read Luuk Herssen's WavesLine message]
Luuk Herssen: Hello, golden boy.
Luuk Herssen: Now that the Dark Side incident is wrapped up, manage any rest after the ceremony?
Luuk Herssen: Things will get busy again soon. You'll need to stay focused, but not wound up like a spring. Stress leads to bad calls.
[Choice]  I've rested up. Don't worry.
(Rover): I've rested up. Don't worry.
Luuk Herssen: Good. I'm a psychiatrist, after all. Happy to know my patient is actually following my advice for once.
[Choice]  I can't really relax until this is over.
(Rover): I can't really relax until this is over.
Luuk Herssen: I see. I sympathize, but can't say I approve. Once this is all settled, remember to give yourself a break.
Luuk Herssen: As for the Exostrider plan we discussed earlier, there's been a development.
Luuk Herssen: Come to my "workspace." It's better discussed where the walls don't have ears.
Luuk Herssen: By the way, I've obtained clearance for the latest motorbike upgrades from the Department of Engineering. You should be able to access the latest features by now. Hope they make your trip here easier.}}

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Meet Luuk Herssen at his "secret workspace"
content:
[Objective: Meet Luuk Herssen at his "secret workspace"]
Luuk Herssen: Candy? It's a new flavor. Sigrika and Lynae suggested it. Great for lifting spirits.
[Dialogue Option]  ...Mint jelly.
[Dialogue Option]  Yep, that'll wake you up.
Rover: Alright, Luuk. What's the word on this Exostrider plan?
Luuk Herssen: My conversation with Lucilla went well. She's on your side. Your showing during the Dark Side incident also helped speed up the Academy's internal review.
Luuk Herssen: That said, you've been a student here for less than a year. You'll need the Spacetrek Collective's approval to officially activate the Exostrider.
Luuk Herssen: Their biggest financial backer is the New Federation. And of course, they answer to an entire board of investors.
Luuk Herssen: And to them? The Exostrider is definitely a "high-value asset."
Luuk Herssen: I've been flooding their desks with reports. Your Academy investigation record, your latest test scores from Rabelle College, and a full physical adaptability eval I wrote myself...
Rover: And? Were they rejected?
Luuk Herssen: We got a meeting. But when that much money's involved, conflicts of interest make everything move very slowly.
Luuk Herssen: Unlike Jinzhou or Rinascita, they've got far too many "cooks" in the kitchen.
Rover: I'm worried we don't have that kind of time.
Luuk Herssen: Exactly. Which is why we're going to strike first. Besides, things have changed.
Luuk Herssen: It all comes down to this guy.
Luuk Herssen: This is Chase. Head of the Spacetrek Collective. He just got back to Lahai-Roi on a Triumph Avionics ship from the New Federation.
Luuk Herssen: President Lucilla, Professor Mornye, and I have all put in a good word. You'll be meeting him at the Research Institute.
Luuk Herssen: Chase started as a low-level employee at Ashridge Energy in the New Fed. Then he dropped off the grid for a few years before resurfacing in a government position.
Luuk Herssen: After that, he left the government and started diving into multiple large-scale investment projects. Some say he's still been Ashridge Energy's man the whole time, but no one's been able to prove it.
Luuk Herssen: He's sharp, low-profile, and very smooth. At his age, he's seen it all. His only real concern is if the Exostrider's pilot can be controlled.
Luuk Herssen: Normally, they'd pick Academy Synchronists who've been signing stacks of NDAs since day one. But—
Rover: Sounds like his attitude changed? Does that have something to do with the "changes" you mentioned?
Luuk Herssen: Come in. Let's talk over some hot drinks.

metadata.subsection: Meet Luuk Herssen at his "secret workspace"

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Head to the inner room]
Luuk Herssen: I heard Lucilla asked for your help after the ceremony. How did it feel working with her?
Rover: Well, at first she was pretty dominant, steering the conversation the whole time…
Rover: But now I understand it's because this Academy means so much to her.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Sit and wait for Luuk Herssen
content:
[Objective: Sit and wait for Luuk Herssen]
Luuk Herssen: Based on your intel, the Reactor Core has been returned. Ideally, we'd wait for the Exostrider to awaken before trying to help Aemeath or confront the Threnodian.
Luuk Herssen: But, recent readings from the Institute's Stridergate monitors... they're off the charts.
Luuk Herssen: Voidmatter reactivity is spiking. The Spacetrek Collective is getting twitchy. If Threnodian Aleph-1 breaks the seal, all of Solaris will be at risk, not just Lahai-Roi.
Luuk Herssen: Now, the Collective didn't establish itself here without binders full of contingencies for a Threnodian event.
Luuk Herssen: Problem is, every one of those plans would scorch decades of scientific progress.
Luuk Herssen: Which, in our case, actually gives us some leverage. Enough to have a real conversation with their head.
Rover: ... Then I'll convince him. I'll show him the lowest casualty count is the only one that makes sense. He'll have to approve me as the Synchronist who pilots the Exostrider.
Rover: Luuk, you mentioned you have contacts in the Black Shores. And this workspace of yours... It's secure, right?
Luuk Herssen: Guaranteed. What are you thinking?
Rover: Lahai-Roi is closed off from the outside world. Public comms are probably tapped by Fractsidus moles inside the Academy. And right now... I need a direct line to the Black Shores.
Luuk Herssen: I see. Give me a moment. I'll establish the link and leave the rest to you.
Shorekeeper: I received your call, Rover.
Shorekeeper: ...Is the situation in Lahai-Roi that dire? You look exhausted.
[Dialogue Option]  ...A lot has happened, Shorekeeper.
[Dialogue Option]  I'm alright. Just a little tired.
Rover: My frequency loss has been resolved. But Lahai-Roi is under imminent Threnodian threat. I need your help, Shorekeeper.
Shorekeeper: Understood. For this purpose… both I, and the Black Shores, exist.
Rover: Any additional intel on the Exostrider within the Tethys System? Verified or not, I need everything you have.
Rover: I trust Luuk. You can speak freely.
Shorekeeper: Records confirm that Luuk Herssen has been providing critical assistance and intelligence to the Black Shores. I trust your judgment.
Shorekeeper: After the founding of Startorch Academy, most information fell under their seal of secrecy. However, in its early days, you mediated negotiations between the Academy and the Roya. Through that process, the Black Shores gained partial access to certain archived insights.
Shorekeeper: The Spacetrek Collective fears that due to the Exoswarm's division, the Exostrider, even upon awakening, might not have enough power to face the Threnodian. This concern led to the Augmented Resonance initiative—the Synchronists.
Shorekeeper: Observing how Sentinels work with their Resonators, they theorized that the Exostrider, sharing similarities, could amplify its power through a Resonator as well.
Shorekeeper: However, considering your link with the Exostrider, the Tethys System does not recommend this method.
Shorekeeper: We have intel that deep beneath Lahai-Roi lies the  left behind by the Exostrider long ago.
Shorekeeper: It rests directly atop the seal on the . You can think of it as a kind of lock.
Shorekeeper: You do not need a cockpit to pilot the Exostrider. So long as its activation sequence remains unobstructed, you may pilot it using the Keystone.
Rover: ...Is it because I'm its "Arbiter"?
Shorekeeper: Precisely. For one who shares its origin, a cockpit would be more of a hindrance.
Shorekeeper: As for Aemeath... I think Dr. Luuk's proposal is viable.
Luuk Herssen: You mean using the Exoswarm-like "shell" that appeared in the cockpit to look for her?
Shorekeeper: Yes. The connection between frequencies will help. Rover,  bring "her" with you when you activate the Exostrider.
Rover: Sure. While I'm there, the Black Shores will need to keep a closer eye on Lahai-Roi.
Shorekeeper: I understand.
Rover: ...I'm counting on you, Shorekeeper.
Shorekeeper: As long as I may be of help to you, I am… content.
Shorekeeper: Please return safely from the Stridergate, Rover.
Rover: I will. Don't worry.
Luuk Herssen: I'll inform Lucilla. Take your time finishing that drink before you head out.
Rover: What do you think? I'm about to ask a man to sign off on a crazy plan, and I can't even promise him it'll work.
Luuk Herssen: Nobody has a plan they promise will work. If Chase agrees, it's because he's betting that you're his best option. Just take the win.
Luuk Herssen: At the end of the day, it all comes down to the person, Rover.

metadata.subsection: Sit and wait for Luuk Herssen

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Head to the office of Academic Affairs
content:
[Objective: Head to the office of Academic Affairs]
Lucilla: Mr. Chase. This is the student I mentioned, Rover. Our best hope for piloting the Exostrider.
Chase: Save the intro, President Lucilla. We've met before.
Rover: (Before…? In my past life at the Academy?)
Chase: Let's just get down to it. The Threnodian Aleph-1 situation is deteriorating. We're running out of time.
Chase: I wanted to wait for the Exostrider's self-regeneration to finish, but the clock has run out on that one.
Chase: So tell me, Rover. Why do you want to pilot the Exostrider? What's the play?
Rover: To find Aemeath and put down the Threnodian.
Chase: Aemeath… Name rings a bell. The one with the high-sync rate. Her disappearance was a real loss for us.
Rover: She's beyond the Stridergate.
Chase: ...Hehe. I see how it is.
Chase: But finding one person in a goddamn interdimensional haystack? Not so easy. You understand our position... the Threnodian is our priority.
Rover: Stopping the Threnodian is my priority too. I'm gonna handle both.
Rover: Look, we have the same objective, so like you said let's "just get down to it." If Voidmatter erupts, Lahai-Roi is ground zero. Every one of your projects will take a hit.
Chase: Regarding Aleph-1, our intel is insufficient. We are not, at this time, considering its total destruction.
Chase: What we need is for the Exostrider to reinforce the seal on the Stridergate.
Chase: To do that, we need a qualified Synchronist. And we need the Institute's Drive Replica. When that gets embedded in the Exostrider's chest cavity, then its repair is complete.
Chase: Right now, the Replica is in its final phase of development. We're still missing critical data.
Rover: A Drive Replica... Is that what you're building from the fallen Reactor Drive after Helios was launched?
Chase: Heh, correct. It's based on the original Drive's framework. You had a hand to play in that. You made sure Helios got launched.
Chase: To complete the Drive Replica, we require precise data from the Exostrider operating in high concentrations of Voidmatter, and environmental readings from inside the Threnodian.
Chase: Without them, we can't guarantee the Exostrider can resist Aleph-1's corruption.
Chase: Here's the verdict, Rover. On behalf of the Spacetrek Collective, I authorize you to pilot the Exostrider.
Chase: But remember, our objective is the data. We need readings from the high-concentration zone to complete the Replica.
Chase: And your personal mission gets ten minutes. That's the max duration our Voidmatter Barriers can cover the Stridergate once it's opened.
Chase: After ten minutes, you return to Lahai-Roi. Whether you found Aemeath or not. Do you accept?
Rover: Deal. One more thing. I won't be using a cockpit. Just show me the way to the Keystone and have the Exostrider ready. That's all I need.
Chase: Heh. Still full of surprises. Always bringing us the... unconventional.
Chase: Lucilla, run a high-pressure sync test for Rover. I've seen the physical eval, but I want live data for validation.
Chase: The moment the numbers hit green, we'll begin preparations for activating the Keystone and deploy Voidmatter Barriers around the Stridergate.
Rover: There's something else. I need a favor.
Lucilla: Go on, Rover.
Rover: The Fractsidus is lying low. Even after failing in the Dark Side, they could move the moment the Stridergate opens.
Lucilla: Ah. That's what's on your mind. Well, I have an update. Remember Sigrika's friend? The… somewhat lackadaisical one?
Rover: You mean Denia?
Lucilla: That's the one. She's gone missing. Our investigation points to her being the agent the Grand Architect referred to.
Lucilla: But don't let it distract you. I have a reliable friend keeping an eye on Fractsidus activity.
Lucilla: You just focus on waking the giant. Leave the rest to us, Rover.
Chase: The Black Shores just sent a formal communication request. They're offering full support for Lahai-Roi's evacuation, if it comes to that.
Chase: You handle it, Lucilla. You have a better read on the situation than I do. And you're better at talking with that Rover.
Chase: Heh... If there's anything else you want to ask me, now's the time.
Lucilla: I'm surprised you're placing this much trust in Rover, authorizing him so readily. Any particular reason?
Chase: We're different, President. I'm a businessman. And businessmen trust their instincts for a good investment.
Chase: The Threnodian could strike at any time. Given the circumstances, Lahai-Roi may have to be written off.
Chase: And with the timeline we have, relocating the Exostrider is impossible. If we're going to lose it anyway, why not let Rover take one last swing?
Lucilla: Understood. We still need to prepare for the worst-case scenario.
Chase: Of course. If this fails, we'll initiate the backup plan—Duskveil.

metadata.subsection: Head to the office of Academic Affairs

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Head to the Academy's rooftop]
Abby: Ugh, that guy gives me the creeps...
Abby: What kind of place is the New Federation, anyway? Are they all gonna be like that?
Rover: We'll find out when we get there, Abby.
Professor Sakya: So, you're Rover, huh? I'm Sakya. I'll be overseeing and evaluating your test today.
Professor Sakya: Lucilla filled me in on everything.
Professor Sakya: This synchronization test is far more intense than the standard procedure. We're simulating the neural load of a direct link with the Exostrider.
Professor Sakya: If you feel anything off, you call it. I won't allow the test to continue under Overclocking conditions. Review and confirm the safety protocols before entering the cockpit.
[Dialogue Option]  (Read and confirm the safety protocols.)
Professor Sakya: Good. The cabin systems are configured. The simulator cockpit is right there. I'll be watching your metrics closely the whole time.
Professor Sakya: I hope... you pass the test smoothly.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
Professor Sakya: I hope... you pass the test smoothly.



Simulation System: Neural network connected. Tactical model constructed.
Simulation System: Resonator vital sighs... synchronized.
Simulation System: Test complete. Recording synchronization rate data.
Simulation System: Cockpit opening. Please exit according to the safety protocols.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Complete the synchronization test]
Rover: ...How did you get all the way here from the lake house?
Professor Sakya: She wanders into the Academy sometimes. Usually, her caretaker bot escorts her back pretty quick, but today she was… being difficult.
Rover: We'll go back together in a bit, okay?
"Aemeath": ...
Professor Sakya: Hmph... So the little terror can be quiet. Never thought I'd see the day.
[Dialogue Option]  Professor Sakya, you knew Aemeath?
Professor Sakya: Yes. I was her teacher. Over ten years ago now. She used to drive me up the wall. Made me lose my composure more than once. She never did seem to mind.
[Dialogue Option]  (I think I've heard this Professor's name before...)
Rover: (Back at the fan meeting… people mentioned a Sakya. They said she was Aemeath's teacher. That she actually really cared.)
Professor Sakya: The last day I taught her, she wrote "Saving the world" as her career path. I asked her if that was really what a Synchronist should be aiming for, then gave her a piece of my mind and told her to rewrite it.
Professor Sakya: She didn't even get upset. Just smiled, took the form, and walked away. She never stepped out of that cockpit again.
Professor Sakya: Now she's back, but not really. What a headache of a student.
"Aemeath": ...
Professor Sakya: Lucilla told me you're her family. Is that true?
Rover: Yes.
Professor Sakya: And you're planning to pilot the Exostrider and bring her back from the Stridergate?
Rover: That's the plan.
Professor Sakya: Sounds like an absurd, bold, utterly delusional idea. No one knows what's actually behind that Gate.
Rover: I know.
Professor Sakya: ...When Aemeath went missing, the cockpit recorded an abnormally high synchronization rate. We couldn't verify it after she disappeared, so it was never officially logged.
Professor Sakya: Your test results are just shy of hers overall. But in some sectors, they're even higher. You've passed, Rover.
Professor Sakya: I hope that absurd plan of yours works… and that you bring my student home.
[Dialogue Option]  No doubt about it.
[Dialogue Option]  ...I'll do my best.
Professor Sakya: The results are out, but preparing the Exostrider will take time. You'll need to wait around two days.
Professor Sakya: We'll let you know when it's ready.
"Aemeath": ...Cas...sette...

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Read Mornye's WavesLine message]
Mornye: Mentor, it's me.
Mornye: The Exostrider has been primed for activation. The data reception framework for the Drive Replica is ready as well.
Mornye: At your request, the Spacetrek Collective transferred "Aemeath" to the Institute… but she won't respond to anyone else. I believe she's waiting for you.
Mornye: I'm at the Institute too. See you soon.}}

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Head to the Research Institute]
Abby: So, we're finally going to where that giant eye is hiding?
Rover: Yeah. And Abby, if you think it's stronger than you, don't try to be a hero, okay?
Abby: I've got this! But uh... We don't know how much strength it's hiding behind that Gate, huh...
Rover: Our priorities are the data and Aemeath. A direct fight with Aleph-1 can wait until the Drive Replica is ready.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Search for traces of Aemeath]
(Obtained: Aemeath's Cassette)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
subsection: Head to the Research Institute's Lobby
content:
[Objective: Head to the Research Institute's Lobby]
Lynae: Hey Rover! Are you... leaving now?
[Dialogue Option]  How did you know?
Lynae: I kinda cornered Professor Mornye. Bugged her until she cracked.
[Dialogue Option]  Were you... waiting for me?
Lynae: Yeah, I was worried. Figured I'd catch you before you left.
Lynae: Rover, so you're gonna pilot the Exostrider.
Lynae: You... feel nervous at all?
Lynae: I know you're awesome and all, but nobody's ever done this before.
Lynae: Nobody knows if the Exostrider will even move, or what else might go wrong.
Lynae: Everything's felt so heavy at the Academy lately. Teachers are stretched thin. Even the nearby Exoswarm seem restless...
Rover: Lynae, are you nervous?
Lynae: ...Eh?! Okay, fine. Is it that obvious?
Lynae: Look, after I aced the entrance exam, I thought, "Sweet. Life's gonna be packed again. Non-stop." Like it used to be.
Lynae: But just when I was ready to finally be a student... my bubble popped. My brilliant student life, "Poof" and done.
Lynae: The Threnodian, Voidmatter, the Fractsidus... They're breathing down our necks, and I can't do anything to help you fight them.
Lynae: I just have to stand here and watch you walk into danger alone. It makes me feel totally useless.
Rover: I'd feel worse if I dragged everyone in Lahai-Roi into danger, just to back me up.
Rover: Of course, if things get really desperate, we'll have to face it together.
Rover: But for now? When I look at all the students who came here chasing their dreams... I want them to stay students.
Rover: Because...
[Dialogue Option]  It's a "savior's" job to protect the world.
Lynae: Dang, that's a heavy title! ...We're in the same year, y'know.
[Dialogue Option]  Protecting the kids is a job for a grown-up.
Lynae: Come on, you're a student too... We're just kids to you, or something?
Lynae: …But I get what you're saying.
Lynae: Making you waste time on a pep talk when you've got a world to save... I do need to grow up.
Lynae: But I won't just sit around. I'll be on standby. Whatever the Academy needs to support your mission, I'm in.
Lynae: And when this is all over, we're going for a drive!
[Dialogue Option]  Sounds nice.
[Dialogue Option]  Maybe we can start a biker squad next time.
Lynae: Heh, can't wait for that day to come.
Lynae: Professor Mornye's up ahead. Good luck out there, my friend!

metadata.subsection: Head to the Research Institute's Lobby

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Meet up with Mornye]
Valentina: Temporary passage is complete. It'll take you directly to the Keystone.
Valentina: The Black Shores will keep a team on standby here at the Institute. If you need our support, just say the word.
Mornye: Thank you. We couldn't have built the data framework this quickly without your team's expertise.
Valentina: Lahai-Roi is a top priority. A joint call by the Shorekeeper and the Tethys System... Oh. Professor Mornye, your guest has arrived.
Mornye: Ah... you're here.
Rover: Is that the way to the Stridergate?
Mornye: Yes. This temporary passage will take you to the Dimmr Plains, deep within Bjartr Woods.
Mornye: Both the Stridergate and the Keystone are located in the Solvein Heartwood at its center. President Lucilla has already departed with the advance team. They'll be waiting on the other side.
Mornye: And also...
Anxious Researcher: Huff—huff—Sh-she's… too fast!
Mornye: What happened?
Anxious Researcher: Professor Mornye, she suddenly bolted into the Cassette Depository and... and took this.
Mornye: This is...
Rover: Can I see it?
Rover: I'll give it back in a moment. Mornye, do you see what's special about it?
Mornye: This ID number... I saw it in the student file during her inspection. This is Aemeath's own Cassette. It's been stored in the Depository since she went missing.
Rover: Why did you want to bring this now?
"Aemeath": ...
Mornye: It may be instinctual.
Mornye: Dr. Luuk did say this Exoswarm-like "shell" shares a frequency link with the real Aemeath.
Mornye: Or it could be the "shell's" residual instinct. Cassettes are proof of a student's identity. Or it could be a weak signal sent from the Aemeath beyond the Gate. We can't determine which theory is correct yet.
Mornye: However, this does remind me... carrying a Cassette into an unexplored Void Storm zone follows standard exploration protocol. Do you have yours?
Rover: Yeah. I've kept it with me.
Rover: I'll head to the Dimmr Plains now then, Mornye.
Mornye: ...I'll have to stay here, monitoring the data and ensuring the Drive Replica is ready. I wish I could go with you.
Mornye: But I'll be fully supporting your mission. Mentor, please... take care.
Rover: I count on you to watch my back, Mornye.
Rover: With what we accomplished with Helios, I trust you'll handle the Drive Replica. We will succeed again.
Mornye: I won't let you down, Mentor. Let this be... a new promise between us.
Rover: Let's go.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Meet up with Lucilla]
Abby: Ugh, stinky, this place reeks! The smell of that giant eyeball's getting stronger!
Rover: That massive glowing tree… is that the Solvein Heartwood?
Rover: (That miko...)
Lucilla: Wait. Before you go, you should say hello to him.
Lucilla: This is Hiyuki, I told you about her before. The only reason we could set up the monitoring equipment so quickly is because she cleared the way for us.
Lucilla: See that lingering frost? Ten years ago, a Voidmatter rift opened in the Dimmr Plains. Hiyuki went there alone and sealed it.
Lucilla: Thanks to her efforts, the Spacetrek Collective and the Roya were able to fortify the seal successfully.
Lucilla: Every task the Academy assigns her, she completes flawlessly. Were she to have a flaw though, it'd be that she goes through blades like nobody's business.
[Dialogue Option]  I remember you came across Aemeath's traces before.
Hiyuki: Yes. Lucilla spoke of what that child did. She is a good one. Strong... But her strength does not change the fact that she is a student.
Hiyuki: That we allow a child to bear such a burden is a failure on our part as adults.
Hiyuki: I sent this white bird to search the Voidmatter's concentrated depths. And I am certain I felt her frequency.
Hiyuki: Somewhere in Voidspace, she waits. The Collective pursues what is right, but your quest to save the one you hold dear? That, I understand.
Lucilla: Very good—! But I'm afraid we can't say more than that, okay? Right now, both sides want the same thing. That's the best we could ask for.
Lucilla: You were worried about the Fractsidus, weren't you? While you're beyond the Stridergate, she'll handle perimeter security.
Lucilla: She's hunted both the Threnodian and the Fractsidus for a long time. There's no one better for the job. Right, Hiyuki?
Hiyuki: Yes. Those two Fractsidus members... I will track them down.
Hiyuki: Here. Take this.
Hiyuki: The white bird carries my power. It will shield you.
Hiyuki: Should you lose yourself in the Voidmatter, it will also guide you back.
Lucilla: Hiyuki is part of Startorch Academy's Special Response Force. She works from the shadows, she's been an incredible help to us all.
Hiyuki: If, in your fight with the Threnodian, you require aid...
Hiyuki: ...You may make a wish to me.
Lucilla: How about I go first? I wish for peace and safety across the Dimmr Plains.
Lucilla: Hehe, Hiyuki is the strong and silent type. Spend enough time with her, though, and you'll find she's rather fascinating.
Rover: Why didn't you introduce us before? Why the reveal now?
Lucilla: No point in hiding what's already in plain sight. Besides, you're both strong and it's safer if you work together.
Rover: What did she mean, "make a wish?"
Lucilla: Just what it sounds like. But… don't make one unless it's life or death.
Lucilla: Granting wishes... always comes with a price.
Lucilla: I've sent you intel on high-concentration Voidmatter zones. Review them when you can.
Lucilla: I couldn't say this with Chase present, but I think you understand. For him, this is a calculated investment. For you, it's a suicide mission.
Lucilla: You've been in Voidspace. You've faced it. If Aleph-1 truly lies beyond that Gate, It'll sense you the moment you cross over... This won't be easy.
Lucilla: The Exostrider isn't fully repaired. If something goes wrong, it may not be able to hold out against Aleph-1. And the Collective won't risk an extraction if a Voidmatter outbreak is imminent.
Lucilla: …Once you enter the Gate, you'll be completely alone. Are you ready, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  Of course.
[Dialogue Option]  And just so you know...
Rover: I've been in situations like this more times than I can count.
Rover: If I only cared about walking away clean, I wouldn't have gotten this far, or be standing here now.
Rover: So… thanks for the concern, President. But I've been ready.
Lucilla: Heh... Very good. I'm relieved you've thought it through.
Lucilla: I'll be here with the others, monitoring the Voidmatter Barriers. If something happens, I have to respond immediately as the Academy's head.
Lucilla: We'll probably be able to maintain a data feed, but based on past intel the Voidmatter's "disintegration" effect will destabilize the signal.
Lucilla: It'll likely cut out once you reach the Keystone. From that point on, every call is yours.
Rover: I understand.
Spacetrek Collective Researcher: President Lucilla, we've checked her condition. No signs of Voidmatter contamination. She's stable.
Lucilla: Alright. Go on, Rabelle College freshman.
Lucilla: The students and faculty of Startorch Academy have been waiting for the day the Exostrider awakens. May you return victorious.

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Head to the Research Institute]
Rover: Am I... back at the Academy?
Abby: You okay? Ugh, I feel terrible too...
Abby: Something just yeeted us outta the Threnodian's gut! Rapid interdimension whiplash is no stroll through the park, I tell ya...
Rover: The Exostrider isn't here.
Abby: The big guy's still stuck inside the Threnodian…
Abby: Did you see that freaky black hand that popped up in the cockpit? The whole dimension freaked out! Like it was tryna spit us out!
Abby: Next second, the Voidmatter had us flushed out here!
Rover: I saw Nivora in the flashes. It's the Fractsidus. Has to be.
Rover: Everyone was standing right here. This is where Voidmatter began to contaminate the sky.
Rover: And Aleph-1 was watching me and the Exostrider beyond the Gate...
Mornye: Mentor! Finally got a hold of your signal!
Mornye: ...We lost contact for an entire day. Everyone's been worried.
Rover: (An entire day? Felt like minutes... Time distortion from being inside the black hole?)
Rover: Mornye, I'm fine. We had an incident. The Exostrider is still inside Voidspace beyond the Gate.
Rover: And now… even the Academy inside the Voidmater Barriers is getting hit by Void Storms. What happened while I was gone?
Mornye: After you went in, the data transmission was perfect. We were celebrating.
Mornye: But not long after, Void Storms began to erupt even inside the Academy. We haven't been able to find any breach or source to explain it.
Mornye: Most of Lahai-Roi has been evacuated to the Collective's escape pods with Black Shores support.
Mornye: Those who remain are gathered here at the Institute.
Rover: (Whose eyes was I seeing through in those flashes? If they're the cause of the Threnodian's breach, could they be a Harbinger? Like in Rinascita?)
Rover: (In that moment, that "shell"... She had the same look in her eyes as the real Aemeath.)
Rover: (Why was she so set on giving me this Cassette? What was she trying to say?)
Rover: (Looks like... I'll have to open it up to find out.)
Rover: I'm coming to you. I brought something back from the other side and want you to see it first.
Rover: The Threnodian struck like a bolt out of the blue. We may not know why yet, but we need to figure out our next move together.
Mornye: Understood. We'll be waiting for you at the Institute.
Rover: (That's a lot of WavesLine messages.)
Rover: (All from when I was beyond the Stridergate... I really made them worry.)

title: Starlights from Yesterdays
Starlights from Yesterdays
content:
[Objective: Meet up with everyone]
The Shaper: The Soliskin have swept the area. None remain in Bjartr Woods.
Sigrika: Someone just posted a call for help on the campus's Wavesline group chat. I'll go back to run a final check later!
The Shaper: Sigrika, are you sure you alone can handle it?
Sigrika: Don't worry. I have my runes. They'll help me drive back any contaminated Exoswarm! The Soliskin will guide me too.
Lynae: I'm coming with you. Finding people is one thing, hauling them back is another. It'll be faster if we take my motorbike.
Lucilla: Status report, Professor Mornye.
Mornye: The launch orbit has been confirmed. The Drive Replica is projected to launch in 16 hours, at which point it will initiate Duskveil.
Lucilla: Then we evacuate every remaining soul in Lahai-Roi before that window closes.
Lucilla: Check the ships at the Roya Frostlands port, in addition to the escape pods.
Lucilla: We don't know how long Duskveil will hold. No one stays a second longer than necessary.
Rover: The Exostrider...
Lucilla: I heard from Professor Mornye. You went dark for a full day. We thought we'd lost you to Voidspace.
Lucilla: Activating the Exostrider before it was fully self-regenerated was a massive gamble. We all knew the stakes.
Lucilla: We hoped for the best, and of course, we prepared for the worst.
Lucilla: You're alive. That alone is good news for all of us.
Lucilla: No time to kick yourself now. I've got a mountain of work waiting for you, Rover.
Mornye: Please have a look at this, Mentor.
Mornye: The Research Institute is running the final modifications on the Drive Replica now. The Roya are assisting with assembly and verification.
Mornye: It's built from the framework of the fallen Reactor Drive. Various materials from the Exostrider, too.
Mornye: It's… it's everything Lahai-Roi has been working toward. This "man-made" heart is our final legacy for Solaris.
Mornye: In 16 hours, we launch it into the Canopy above Lahai-Roi.
Mornye: Once evacuation is complete, it will activate, transforming the Canopy into Duskveil. It'll contain the spread of Voidmatter.
Mornye: We only finished it because of the data you sent back from beyond the Stridergate.
Lucilla: See? Not a total loss after all.
Rover: ...Thank you. All of you.
Rover: About what I experienced beyond the Gate… there's something I want to show you.
Rover: I don't think she gave me this Cassette for no reason.
Rover: Whether it's her "shell" or Aemeath herself, she was trying to tell us something.
Lucilla: A Cassette retrieved from within the Threnodian… Heh. Now that is intriguing.
Lucilla: Professor Mornye, is the analyzer in the Cassette Depository still operational?
Mornye: We can head there now.
Sigrika: What's happening? Why are all the Cassettes rewinding…?
Lynae: The whole server bank's going nuts! Every screen is flickering!
Mornye: The data volume is far beyond the Cassette's capacity. It's as if thousands of people left their records in it...
Mornye: The storage system has destabilized. It's now flooding data into every archived Cassette in the room.
Mornye: But this isn't memory data.
Mornye: Aside from the corrupted junk, the compressed mass consists of coordinates.
Lynae: Coordinates? From beyond the Gate? Are they... locations inside the Threnodian's black hole?
Mornye: Based on your report, Mentor, conventional spacetime doesn't apply in Voidspace. You can't plot a standard map there.
Rover: If Aemeath went to these lengths to give us this, she wouldn't have made it impossible to follow.
Rover: What if they're coordinates in Lahai-Roi?
The Shaper: ...If such is the case, the origin might be... Please, allow me.
The Shaper: A uniform format, these coordinates share. I have verified one hundred and fifty points using Sundermere as the origin.
The Shaper: Each one aligns with a site of Royan runes etched upon stone. Just as you beheld within Solisylum.
The Shaper: Forged by the Exostrider, these patterns are. Void Storms do not affect them. We have only glimpsed fragments of their meaning through the lens of Solisylum.
Mornye: I see. Let me overlay these coordinates onto a Lahai-Roi map. It should make things clearer for us.
Mornye: Done. Using Sundermere as the origin, the distribution looks like this.
Sigrika: Everything matches. I'm spotting every Royan rune site in Bjartr Woods on this map.
Rover: (But what about the other coordinates...)
Lynae: Wait, I know that spot. That's where the Void Storm hit at the start of all this.
Lynae: You know... that time. When we first met.
[Dialogue Option]  The time we ran into a Voidworm?
Lynae: Yeah, yeah, that one.
[Dialogue Option]  The time you hit me with your motorbike?
Lynae: Ahaha, sorry... Ahem, anyway! Back to business!
Lucilla: Void Storms...
Mornye: If we reverse-match the coordinates by transcription order…
Lucilla & Mornye & Rover: Then Royan runes could be marking every spot a Void Storm has ever hit!
The Shaper: ...So it is. We Roya have observed something similar, but never perceived it as a universal law.
Lynae: Well, the runes aren't exactly neon signs on the stone boulders saying "LOOK HERE."
Mornye: There are too many locations. With the personnel we have left and the autonomous bots...
Lucilla: Leave the manpower to me.
Rover: You want to bring people back from the escape pods?
Chase: Precisely, Rover.
Rover: With Void Storms spreading, sending people back out to find hidden runes is too dangerous.
Chase: Any venture into the unknown carries risk, Rover.
Chase: Studying the Threnodian was a risk. Playing chess with the Fractsidus was a risk.
Chase: And piloting the Exostrider through the Stridergate was certainly a risk.
Chase: But where there is a sliver of hope, the Spacetrek Collective will always find people willing to bet on it. Once Duskveil is initiated, this place becomes a sealed tomb.
Chase: The intelligence retrieved from Voidspace is our only remaining asset up for study. It's our only leverage against Aleph-1 before Duskveil fails.
Chase: We have the capability, the responsibility, and the will to secure this Voidspace data.
Chase: Face the unknown, and we may lose much. Flee from it, and we lose everything.
Rover: Then leave Bjartr Woods to me.
Lucilla: It's the most heavily contaminated area. If this is because of what happened to the Exostrider—
[Dialogue Option]  Capability, responsibility, and the will...
[Dialogue Option]  I have them all.
Sigrika: Then, then...Please give me your hand, Rover!
Sigrika: Use this. It will guide you to other Royan runes.
Sigrika: Oh, and take this one too! It's for protection. With it, you'll definitely come back safely!
[Dialogue Option]  With your runes, I'll be fine.
[Dialogue Option]  With Siggy's magical rune, nothing bad will happen!
Chase: The clock starts now. Recover all Royan runes before Duskveil gets initiated.
Sigrika: Oh...
Lynae: My hand feels so warm. Incredible, it's like magic...
Chisa: Huh... so this is a Royan rune...
Lucilla: I'm splitting everyone into teams. They'll depart in waves according to their assigned groups.
The Shaper: Good. I will prepare the interpretation for the Royan runes.
Chase: I'll take charge... Yes, I'll make sure none of the Spacetrek Collective's proprietary tech leaks...

Lucilla: All units that have completed your missions, report back to the Research Institute immediately.

Lucilla: Please report to Dr. Luuk and N.A.N.A. for medical evaluation, then return to the shelter at once.
Lucilla: Analysis of the Royan runes has already begun. You have all done your best. Now, it's our turn to uncover the secrets hidden within them.}}
Rover: What's going on?
Mornye: Ah, Mentor. You're back.
Mornye: We've finished analyzing the runes, but their meaning still escapes us.
Mornye: As for the overlapping coordinates, we've run multiple standard decryption algorithms, but the results are contradictory.
Rover: I'm no rune expert… but we have a one here, don't we? She resonates with them.
Sigrika: Who—wait... Me?!
[Dialogue Option]  You wanted to say something, didn't you?
[Dialogue Option]  Bingo.
Sigrika: …If you're asking me, these runes don't feel flat. They feel… spherical.
Sigrika: About this big. And these two points are relative… like this.
Mornye: Three-dimensional coordinates... orthographic projection...
Mornye: If we take the Reactor Drive's light data from the database as a depth layer and reconstruct it...
Mornye: A map forms. The Royan runes are conveying a spherical map.
Rover: What are these two places...?
Mornye: The one on the surface corresponds to the Stridergate. As for the one at the center... there's too little data to confirm.
Mornye: But by geometric definition, it's the origin point of the entire map.
Rover: The Exostrider. That must be where it is in Voidspace.
Rover: It's the only thing that could survive there. The lodestar Aemeath was trying to show me.
Chase: Contamination around the Keystone is off the charts. We've got no viable spatial data. In other words, using the Stridergate to get you to Voidspace isn't an option.
Rover: I remember Lucilla mentioning a sealed rift in the Dimmr Plains.
Chase: Yeah. right. Once Hiyuki from the Special Response Force breaks the seal, that could serve as a new entry point.
Chase: But without the Exostrider... are you suggesting crossing the Stridergate and searching for it yourself, Rover?
Rover: Now that we have a concrete map, I should be able to retrieve the Exostrider before my power of Separation gives out.
Chase: ...A compelling proposal. Hard to refuse.
Chase: But don't forget the Exostrider is currently out of power. Finding it is one thing. Extracting it is another.
Rover: Then we set a hard deadline.
Rover: If I can transmit the Exostrider's coordinates to you before Duskveil initiates—
Rover: Then tell me you'll consider entrusting the Drive Replica to us.
Chase: "Consider," huh... so you're handing the choice to us?
[Dialogue Option]  It's not about who's making the choice.
[Dialogue Option]  It's about trust.
Rover: I'm not asking for a guarantee.
Rover: I'm trusting you, the professionals on this side, to make the right call. Whatever that call is.
Chase: ...The Exostrider's value justifies the risk. I agree to your proposal.
Lucilla: The Command Post only just pulled back from the Void Storm frontlines. Took longer than expected.
Lucilla: I've been briefed on the situation. Sorry I had to be absent for that.
[Choice]  No worries. It's all settled.
(Rover): No worries. It's all settled.
Lucilla: Still, I'd like a word with you before you go.
Lucilla: Let's meet by the Research Institute.}}
