[Objective: Welcome the auditor]
Lucilla: Uh, what's all this?
Sigrika: Professor! We heard a very important visitor is coming to tour the Academy. Don't worry, we'll make a good impression!
Lynae: Yep, we even threw together a little welcoming thing.
Lucilla: Oh, you rascals... Alright, but follow my lead. If this auditor is a by-the-book type, then we—
Aalto: Aha! WOOO!
Aalto: Oh yeah! What a ride! Now that was top-notch!
Aalto: So... S-so many people?
Aalto: So not a confidential audit, huh?
Lucilla: Welcome to Startorch Academy. I'm Lucilla, the Academy President. So glad you could make it.
Students: WELCOME TO STARTORCH ACADEMY!
Aalto: Oh! Uh, right. I'm Aalto. Haha... You guys really know how to roll out the red carpet.
Sigrika: Nice to meet you, honored sir! I'm Sigrika, from the Preparatory Program. Thank you for coming to tour the Academy!
Aalto: Hello, hello! And please, just Aalto is fine. No need for that "honored sir" stuff...
Sigrika: Got it. I'm a Roya, you know! And I just want to say the Academy has been so wonderful to my people. We're all working together to make the world a better place!
Sigrika: Oh! And there are lots of Roya students in Rabelle College too! Everyone works so hard!
Aalto: Uh? Huh...
Dorian: Chief Aalto! I'm Dorian from the Agronomy Wing! I've brought you a  Complete Nutrition Squeezy Jelly and our department's special self-heating Cup Noodles!
Aalto: Cup Noodles? Uh, thanks. And hey, just call me Aalto...
Misha: Director Aalto! I'm Misha from the Department of Exostrider Engineering! I couldn't bring my project here, so I'm here to sing instead!
Nevin: Director, I'm from the Department of Voidmatters, sir! I can dance!
Lynae: And I can do some custom mods on your bike!
Lucilla: Mr. Aalto.
Lucilla: This is Rover from Rabelle College. He will be joining us for the duration of your tour.
[Dialogue Option]  What's cooking, Director Aalto?
[Dialogue Option]  It's an honor, Esteemed Auditor, sir.
Aalto: Rover! What a fantastic name! Not too long, not too short!
Aalto: Are we supposed to know each other or not?
Rover: We are. But don't make it too obvious.
Aalto: Copy that.
Lucilla: Well then, without further ado, let's head over to Rabelle College. I'll fill you in on our facilities along the way.
Aalto: That'll be great.
Lucilla: Tell those kids to go their separate ways. I'll meet you at Rabelle College.
Rover: Got it.

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Learn about the crisis from the students
content:
[Objective: Learn about the crisis from the students]
Rover: Someone want to tell me what's happening?
Lynae: You didn't know, Rover? Everyone's saying the board is looking to shut down Rabelle College.
Sigrika: No, not the college. Just the Synchronists. A professor covering our Royan History class told us the Spacetrek Collective wants them out of the Academy!
Lynae: Yeah, well, the rumor mill says Rabelle eats up two-thirds of the Academy's budget, and the Collective's investors have strong opinions 'bout that.
Lynae: I say investors, but it's mostly New Federation money. Can't say I'm surprised they're pulling this kinda stunt.
Rover: What about you, Chisa? What have you heard?
Chisa: Me? Actually, I don't know the specifics of what's happening. I just wanted to help...
Rover: (So it's all just hearsay for now...)
[Dialogue Option]  Is this all happening because the Exostrider left?
Lynae: Probably. I mean, they were literally picked just to pilot the Exostrider.
Sigrika: But Synchronists are all such brilliant students! Even if they can't pilot anymore, they still...
Lynae: The New Fed only cares as long as you're an asset. The second you're not, you're out.
Rover: (There must be more to it than that.)
[Dialogue Option]  Why didn't any of the Synchronists show up?
Chisa: That's what's strange to me. But Professor Lucilla only had Rover come, so maybe it's not as serious as we think?
Sigrika: Why do I feel like asking Senior to come means the opposite?
Lynae: That Aalto guy... he's got a reputation in New Fed's circles. Known for handling intel, if you catch my drift.
Lynae: Isn't this supposed to be a cooperative visit...? Why's the Black Shores sending his type here?
Rover: (I'd better check the situation at Rabelle College.)
[Dialogue Option]  I see. Thanks for filling me in.
Rover: The President and I are on it. You guys should head back for now.
Lynae: Hm, well... Gimme a shout if you need backup! There's no way I'm letting them do the Synchronists dirty like this!
Sigrika: We're counting on you, Senior!
Chisa: We trust you!
[Dialogue Option]  (Head over now.)
[Dialogue Option]  (Head over later.)

metadata.subsection: Learn about the crisis from the students

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Visit Rabelle College's classrooms]
Lucilla: In addition to Augmented Resonance training, we place strong emphasis on general education for our Synchronists. This is Professor Mornye who teaches Synth Armament Studies.
Lucilla: Shall we sit in for a bit, Mr. Aalto? Before we tour the student projects?
Aalto: If it's no trouble?
Mornye: Alright. In the last lecture, we proved that the Ruehl Equation holds true for Type-II Synth Armaments. Today, we'll move on to their Tuning Stability Constants.
Mornye: Lixian, could you please write the final derivation from the last lecture on the board?
Lixian: Yes... Professor..
Mornye: While she gets started, let's do a quick review. Waleo, what is the standard medium used to measure Tuning Stability in a lab setting?
Waleo: It's s-so... s-so... mmm...
Mornye: Yes, sodium. An interesting choice, though its volatility makes it impractical for standard testing.
Mornye: Sonia, could you tell me the standard medium for determining Tuning Stability in Synth Armaments under laboratory conditions?
Sonia: Mm... S-squ... Squeezy... Jelly...
Mornye: Squeezy Jelly, you say... Well, it seems we moved through the material a bit too quickly last time.
Mornye: But that's alright. Everyone, please refocus. Let's go over Lixian's board work—
Lucilla: As you can see, Mr. Aalto, this is our signature "Sleep Learning Program."
Aalto: Oooh! Very impressive! Ahem... How about we move on to the next stop?
Lucilla: After you.
[Dialogue Option]  Hang in there.
[Dialogue Option]  I'll see you later.
Lucilla: Now we're about to show you some Augmented Resonance projects developed by our Synchronists.
Lucilla: Among them, the unmanned vehicle prototype shows exceptional promise across multiple market sectors—
TARD-E Unit: Absent Students: 8. Data uploaded to cloud storage.
Lucilla: These children... seem to have forgotten the importance of honoring their commitments.
Aalto: (What's the deal?)
Rover: (Looks like the students all skipped class.)
Aalto: Ahaha! Maybe we're just too early, President Lucilla. Why don't we take a stroll elsewhere? I'm actually quite curious about the Academy's catering system!
Lucilla: Hah... My apologies, Mr. Aalto. How fortunate we are to have you here despite our apparent lack of preparation.
Lucilla: There's no point denying it. You're seeing firsthand how the ongoing debate within the Spacetrek Collective has begun to affect our students.
Lucilla: Startorch needs support now more than ever.
[Dialogue Option]  (Shoot a knowing look toward Aalto.)
Rover: (Got any solutions?)
Aalto: (Not really...)
[Dialogue Option]  (Stay silent.)
Rover: (Dragging the Black Shores into this might make things difficult for Shorekeeper. Let's just observe for now.)
Aalto: I understand, President. And this is precisely why I'm here to convey the—
Lucilla: Mr. Aalto, how about we add an extra tour this evening? We can discuss anything you'd like after that.
Aalto: Uh... Works for me?
Lucilla: Rover, I'll take Mr. Aalto for a meal, then. Would you mind checking back in with Professor Mornye for me?
Aalto: (See—You—On—WavesLine.)

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Learn about the current situation from Mornye
content:
[Objective: Learn about the current situation from Mornye]
Rover: Why didn't you wake them up?
Mornye: This class is difficult to follow, so it's normal for some to drift off. Still, it's rare for the entire class to go like that.
Mornye: If only I could make my lectures more accessible...
Rover: This isn't your fault.
Mornye: It's like metal fatigue. These students are being tempered and pushed to their limits over and over. Eventually, the metal just snaps.
Mornye: Should I have woken them? Reprimanded them? Or offered them assurance...?
Mornye: I've heard about the pressure they've been under lately. Maybe the best thing is a few days away from all this...
[Dialogue Option]  Don't worry. Lucilla and I will take care of it.
Mornye: Thank you, Mentor.

metadata.subsection: Learn about the current situation from Mornye

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Read Aalto's WavesLine message]
Aalto: Be at the square by 8. The one we passed earlier. Got some intel to share.
[Choice]  OK.
(Rover): OK.
Aalto: Any recs on what to order? Lucilla went back to her office to take care of something.
[Choice]  Just order everything on the menu.
(Rover): Just order everything on the menu.
Aalto: Gotcha!
[Choice]  Get the cheap ones so you can toss them without feeling guilty.
(Rover): Get the cheap ones so you can toss them without feeling guilty.
Aalto: That bad? Now I HAVE to try 'em!}}

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Meet up with Aalto]
Aalto: You have my deepest respect. Working in this food desert takes a special kind of fortitude.
[Dialogue Option]  What did you have for dinner?
Aalto: Something that looked like toothpaste. Didn't go down well. Next thing I know, there were students everywhere shoving snacks at me like it was my birthday.
Aalto: Ugh, hellish.
[Dialogue Option]  Why is Encore not with you?
Aalto: I couldn't convince her. She hit me with "I'm too grown up for school now."
Aalto: But that's fine. I asked President Lucilla to give me some "grown-up" worksheets. See how she likes those, hmph!
[Dialogue Option]  Tell me what happened.
Aalto: To put it simply? The Exostrider's gone, so the Synchronist Program needs to go. Problem is, everyone has a different idea of what to do with those students—And by "everyone," I mean President Lucilla versus everyone else.
Aalto: Anyway, the New Federation and the majority of the board want to pull the plug immediately and draft a new teaching plan from scratch.
Aalto: Meanwhile, the Executive Committee moderates have promised to stay out of it, as long as their nation's Synchronists are covered. With either guaranteed support back home or a smooth transfer somewhere else.
Rover: Where does Lucilla stand?
Aalto: She wants to continue the Synchronist Program.
Rover: Continue?
Aalto: Yep. Confusing, isn't it? Speaking of which... how well do you know her, Rover?
[Dialogue Option]  Pretty well.
Aalto: Hm. I see.
[Dialogue Option]  (Do I really know her, though?)
Aalto: Hm, so you're not so sure either, huh?
Aalto: I'll be honest with you, Rover. The Black Shores doesn't trust her right now.
Aalto: Between her proposal, her deep New Fed connections, and that evasive attitude... There are just too many uncertainties for us to take on the risk of helping her.
Aalto: At least, that's the conclusion we've reached based on the facts we have so far.
Aalto: But... the Bloombearers who graduated from Startorch heard about this and stepped up to endorse Lucilla. That's what changed Shorekeeper's mind.
Aalto: A teacher who gets that kind of trust from her students... That's pretty impressive.
Rover: So what do you need from me?
Aalto: Actually, according to Shorekeeper, you are the one really running this audit.
Aalto: So we need you, acting as both a Startorch student and a Black Shores auditor, to tell us if Lucilla is solid. And what she's really planning.
Rover: (I want to do something for the Synchronists, but I've also got my responsibility to the Black Shores. I don't think Lucilla would put her students in harm's way, but still...)
Rover: Got it. I'll do what I can to help you.
Aalto: I should be the one saying that to you. Anyway, we need a plan for—
Aemeath: Great, another grand plan. Why'd you gotta make everything so complicated?
Aalto: What the—?! How's that—?!
Aemeath: Helloooo, Mr. Aalto! This is a once-in-a-lifetime chance to invest in the Exostrider Project. I suggest the Black Shores chips in... this much!
Aemeath: Or, you can just patch me through to the Collective's board. I'd be happy to handle the negotiations myself!
Aalto: Is this... Aemeath? I can't believe she just hacked a Black Shores Terminal!
[Dialogue Option]  Aemeath...
[Dialogue Option]  This is serious...
Aemeath: Ahem! I am being serious! If Synchronist degrees get canceled, my record will say I only finished Roya preschool!
Aemeath: Besides, keeping Rabelle College around isn't that hard. Get creative. Talk to Chase. Talk to Shorekeeper. The Collective's investors can't be tougher to handle than Aleph-1, right?
Aemeath: So what if they don't care about your contributions? If they actually want you on their side, they'll have to listen anyway. That's how leverage works.
[Dialogue Option]  (Aemeath might actually be a genius.)
[Dialogue Option]  (No, that's too reckless.)
Rover: If we lean on that kind of leverage now, we'll be held to it later. My experience has shown me that it's often better to act as an individual.
Rover: Since you're planning on the "savior" career path, I think you'll understand what I mean, Aemeath.
Aemeath: Hmm, makes sense. Kinda old-school thinking, though.
Rover: (I need to figure out what Lucilla is really thinking. Then I'll play it by ear.)
Rover: If I want them to protect the Synchronists when I can't, I've got to work inside their system. That's just how this game works.
Rover: Trust me and Lucilla. We'll find the right way to handle this.
Aemeath: Ha! Alright then. But just so you know, if my school record disappears, I'm renaming the Spacetrek Collective to the "Aemeath Collective!"
Aalto: Honestly? If we let Aemeath loose on them, it might actually take some pressure off Lucilla.
Rover: But like she said, she's a Synchronist too. That just makes her one more person Lucilla has to protect.
Aalto: Fair enough. But I'm afraid we have less time than we thought.
Aalto: I spotted some New Fed spies back at the station. Lost 'em on the motorbike, but it won't be long before they track us here.
Aalto: Before Lucilla's next tour begins, let's poke around and see what we can find.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Investigate with Aalto]
Aalto: Students run flea markets on campus? I'm starting to get the hype!
Aalto: Wait, isn't that the student who dozed off in class earlier? C'mon, let's go over.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Check out the students' stalls]
Sonia: If we follow this method, the convergence radius for this series is obviously—
Sigrika: Y-yes, I'm following! Mm-hmm!
Sonia: ...I'm terrible at explaining this, aren't I?
Sigrika: No, no! I'm just slow! I-I'll focus harder!
Sonia: No. You paid me to tutor you, and I'll make sure you get your money's worth!
Sonia: Here, I'll write down a third way to solve it. Watch how it goes, okay?
Sigrika: Okay!
Rover: (So that's why she was drowsy in class... She's been staying up late tutoring other students.)

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
Sigrika: Okay!
Rover: (So that's why she was drowsy in class... She's been staying up late tutoring other students.)



Aalto: You're telling me you've modified every bike here? That's insane.
Lynae: Well, Waleo's been in the expedition motorbike program since day one. These bikes here are basically his family!
Waleo: Soulmates.
Lynae: So, whaddya say, Auditor Aalto? How about you order ten as a starter pack!
Aalto: (Ten soulmates sold in a pack, huh...)
Waleo: I heard you test-drove the Academy's stock model this morning. With the rain the last two days, probably felt a little slip on the turns, yeah?
Waleo: Try this one. I tweaked the ABS and TCS myself. You could take this straight to a pro race, no problem.
Aalto: No wonder you were sleeping in class. Up all night in the garage?
Waleo: No. Bikes have been ready for weeks. Last night, I was just... saying goodbye to them.
Aalto: (Well, that's depressing. I'd feel bad buying them now.)

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Investigate with Aalto]
Lixian: Hands off, you little—
Liheng: Never!
Chisa: ...Please don't fight, you two. Um, maybe I'll just check out the other stalls...
Lixian: Don't go, Chisa! You've got a real eye for quality. This piece was meant for you!
Liheng: No, it isn't! She's just a prep student! She doesn't know anything about quality!
Lixian: EXCUSE me?! The audacity! Just begging for a smack, aren't you!
Chisa: Sorry, I'm not familiar with the mechanics, but I can "see" (Eye of Unraveling) that this device's internal structure is finely crafted.
Chisa: From the external casing down to the internal wiring, the structure and circuitry are meticulously designed. Someone... put their heart into this.
Lixian: ...It's the best thing you'll find in the market, isn't it?
Chisa: Yes, the best!
Lixian: Thank you. That means more to me than you know. Honestly, if we weren't fundraising today, I'd just give it to you. But tell you what, I'll give you 20% off!
Liheng: No! SIX YEARS, Lixian! Six years of your life, just to sell it for nothing?!
Lixian: "For nothing?" I'll tell you what "nothing" is, little brother.
Lixian: It's having nothing to show for the past and nothing waiting in the future. That's "nothing."
Lixian: Look around, Liheng. We're Synchronists. Synchronists who had the most resources but never became the chosen one for the Exostrider. We've achieved... nothing.
Lixian: But if we drop our stupid pride and try to support the students coming up behind us, then we can still be worth "something."
Liheng: You wanna support them, sure. But who's gonna support you!
Lucilla: Me. I will support you.
Lucilla: Nothing to show? I refuse to let anyone write your epitaph before your work's even been seen.
Lucilla: Nothing waiting? You all have me.
Lucilla: I, Lucilla, President of Startorch Academy, will always stand with you. Even if the whole world turns its back. Even if I have to do it alone.
Lucilla: Oh, and by the way, we just landed a very generous sponsor. The new research fund will arrive tomorrow.
Lixian: Th-that means...
Lucilla: That means pack up this stall. Unless you want to sell your hard work at a loss.
Students: PRESIDENT FOR THE WIN!
Sigrika: Chief Aalto! It was you, wasn't it?! You're the sponsor!
Aalto: Huh? Ah... well...
Students: THANK YOU, CHIEF AALTO! YOU'RE THE BEST!
Lucilla: Tch—Hmph—Impudent little hamster! Really, using a crisis to haggle me down to wholesale?!
Lucilla: Just had a bit of a tiff with a rather difficult partner...
Rover: (She closed a deal in a single afternoon? That must've been a hard bargain...)
[Dialogue Option]  (Show your concern.)
Lucilla: I appreciate it, but if a teacher needs her students to worry about her, she's already failed.
Lucilla: Let's just keep it between us, hm?
[Dialogue Option]  (Say nothing.)
Lucilla: Look at them. Adorable, aren't they?
Lixian: Sorry, Professor. We were out of line.
Lucilla: Out of line? For defending your work? That's not something to apologize for. You're braver than I ever was.
Lucilla: Listen to me, Lixian. This pioneering spirit of yours? In all of you? It deserves to be seen by more people.
Lucilla: Don't ever let go of it.
Lixian: I won't!
Lucilla: Oh, and maybe go a little easier on your brother? He's running out of brain cells to lose.
Lixian: Er... Professor? There's something I should tell you.
Lucilla: About Lenie and the others skipping class? Don't worry. I've already been briefed on their whereabouts.
Lucilla: So, Mr. Aalto, shall we move on to the evening's special viewing?
Aalto: Let's do it!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Enter the students' secret workshop]
Lucilla: So they turned the reading room into a workshop.
Lucilla: Not bad. Kids know how to hustle.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Investigate the secret workshop]
Lucilla: Lenie, you broke our little promise. I'm heartbroken, you know.
Lenie: I promised to "show off the Sychronists' club projects." You really think that scrap you wanted me to parade around was gonna win over a single investor?
Lenie: This is what a win looks like!
Lenie: All-terrain self-propelled artillery. AI-driven, multimodal autonomous defense system. Best part is, full Augmented Resonance Effect control. Means zero electromagnetic interference!
Lenie: You could drop this thing in the middle of the Etheric Sea, and as long as I'm still breathing, I'm still piloting!
Lenie: Auditor!
Aalto: Ah—! Present!
Lenie: If you keep funding Synchronist research, then this goes into mass production in one year. No, six months!
Aalto: Mass production?!
Lenie: I know, hard to believe. But just let us show you!
Aalto: No, no, no, that's not what I meant. It's just... the Black Shores isn't a mercenary group.
Lenie: But it cuts through Tacet Discords like a hot knife through butter!
[Dialogue Option]  (Speak up for Aalto.)
Lucilla: Leave this to me.
[Dialogue Option]  (Wait for Lucilla's reply.)
Lucilla: I've got this.
Lucilla: Remove the safety, Lenie. Let's give it a test.
Lucilla: Be careful.
Lenie: Activate!
Rover: (That vehicle...)
Rover: Watch out!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Clear the threat]
Lucilla: Are you alright?
Injured Club Member: Sorry, Professor, Mr. Aalto... and Club Leader Lenie. I lost control. I'm... I'm really sorry...
Lucilla: N.A.N.A., please contact Dr. Luuk to check on them.
Lucilla: Are you alright, Lenie?
Lenie: ...
Lucilla: Go get yourself patched up in the infirmary. I'll handle the rest.
Lenie: ...
[Dialogue Option]  I didn't expect it to be operated solely through Resonance.
[Dialogue Option]  Your work is amazing. Really, a lot of potential.
Aalto: I agree. And I'm not just blowing smoke, Lenie. Controlling delicate equipment through pure Resonance is an ability only you Synchronists possess.
Aalto: This technology has huge potential. Especially if you... Ahem, maybe lose the terrifying weapons.
Lenie: But it's too late now...
Lucilla: It's never too late. I've been talking to new partners. There are many who still want to support us.
Lenie: "We are here to strive for the future of civilization."
Lenie: "Startorch Academy will be the cradle for Synchronists and the vanguard of our collective hope."
Lenie: That's what my admission letter said. That's what I believed.
Lenie: I knew I was signing up to be one of the Exostrider's thousand backup pilots. A spare part. An appendix to a civilization's appendix. And I never regretted it.
Lenie: "Strive for the future of civilization." Heh...
Lenie & Mysterious Girl: Professor, is it true that no one cares about us now that the Exostrider is gone?
Lucilla: I care.
Lenie: Professor... Professor...
Aalto: I used to think this whole Synchronist thing was just shuffling students from one class to another.
Aalto: But I get it now. These kids... they aren't fighting to keep their Synchronist privileges. They're fighting to protect the Synchronist mission.
[Dialogue Option]  The investors' decision will crush their spirit.
Aalto: That's why President Lucilla is so adamant about keeping the program. Emotionally, I'm right there with her. But...
Aalto: It's not enough to win over the review committee. Without the Exostrider, the Synchronist Program is just a drain on their resources.
[Dialogue Option]  That mission comes with a lot else at stake.
Rover: This Academy was a global initiative from the start. Nations and countless people invested in it. That's the bedrock of this place, and the bedrock of what it means to be a Synchronist.
Rover: That gives everyone a stake, even if they don't benefit from the Synchronist Program directly. They deserve to ask questions. And they deserve the chance to be won over.
Aalto: Fair point. Besides, touching stories won't be enough to sway the review. Without the Exostrider, the Synchronist Program is just a drain on their resources...
Rover: I don't think Lucilla is the type to wager on sentiment alone. She's definitely holding her plans close to her chest.
Aalto: Asking for our help while keeping secrets... Hm, or is there some other explanation?
Aalto: Either way, ball's in your court, Rover. Our undercover auditor!
Lucilla: I'm sorry for the incidents today.
Aalto: Please don't be. It was a rewarding day. Those young Synchonists left a great impression on me. Speaking of which, is Lenie gonna be alright?
Lucilla: She's fine. Dr. Luuk is taking her to the infirmary. And at this hour, allow me to walk you to your room.
Aalto: No need for that. Dr. Luuk showed me the way earlier. Actually... you look like you're the one who could use a rest. Rover, why don't you walk the President back instead?
Lucilla: Alright, then. See you tomorrow morning.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Walk with Lucilla]
Lucilla: I need to stop by the Conference Hall before heading back. Care to walk with me?
Rover: Sure.
Lucilla: *A tired sigh*
Rover: When was the last time you slept?
Lucilla: Can't remember.
Rover: The last time you ate?
Lucilla: Hehe, I did keep track of that.
Lucilla: What's the weather like at the Black Shores?
Rover: Umm... It doesn't really change much.
Lucilla: And the food?
Rover: A bit better than what we get here.
Lucilla: Just a bit?
Lucilla: Hah... my students who joined the Black Shores barely write to me. Even when they do, they never mention their daily lives.
Lucilla: If I do get a sudden call out of nowhere, it's just "Professor! I have a question!"
Lucilla: Adorable little gremlins, all of them... As long as they're safe, that's what matters.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Lucilla]
Lucilla: So, when are you going to start?
Rover: Start what?
Lucilla: Fishing for intel. That Mr. Aalto must've put you up to it, right?
[Dialogue Option]  You're something else...
[Dialogue Option]  I was waiting for you to tell me yourself.
Rover: We could've just cut to the chase.
Lucilla: Rover, would you let the Black Shores compromise its founding mission of fighting the Lament to get tangled up in superpower politics... Just for my sake?
Rover: ...
Lucilla: I asked myself yesterday if I really knew you. Turns out, I don't. And I kept going back and forth on what role you should play here...
Lucilla: This situation isn't noble. Isn't just. It's just businessmen and politicians squabbling over a slice of the pie.
Lucilla: But I want this to be a collaboration between Startorch and the Black Shores. Not because we're friends, but because it makes sense.
Lucilla: I put you through this "detour" because I was afraid that if I asked you directly, you'd just say yes to helping me.
Lucilla: So I wanted you to see it for yourself. Judge it with your own measures. That way, when you go back to your people...
Lucilla: You can tell them if Lucilla is worth trusting. And if these Synchronists are worth fighting for.
Aalto: Rover, are you still with the President?
Aalto: Change of plans. The New Federation caught wind she was rallying support and moved the review up.
Rover: To when?
Aalto: Tomorrow morning. Technically, that's in three and a half hours.
Lucilla: Heh, classic New Fed. They probably had a review panel parked outside Lahai-Roi for days, just waiting for the Black Shores to show.
Rover: How'd they win over the other member states and round up representatives so quickly?
Lucilla: Spacetrek Collective budget bylaws. Because the New Fed is a permanent member and rotating chair, they only need half the members to abstain to control the outcome.
Lucilla: They likely had this "review" rigged before it was even proposed...
Aalto: Gear up, President Lucilla. We'll see how the review plays out and take it from there.
Lucilla: Three and a half hours... that's plenty of time.
Lucilla: Let's go, Rover.
Rover: Where to?
Lucilla: The second half of the tour.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Enter the elevator]
Lucilla: Are you upset?
Rover: About how you dragged me into your plan? Or the things you're still not telling me?
Lucilla: My, my...
Lucilla: Sorry. Call it a teacher trying to keep on her mask... You're still my student on paper, after all.
Rover: It sounds like you're saying I can just sit back and enjoy the show?
Lucilla: Haha! Bet that's not something you get to do every day, is it?
Rover: I didn't expect there to be a place like this beneath Rabelle College.
Lucilla: Before Sundermere base was built, this was a research facility for Augmented Resonance Effects and Void Storm countermeasures. It's been decommissioned for years.
Lucilla: The Executive Committee told me I could do whatever I wanted with the space. So I used my Forte to do some light remodeling.
Lucilla: Memories of my students that should exist only in my mind, here... they become real. A tangible piece to display.
Lucilla: We still have some time. If you're interested, feel free to look around.
Rover: You're using your Forte to do all this? How long did it take you to create this?
Lucilla: However long it took, it was worth it... So the ones who "stay" don't just stay, and the ones who "leave" don't just leave.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Inspect the object]
Lucilla: The exhibits we're looking for are here.
Rover: Hmm? Behind the wall?
Lucilla: Don't forget, this is my Memory Palace. Naturally, memory locks require memory keys to unlock.
Lucilla: Allow me to demonstrate—This fancy trick only works in this little domain of mine.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Head to the central area]
Rover: What is it?
Lucilla: This is the very reason I built this exhibition hall in the first place.
Mysterious Girl: Professor, do you trust me?
Lucilla: I...
Rover: Lucilla?
Rover: You spaced out there. Are you alright?
Lucilla: I'm fine. Just had a dream that only lasted a few seconds. Rather fascinating.
Rover: Maybe it's a good idea to rest before the review starts?
Lucilla: Don't worry. I promise you I'll crash the second this is over. But right now, we must bring these exhibits with us.
Rover: Will a few exhibits be enough to sway them?
Lucilla: ...
Rover: (She usually knows exactly how to sell anything, so why does she look so hesitant now?)
Lucilla: Thank you for your trust. I know you have a thousand questions burning in your mind.
Lucilla: "How will she handle the New Fed?" "What's her plan for the Synchronists with the Exostrider gone?" Forgive me for not having the answers just yet.
Rover: I know you'd never harm the students. That's the only answer I need.
Lucilla: I... Terrible timing for a compliment, Rover.
Lucilla: Anyway. Let's take these two exhibits and—
Mysterious Girl: See you soon, Professor.
Rover: Some kind of force pulled us down here. Do you know where we are?
Lucilla: If my memory serves, we're directly beneath the exhibition hall.
Lucilla: This way.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Investigate the research area]
Rover: A Synchronist's cockpit? Was this the prototype?
Lucilla: It looks the part, but this was actually our "Plan B." Designed without safety limiters to get sync rates up quick. Lets a Synchronist pilot the Exostrider by force.
Rover: ...
Lucilla: I know, I know. It was meant as a last resort if civilization was staring down extinction. The project was terminated after the initial trials.
Lucilla: The Synchronists who volunteered... In the end, they lost their ability to resonate with the Exostrider ever again.
Lucilla: What our students are facing now isn't new.
Lucilla: I just hope I can do better by them this time.
Rover: Any idea how we find our way out of here?
Lucilla: With our eyes open. The key (Photo) should be somewhere here.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Investigate the research area]
Lucilla: Excellent. You're catching on quickly.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Lucilla: A little coaching and you're already a pro.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Lucilla: Oh? It seems we've stumbled upon a little bonus.
Rover: That was quite the...
Lucilla: ..."extraordinary Forte," yes?
Lucilla: Some memory fragments... Not a good sign.
Rover: Are you alright?
Lucilla: ...Why are you asking?
Lucilla: Because this domain is becoming more and more warped?
Rover: That staircase over there looks like...
Lucilla: Let's keep heading upwards. We'll find our way out soon enough.
Lucilla: There's probably a device nearby controlling the barrier.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Rover: What's happening?
Lucilla: Something rather unpleasant, I imagine.
Rover: Lucilla...
Lucilla: Fine, no more jokes. Honestly, anyone watching would think you're the one facing the board. There, there, I know the way out.
Lucilla: Remember what I told you before entering the Dark Side? About the memories I erase periodically that can never be recovered?
Lucilla: Some things... I can't bear to remember, but I also can't bear to forget, so I store them here. Looks like some of them are tired of being locked up...
Lucilla: Rover, look up. The exit is right above. We can use this key (Photo) to leave. But I need your help to get there.
Lucilla: Everything here is from my memory, but I know you are real. And wherever you are, that must be reality.
Rover: I understand. I'll be your reference point. But what about that girl? Are we just leaving her?
Lucilla: Rover, do you have any experience dealing with children? Tell me, what makes a child the most flustered when they're playing hide-and-seek?
Rover: ...Ah. I see.
Lucilla: Now, come along. Let's treat this little escape as a warm-up for the review.
Lucilla: Welcome to the Anti-Voidmatter Materials Lab. It's where they first developed the materials for the Academy's Antivoid Canopy.
Rover: What's all of that in the center of the room?
Lucilla: The scrap of the day. Even the best recycling can only keep up with so much.
Lucilla: Let's look around to see if there are any leads.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Lucilla: Only one in a thousand makes the cut. Which means nine hundred ninety-nine don't.
Lucilla: People see the Antivoid Canopy and praise its ingenuity. They'll never get to see the blueprints of the ones who were rejected.
Lucilla: Well... we made quite the headway there, didn't we?
Lucilla: That said, I'm glad to see we're at least moving.
Lucilla: Let's keep heading upwards. We'll find our way out soon enough.

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Seach for clues in the room
content:
[Objective: Seach for clues in the room]
Rover: (I have the photo. Now, where is the right spot to project it?)

metadata.subsection: Seach for clues in the room

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Rover: Is this artificial Retroact Rain?
Lucilla: Oh, dear me. This is but a pale imitation.
Lucilla: Among the Synchronists who survived the experiments, there was one from Jinzhou. Once he realized he'd never resonate with the Exostrider, he returned home and joined the Ministry of Development's Defense Division.
Lucilla: There, he and his colleagues worked together to develop Jinzhou's Retroact Rain defenses.
Rover: You're saying the shields against Retroact Rain and Void Storms share the same origin?
Lucilla: Not exactly. His approach didn't work on Void Storms at all... and it was discarded. Long ago.
Lucilla: Before he left the Academy, the only things he asked to take with him were a few sheets of material buried under that pile of junk.
Lucilla: I often wonder... was he just reluctant to let go of his design? Or had he already mapped out how to protect his hometown?
Rover: The girl who trapped us here... She must be trying to show us something through this memory.
Lucilla: Hmm. Seems I've been getting schooled by my own students a lot lately...
Lucilla: Let's go. It's time to move on to the next "classroom."
Rover: Do you want to stop and take a rest?
Lucilla: Not even close.
Rover: This really is an extraordinary Forte.
Lucilla: Shame the New Fed doesn't usually use words like "extraordinary" to describe Fortes...

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Head to the photo spot]
Lucilla: ...
Rover: What's wrong?
Lucilla: Stay where I can see you, Rover. We've wandered into an unpleasant memory.
Lucilla: It's far too easy to get lost in here...
Rover: It doesn't look like there's a way to cross the barrier ahead.
Lucilla: Hmm... I have an idea.
Lucilla: Rover, just go with me on this, alright?
Lucilla: Rover, can you step a little to the side?
Rover: Hmm?
[Dialogue Option]  (Take a step forward)
Rover: Like this?
Lucilla: Perhaps a step forward?
[Dialogue Option]  (Take another step forward)
Lucilla: Hmm... Maybe a step back?
[Dialogue Option]  ...
Lucilla: Alright, this is the last one. Let's see that handsome smile.
[Dialogue Option]  ...
[Dialogue Option]  (Smile)
Rover: Haha.

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Let Lucilla use her power on you
content:
[Objective: Let Lucilla use her power on you]
Lucilla: Heh... Has anyone ever told you that you're not the most photogenic?
Rover: They have now.
Lucilla: No more teasing. This shot will have to suffice...

[Dialogue Option]  LlO0i1l

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Crack the Terminal]
Rover: Should we pick up the pace a little?
Lucilla: Where was this enthusiasm during class, hmm?
Lucilla: *Yawn*
Lucilla: There should be a console around. Follow my instructions to disable the security system.
Lucilla: First, initiate emergency mode. Type in: LI0Oi1l. Then select Lift Restrictions, and you're good to go.}}
Lucilla: Are you hanging in there alright?
(Rover): I could ask you the same.
(Rover): Let's regroup ASAP.
Lucilla: Agreed. The space here seems to be constantly shifting. We'll need to rendezvous in a memory vivid enough for me. Keep this photo I'm sending over.
Lucilla: Find a suitable place. You know what to do... And keep your wits about you, Rover. Don't get yourself lost in a memory.}}

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Cast Resonance Liberation to break the Terminal
content:
[Objective: Cast Resonance Liberation to break the Terminal]
Lucilla: I'll have to pay for any property damage out of my own pocket, you know...
Lucilla: So please, try to be gentle with the facilities.

metadata.subsection: Cast Resonance Liberation to break the Terminal

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Doctor from Memory: Clear as day, Madam. Your daughter isn't sick. She has awakened her Forte, and it's a remarkably rare memory-type.
Doctor from Memory: Congratulations! I'm certain she'll make an immense contribution to the New Federation one day.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Explore ahead]
Lady from Memory: Nonsense! My Luci will never become a Resonator!
Girl from Memory: Mom...
Girl from Memory: I don't want to be a Resonator. Please... no!
Lady from Memory: Luci!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Take down the monsters]
Rover: Lucilla?
Rover: Not good.
Rover: (Without a "reference point", she's getting pulled into the deep end of her memories. I need to find her before too much time passes.)

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Check WavesLine]
[Dialogue Option]  Screenshot
???: Are you still there, Lucilla?
Lucilla?: Yes.
???: Then why aren't you answering?
Lucilla?: What do you want me to say?
???: You can say "Okay," or "I understand."
???: This is the perfect moment—while our opponents are spread too thin, we take the reins. Just like the time you became President...
???: Don't worry about the narrative. We'll play the villain. You just act tough, rope the independent auditor in, and we'll force another round of review.
???: You fight hard. We express our "concerns." And then... we both take a step back. As long as we ensure our control over the future of the Synchronist Program, nothing else matters.
Lucilla?: And what do you want from my students?
???: Simple. We both get what we want. They have talent, and we help them achieve their dreams. And it'll be their choice.
Lucilla?: Their choice? Whose dreams are we really achieving?
???: It will be their choice, Lucilla. My Luci. I won't speak of your past choices, but tell me, has there been a single choice that wasn't your own?
Lucilla?: I still refuse.
???: There. Just like that. "Act tough," "fight hard," and then we both "take a step back" at the review...
Lucilla?: From the Academy to the Pioneer Association, then to the Spacetrek Collective, and now here… No wonder I was never cut out to be President.
Lucilla: Watch out! That's "me" from the Dark Side. I used this memory to trap her.
Lucilla?: When are you going to tell him, Professor Lucilla? President Lucilla? That you've already made a deal with the New Federation?
Lucilla: Let's go.
Lucilla?: You think you can outrun yourself, Lucilla?
[Dialogue Option]  (I need to know the truth.)
Rover: Your plan... Are you just following the New Federation's playbook?
Lucilla: Don't let her get to you. How could I ever sell out my students? I have a plan, it's just...
[Dialogue Option]  (I trust Lucilla. That's enough.)
Rover: Before the meeting starts, I need you to take the time to fill me in on what's really happening.
Lucilla: Thank you. I promise, I'd never let the New Federation lay a single finger on my students. But...
Lucilla?: That's just her wishful thinking. A moth to the flame, daring the sky with wings of wax.
Lucilla?: Your students will die because of you!
Lucilla: ...Let's leave this place, Rover.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Check WavesLine]
Rover: Is this it? This is as far as we've got?
Lucilla: That just means we'd better pick up the pace.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Move ahead]
Rover: You could've erased this memory. Why keep something so dangerous locked away?
Lucilla: To keep the sting fresh. A sharp reminder of the cost of slipping up if I ever get too comfortable in the Academy's peace.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Move forward]
"Voice from the Heart": Let it go, Lucilla. Face what you know is reality...

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Find out the secret buried deep in her heart
content:
[Objective: Find out the secret buried deep in her heart]
Memory Fragment: Once again, I found the courage to step into this room. Time flows here, silent and peaceful, and the Academy is alive and thriving. We've come so much further than I ever dreamed. I wish you were here to see it.
Memory Fragment: The accident report is indisputable. "Cable insulation failure leading to flight control abnormality." But the truth is simpler. I approved the plan. I killed her.

metadata.subsection: Find out the secret buried deep in her heart

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Return to the dormitory hall]
Memory Fragment: I wrestled with it for so long. What's a teacher supposed to do when a student dreams something so brilliantly insane? But she chose the sky. And I thought... at least let her have one chance to fall.

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: A secret buried deep in the heart
content:
[Objective: A secret buried deep in the heart]
Rover: Is that Sundermere? Are we back before the Starward Riseway was even built?
Lucilla: Most of the students who lost their Synchronist status in those forced sync trials decided to return home. All but one.
Lucilla: She told me it wasn't that she'd lost the Exostrider. The Exostrider had lost her.
Lucilla: She said she'd designed a revolutionary transport method.  A "rocket piercing the sky." A way to bridge that "sky" and the "earth."
Lucilla: This was the day she tested it. Her first crewed flight.
Rover: Then that wasn't a falling star. It was—
Lucilla: A spacecraft. Carrying the most brilliant student I've ever known.
???: Amiya to Sundermere Lookout. Professor, can you hear me?!
Lucilla: Yes.
Amiya: The weather couldn't be more perfect today! Oh, and I just saw a super huge Soliskin! I'll snap a picture for you as soon as I can!
Lucilla: Okay.
Amiya: Professor? You don't sound like your usual self. Are those investors giving you a hard time again?
Lucilla: No, it's not that. I just... I haven't slept much lately. I'm a little tired. That's all.
Amiya: ...Professor, do you trust us?
Lucilla: I...
Amiya: Hey, remember that old Huanglong saying? "Know the way at dawn, and... and something-something at dusk?" Ugh, it went right out of my head!
Lucilla: I can't remember it either...
Amiya: That's okay! I'll look it up and tell you the second the experiment is over!
Amiya: Talk to you soon!
Lucilla: Please, Rover...
Mysterious Girl: From the way it fell, Voidmatter must've pierced the shielding mid-flight. But if we'd reinforced the coating... Hmm...
Mysterious Girl: What kind of civilization do you think built the Exostrider? If they were that advanced... do you think they'd already defeated the Threnodians? Overcome the Lament?
Mysterious Girl: But before they reached the stars, they must have fallen too. Again and again.
Mysterious Girl: Go. Be our eyes. Walk with humanity.
Mysterious Girl: Please give this to our teacher. Humanity's smallest step... and everything we had to give.
Rover: This isn't good.

metadata.subsection: A secret buried deep in the heart

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Catch up with Lucilla]
Rover: Lucilla!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Catch up with Lucilla]
Rover: Lucilla, wait!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Catch up with Lucilla]
Rover: Lucilla, your emotions are affecting this domain! It's dangerous!
Lucilla: Staying here is the real danger. We have to leave.
Lucilla: Almost there.
Lucilla: As long as we keep moving upward, we'll find the way out.
Rover: So this is why you wouldn't tell me what your plan was.
Rover: This "way out" you've been building for the Synchronists... It's just a dead end, isn't it?
Lucilla: I don't want the New Federation to lay their dirty hands on my students. But the more I think about it rationally, the more I realize I can't reject their offer.
Lucilla: Because on what grounds can I propose a plan that might kill them?
Rover: I think I know why that girl trapped you here.
Lucilla: What?
Rover: You're terrified that your proposal will be their end.
Rover: You're afraid because you know they'll support any plan you bring to the table.
Rover: Because you're their teacher.
Rover: Because no one in this world understands them the way you do.
Lucilla: Another lesson from my own student, huh...
Lucilla: See you later, Rover.

title: We Choose the Sky
subsection: Head to the depth of memories
content:
[Objective: Head to the depth of memories]
I hope humanity can soar even higher!
I hope humanity can venture even farther!
I hope humanity can weather any storm!
Mysterious Girl: Professor, what's your dream?
Lucilla: My dream? My dream is simply to see all of yours come true.
Mysterious Girl: See you later, Professor.
Lucilla: Let's go. Together this time.

metadata.subsection: Head to the depth of memories

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Defeat the enemies]
Amiya: Professor, can you hear me?!
Lucilla: I hear you. Loud and clear.
Amiya: The weather couldn't be more perfect today! Oh, and I just saw a super huge Soliskin!
Lucilla: Yes, I see it too. You're right, it's absolutely huge.
Amiya: Great! I thought you weren't gonna believe me!
Amiya: Right, I'll see you soon!
Lucilla: Mm, see you soon!

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Touch the Soliskin]
Rover: Was that girl another one of your students?
Lucilla: She is every memory I have of this Academy. She is every one of my students.
Rover: We've come all this way and I still don't know what your plan actually is.
Lucilla: That's okay. Everyone's about to find out.
Lucilla: *Yawn*
Rover: Tired?
Lucilla: That was an excited yawn, Rover.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Attend the review]
Aalto: Rover, where are you and Lucilla? The other panelists have all taken their seats. The students, too.
Aalto: Can we really trust this plan of hers? Anyway, I'm leaving the speech to you!
Lucilla: If I...
Rover: Then we'll face it together.
Rover: See you later, Professor.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Step onto the podium]
Kamerel: President Lucilla. I am Kamerel, Permanent Secretary of the Spacetrek Collective Board.
Kamerel: By appointment of the Board, and on behalf of the Investors' Conference, I hereby convene this second special inquiry concerning the Synchronist Program of Startorch Academy.
Kamerel: Pursuant to Article 12 of the Spacetrek Collective Charter, President Lucilla, you may now raise any procedural objections regarding the attendees, the agenda, or the draft of this session.
Lucilla: I would like to know the national composition of this review panel, Ms. Kamerel.
Kamerel: This panel consists of ten members, all from the New Federation. Five serve as special representatives, and of the remaining four permanent Board members, two have abstained and delegated their voting rights to the Federation.
Kamerel: Additionally, we have Mr. Aalto attending as Independent Auditor on behalf of the Black Shores.
Lucilla: Then, Ms. Kamerel, I believe the current composition of this panel fails to comply with Charter regulations governing review committees.
Kamerel: According to the Regulations, any participant authorized by a Board member shall be deemed to hold the same nationality as that member. The panel's composition is perfectly valid.
Aalto: Pardon the interruption. If that's the case, then Rover—currently a student at Rabelle College—can also be considered a panelist appointed by the Black Shores. Here's the paperwork.
Kamerel: ...Welcome, Rover.
Lucilla: I have no further questions, Ms. Kamerel.
Kamerel: Then per the agenda, I will now relay the investors' resolution following our previous inquiry.
Kamerel: Given that the loss of the Exostrider constitutes a de facto failure of the program, our immediate priority is to establish a compensation plan for the affected assets and students.
Kamerel: Furthermore, the Board directs that the Synchronist Program must be terminated immediately, or at minimum suspended.
Lucilla: My stance remains unchanged, Ms. Kamerel. I intend to continue the program.
Kamerel: We require a justification.
Lucilla: Panelists, this is a theoretical prototype for a shield designed to counter Retroact Rain, created by one of our Synchronists.
Lucilla: This prototype significantly accelerated the development of Jinzhou's own defenses. It saved countless lives during the war against the Threnodian Ovathrax.
Lucilla: And yet, the material used in this prototype was originally nothing more than discarded scrap from one of the Engineering Department's experiments.
Lucilla: It was only because its designer was a Synchronist—educated in engineering, Voidmatter, and even meteorology—that this material found a second life.
Kamerel: You seem to be arguing for the superiority of general education for the Synchronists, President Lucilla.
Kamerel: However, general education isn't even included in the program's White Paper. I fail to see a link between that and advancing the Synchronist Program.
Kamerel: The shield is an impressive surprise, but given the cost of gambling on such a slim probability, the cost-effectiveness is simply too low.
Lucilla: Ms. Kamerel. Panelists. How exactly are we meant to measure the cost-effectiveness of failure?
Lucilla: As you can see, this shattered component comes from a failed experiment. One that was not even recorded in the Collective's official gazette.
Lucilla: A Synchronist gave her life as the price for validating her theory.
Lucilla: Fifteen months later, this very component became the final piece for the construction of the Starward Riseway, the bridge between Lahai-Roi's earth and the sky.
Lucilla: Humanity does not always set out for the sake of victory, Ms. Kamerel.
Lucilla: Our Synchronists know from the day they enroll: No one knows when the Exostrider will awaken, and the odds that they'll be the one to pilot it are slim.
Lucilla: Yet they come anyway. They march toward likely failure from the very start.
Lucilla: So I ask you, can you truly say that such failure has no value?
Lucilla: And how can we call that a "failure" of the Synchronists, when the Exostrider was the one who banished Aleph-1 from our world?
Aalto: Secretary Kamerel, the Black Shores representative requests the floor.
Kamerel: Proceed.
Aalto: On the subject of unforeseen benefits from the program, we find ourselves in agreement with President Lucilla.
Aalto: This is a set of disclosable data we've just compiled. A significant proportion of current Black Shore members came from Startorch Academy.
Aalto: These Bloom Bearers demonstrate exceptional capability, talent, and resolve—traits most prominent among the Synchronists.
Aalto: Furthermore, the Synchronists serve as role models for other students. I believe Rover is better suited to speak on that.
[Dialogue Option]  Synchronists are a rallying banner.
[Dialogue Option]  Synchronists are a living symbol.
Rover: The Synchronist Program is a search for a way out for our civilization.
Rover: When we believed the Exostrider was the only route, then those fit to pilot it were the Synchronists.
Rover: Now that the Exostrider is no longer a viable option, the ones fit to search for a new way out... Are still our Synchronists.
Lucilla: Yes, which is why I must disagree with evaluating the Synchronist Program purely in terms of cost-effectiveness. I urge investors to reconsider the criteria used to measure its value.
Kamerel: ...We require a discussion. This session is adjourned for five minutes.
Lucilla: (Let them see your potential. Let them see your value.)
Lucilla: (But... that is not enough.)
Kamerel: President Lucilla, following the review panel's deliberation: We fully recognize the potential value of the Synchronists as an independent academic division, as well as their role model effect. However—
Kamerel: As Rover stated, only those fit to shoulder the burden of finding a new way out deserve the title "Synchronist."
Kamerel: Therefore, we propose a compromise: Rabelle College will be preserved, but all future training must be subject to the guidance and review of this panel.
Kamerel: Let's "both take a step back," shall we, President Lucilla?
Lucilla: This is it. The final fight, Lucilla.
Lucilla: Take a deep breath. Keep your composure. And remember.
Lucilla: Everything you regret
Lucilla: Everything that brings you joy
Lucilla: Everything you have lost
Lucilla: Everything you have witnessed
Lucilla: The answer you chase
Lucilla: The treasure you give everything to protect!
Lucilla: No, that won't be necessary, Secretary Kamerel.
Lucilla: The Synchronists of today... They remain the closest thing this world has to a way out for our civilization.
Lucilla: After our confrontation with Aleph-1, we recovered this audio recording from the interstellar probe "Farwatcher."
Kamerel: It's nothing more than static.
Lucilla: Even so, it is the only legacy the pioneers of Solaris have left us—we are not alone, Secretary Kamerel.
Lucilla: Just as our ancestors took shelter in caves, just as Startorch Academy was built in Lahai-Roi, just as humanity itself endures on Solaris...
Lucilla: A brave soul took the first step to claim that future.
Kamerel: I fail to see what this has to do with the Synchronists.
Lucilla: Using Rabelle College research, we can build vehicles driven entirely by Augmented Resonance. That means complete immunity to frequency interference.
Lucilla: And the training our Synchronists undergo makes them the perfect pilots for these vessels.
Kamerel: But the Stridergate has been sealed. Not to mention, whatever lies beyond can hardly be called a "route."
Lucilla: Who said civilization's route to the future has to go "down"?
Lixian: The stars.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
Lucilla: Who said civilization's route to the future has to go "down"?
Lixian: The stars.



(Cutscene plays)
President Lucilla.
I'm sure you know—
—Any instrument that nears the Etheric Sea...
I am well aware of that.
However, by relying on Augmented Resonance Effects...
The Academy can overcome that barrier.
And if it fails—
The cockpit becomes a coffin.
Is that a chance you're willing to take?
This is our decision
If the answer lies beyond death—
Then that's where we go!
Just wait and see!
My brightest students...
Will pierce the sky for all to see!
(Cutscene ends)

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Say goodbye to Aalto]
Aalto: The car will be here soon. I can take it from here.
Rover: Thanks for everything, Aalto. Really.
Aalto: Phew, it was a long day. The kind you don't forget, though.
Aalto: Rover, can you pass a message to the President for me? After a speech like that? The outcome doesn't matter half as much.
Aalto: Anyway, chillax. Everything's going to be alright!
Aalto: Well, catch you at the Black Shores, Rover.
Rover: Yeah. Till next time.

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Talk to Hiyuki]
Hiyuki: She is not here. She is likely still at the Review Hall.
Rover: Thank you. I'll look for her there.
Hiyuki: I'm sorry.
Rover: What for?
Hiyuki: If I had been more helpful, perhaps the outcome would have been more satisfying.
Rover: This was her battle. You and I have already done our best for her.
Hiyuki: Go check on her.
Rover: Mm.
[Dialogue Option]  (Go find Lucilla)

title: We Choose the Sky
content:
[Objective: Find Lucilla]
...The Executive Committee still considers the Synchronist Program to be extraordinarily costly, high-risk, and fraught with inestimable difficulties... Investing our technical talent into this program could incur incalculable losses for the Spacetrek Collective or even humanity itself.
...Yet, we must also admit that the Synchronist Program has shown us another possibility. A "way out." The very thing we have been chasing.
Therefore, the Executive Committee of the Spacetrek Collective has determined that we will, once again, challenge the sky.

title: Chapter IV
section: Act I - The Wind Before the Storm
content: Quest Objective: After the events in Lahai-Roi are resolved, you decide to return to Huanglong, only to receive news of Yangyang's disappearance. In order to find her, you join Suisui, Yangyang's elder sister, on a journey to the Land of Xuanfang in Mengzhou.

metadata.section: Act I - The Wind Before the Storm

title: Chapter IV
section: Act II - Xuanling Sings, Storm Quelled
content: Quest Objective: The Land of Xuanfang is thrown into turmoil following an unexpected riot of out-of-control Autopuppets. As you investigate, you uncover the mastermind behind the scheme—a mysterious Artisan who covets the Sentinel's technology. In the culmination of the event, this figure commands the rogue Autopuppets to launch an assault on Xuanfang Hold.

metadata.section: Act II - Xuanling Sings, Storm Quelled

title: Chapter IV
section: Segue - The Chant of Unseen Ties
content: Quest Objective: Days after the Autopuppet crisis was solved, Yangyang chooses to stay behind in the Land of Xuanfang to assist the soldiers and the civilians. As she's waiting on her Resonance Assessment report, a mysterious voice starts to whisper in her ears...

metadata.section: Segue - The Chant of Unseen Ties

title: Chapter IV
section: Act III - Song of the Heart Sword
content:
Quest Objective: With the great battle over, the Land of Xuanfang is slowly returning to how it once was, though plenty of aftershocks have yet to settle. Then one day, a WavesLine message from Yangyang arrives out of the blue: Suisui is about to head back to Mengzhou City...

Quest Objective: To trace the anomaly to its source, you and Qingxiao ventured into the Manifold Sanctum, only to find that Xuanfang Hold's control mainframe had been eroded by Reverberations. As the Sanctum, and then all of Xuanfang Hold, took to the air, the two of you fell into a deep valley...

Quest Objective: Not long after the upheaval that swept the entire Land of Xuanfang came to an end, Suisui, far away in Mengzhou City, wants to share what her investigation turned up with you and Yangyang... Come to think of it, what has Qingxiao been up to lately?

subsection: Sign the package delivered by Lollo Logistics
content:
[Objective: Sign the package delivered by Lollo Logistics]
Lollo Logistics Courier: Huff... Huff... Rover! I have a delivery for you! It's from Huanglong!
[Dialogue Option]  Thank you.
[Dialogue Option]  A delivery from Huanglong...?
Abby: Huh? A package from Huanglong? What is it, what is it? Someone sent you snacks?
Rover: It's a letter from Yangyang.
Abby: Ohhh... from Yangyang, huh? Yeah, that time of year, I guess...
Rover: There's a whole box of treats for you.
Abby: Whoa! Yangyang's the best!
[Dialogue Option]  Save some for me.
[Dialogue Option]  There's enough for everyone.
Abby: Ahem... I-I know that. Hello? You're looking at the maestro of sharing here! But hey, what'd Yangyang say in her letter?
[Dialogue Option]  Jinzhou is seeing some trouble...
Abby: Ugh... Don't tell me Ovathrax is stirring up chaos again? Nah, couldn't be.
[Dialogue Option]  Her older sister is going to visit her.
Abby: Huh?! Yangyang has a sister? What's she gonna be like... Ah, I can't take the suspense!
Rover: Let's write back and ask her.
Rover: (Need to find a place to write this letter.)

title: The Wind Before the Storm
subsection: Write a reply letter to Yangyang
content:
[Objective: Write a reply letter to Yangyang]
Rover: (Now, what should I write...?)
[Dialogue Option]  (Write about how you and the Academy fought off the Voidborne Threnodian.)
Rover: The Voidborne Threnodian, Aleph-1... it devours a person's will and tries to strip human existence of all meaning. We could not have defeated it without Exostrider "Lahai-Roi," everyone at Startorch Academy, and the local Roya people.
Rover: After that... Lahai-Roi could be reborn as something new. A different kind of civilization. Something even brighter.
[Dialogue Option]  (Write about how Rabelle College averted being shut down.)
Rover: After the Exostrider disappeared, the Spacetrek Collective's investors even wanted to shut down Rabelle College at one point. But President Lucilla fought them tooth and nail, and the faculty and students let their work speak for itself. In the end, they saved it.
Rover: And they'll only keep reaching for the stars.
Rover: (Anything else I can add...?)
[Dialogue Option]  (Ask how everyone's doing in Jinzhou.)
Rover: How's everyone in Jinzhou doing? Ever since that Moon-Chasing Festival, there hasn't been much opportunity for me to get together with everyone.
Rover: My footsteps... Before I knew it, I'd already come a long way.
Rover: Sometimes I find myself thinking... Maybe I should pause once in a while. Go back somewhere familiar. But every time the thought crosses my mind, some new trouble always finds me.
[Dialogue Option]  (Ask how Yangyang's doing.)
Rover: What about you, Yangyang? How have you been?
Rover: Every letter you send makes me realize how far I've come from where I started. I know you must be working on your own goals while I've been away, too. Next time we meet, let's trade stories. See what we've both made of ourselves.

title: The Wind Before the Storm
subsection: Write a reply letter to Yangyang
content:
Rover: (Yangyang mentioned a dream...)
Rover: (Ever since you woke me up, I've had many dreams of my own. Good dreams, bad dreams. Some slip away like the wind as soon as I wake. Others are seared into my heart for a long time.)
Rover: (But they're just dreams. Scenes that never existed. Lingering notes that the present hasn't yet swept away.)
Rover: (But that moment in the Gorges of Spirits, the first time we met, is a reality we share that no number of dreams could ever erase.)
Rover: (Just like the name you gave me, maybe I'm destined to rove endlessly. Maybe my journey is destined to be filled with the unknown.)
Rover: (But that also means...)
Yangyang: But that also means...
Yangyang: In countless tomorrows lie countless possibilities...
Yangyang: Where our paths intertwine.
Chixia: Hello—! Yangyang! You comin' or what?
Yangyang: Yes, I'm coming.
Chixia: Lemme see... Once we pass through that checkpoint up ahead, that's Xuanfang territory. Didn't expect following those leads would take us all the way out here.
Yangyang: This is where those missing people were last reported...
Chixia: And that's all thanks to you and that  of yours, Yangyang! If you hadn't connected all the dots, we'd still be runnin' circles back in Jinzhou!
Yangyang: You're exaggerating, Chixia... According to the Patrollers' investigation reports, the victims all had reasons to travel to Mengzhou, and Xuanfang lies right along the only route there.
Yangyang: But none of them ever made it to Mengzhou, nor did they come back. But if memory serves, Xuanfang—
Chixia: Come on, we'll find out what happened once we get there. I already filed for a warrant. Just gotta show the folks at the checkpoint the paperwork, and they should let us into the Hold.
Chixia: Phew... This is my first time on a field op this far from home. Anyway, we're bringin' those missing people back safe and sound! Right, Yangyang?
Yangyang: Yes. Let's go.

title: The Wind Before the Storm
content:
[Objective: Continue forward]
Chixia: By the way, what were you lookin' at back there all by yourself? I saw you smilin' the whole time... You don't get that look on your face every day, ya know.
Yangyang: Huh? I'm not usually that serious... am I?
Chixia: Ain't the same. Anybody with eyes can tell ya, a smile ain't just a smile. There's the smile you put on 'cause you're s'posed to, and the smile that comes from the heart. So what's got my Yangyang smilin' like that, I wonder...
Yangyang: ...Let's just focus on the mission, Chixia.

Chixia: That's weird. Where is everybody? There should be guards stationed here...
Yangyang: Stay alert, Chixia.

subsection: Head to the checkpoint at the Gate of Xuanfang
content:
[Objective: Head to the checkpoint at the Gate of Xuanfang]
Yangyang: Something's not right, Chixia. Ready your weapon.
Chixia: Yangyang? Are your birdie senses tingling or somethin'?!
Yangyang: TDs... One. No, two. They're coming from every direction!
Chixia: That can't be right! This place is s'posed to be—
Yangyang: ...Prepare for combat.

Chixia: What happened to the Xuanfang guards!? You don't suppose these TDs took 'em out...?
Yangyang: I'm not sure. But there was something different about these TDs...
Yangyang: The ones born in the wild don't usually form groups of this size...
Chixia: If they ain't comin' from outside the city, then that means... they came from—
Yangyang: ...

title: The Wind Before the Storm
content:
Abby: Oof... I feel empty.
Abby: Loong Whiskers Crisps, Wuthercakes, Honeysuckle Bread... Desserts from Rinascita and Lahai-Roi are great and all, but the stuff from Huanglong is what really hits the spot.
Abby: Now that I think 'bout it, it's been ages since I've had Crispy Squab, Jinzhou Stew, Loong Buns, Poached Chicken, Candied Caltrops, Moon Pearls.
[Dialogue Option]  Please, make it stop...
[Dialogue Option]  Is your stomach feeling homesick?
Abby: What else am I supposed to do?! Blame Yangyang for sending us those tasty snacks. They brought back all my great memories of Jinzhou!
Rover: Point taken. It really has been a while since we visited Jinzhou.
Rover: (Yangyang hasn't written back yet. Yangyang, Chixia, Baizhi... and even Jinhsi. I wonder how everyone's doing?)
Rover: Things here at the Academy are wrapping up. Maybe now's a good time.
Rover: (And the thing we found inside that satellite... It might have something to do with the Court of Savantae.)
Abby: I know what you're gonna say! Let's go visit! We'll make it a surprise!
[Dialogue Option]  We're not going on vacation, you know.
[Dialogue Option]  We'll still have work to do when we go back.
Abby: Rising Loong, Star Flakes, Jinzhou Maocai, Spicy Pulled Chicken... Hehe...
Rover: (Abby's completely lost in a fantasy world now...)
Rover: (Eh, that's fine, I guess.)
Rover: (I should let everyone at the Academy know before I leave for Jinzhou.)

title: The Wind Before the Storm
content:
[Objective: Leave the Archive]
Luuk Herssen: Ah, Rover, perfect timing. We were about to go look for you if you took any longer.
Rover: Why's everyone...
Hiyuki: To bid you farewell.
Mornye: Mentor, I...
Mornye: ...No matter what difficulties lie ahead, Startorch Academy will always have your back. I... We will all be waiting for you here.
Mornye: So go. Don't worry about us.
Hiyuki: Huanglong... What a shame. Should the opportunity arise, I would like to visit.
Hiyuki: If you need anything, you have but to reach out.
Luuk Herssen: With all that said, don't forget to share your experiences with us once you're back in Huanglong.
Luuk Herssen: Safe travels. Send us a WavesLine when you have the time.
Rover: Thank you, everyone. Well... Off I go, then.
Hiyuki: Ah, yes. Lucilla mentioned a "special" arrangement for you. Do look forward to it.
